Nor do they permit, following the example of Peter, to whom they also assign a daughter, Petronilla, that someone be chosen who is married and remains married; or that someone rely on the examples of certain bishops of the Roman Church itself, who, perhaps rarer because of the violence of persecutions, were married; or that someone claim, from the example of the honorable marriage even of clerics, the legitimate birth of Felix III and Agapetus I, who were sons of presbyters, or of Silverius, who was a son of a bishop, or of Deusdedit, who was a subdeacon, or of Theodore I, who was a son of a bishop again; these are found, at least according to Platina in the index to his Lives, to have been the sons of the Fathers.

units.la: XXIII. Ferendum esset, imò utile esset, si continentes in tali statu eligerentur atque electi manerent. Sed quia eliguntur saepe, saltem electi fuerunt, donec Juvenes, sive viri nondum decrepiti (quod ex Cardinalium vivendi modo jam constat, & mox ampliùs de Papis ostendendum erit) quorum vitium hac etiam in parte jam apparet, vel apparuit, & de quibus Castitatis secuturae exigua spes est vel fuit; Quemadmodum etiam historiae eorum impuritatem passim produnt, atque jam Johannem XI. Sergii Papae spurium, proin hoc etiam respectu ex Jure Canonico 56. dist. c. 1. conferatur: illegitimum, impudicam item Papissam, & occasione illa tales, qui in impuro coelibatu ante Electionem se mares esse probant, commemoravimus, ideo non leve quoque in hoc vitium ratione eorum, qui eliguntur, occurrit, & in hoc, quod, dum liberos habere juxta Apostolicam sententiam olim quasi commendationis pars, saltem non vitiosum fuit, jam vice versa liberos habere maxime obest; Quia nimirum alii nunc sunt mores, & Ecclesia dives alere non potest, quibus Ecclesia pauper sufficere debuisset & potuisset, atque alii sunt isti liberi, non probi & in subjectione, sed improbi atque paterno nomine sceptra tenentes; non ex legitimo matrimonio, quamvis & hi obsint, atque Electionem valde impediant, sed nothi. Exemplo sit Cardinalis Savelli, non enim defuit in Conclavi Sixti V. che gli opponesse, che gli haveva non picciol numero de' sigli bastardi, tenuti da suoi per molto tempo, con molti altri secreti &c. id est; qui ei opponeret magnum spuriorum ejus numerum, qui a longo tempore ipsi attribuantur, cum multis aliis secretis &c. Sed vel maxime ei obfuisset, ejusque electionem vel istud solum plane impossibilem reddidisset, si habuisset cum conjuge legitima liberos legitimos, atque tam bene cessit Papissa, ut unicam habuisse omnibus sufficiat; modo, si per aetatem licet, Johannae, Theodorae, Maroziae &c. (de Ganymedibus ut nihil dicam;) conjugum vices suppleant.
units.tr: XXIII. It would be tolerable, indeed it would be useful, if celibates were elected in such a state and remained celibate once elected. But they are often chosen, or at least have been chosen, while still young men, or men not yet worn out by age (as is already clear from the way of life of the Cardinals, and more will be shown about the Popes shortly). Their vice already appears, or has appeared, in this respect too, and there is or was little hope that chastity would follow. Their histories everywhere reveal their impurity. We have already mentioned John XI, the spurious son of Pope Sergius, so in this respect compare 56. dist. c. 1. of the Canon Law: he was illegitimate. We have also mentioned the shameless Papess, and on that occasion those who prove themselves men by an impure celibacy before their election. Therefore there is no slight vice in this regard too, concerning those who are elected. And in this respect: whereas having children was once, according to the apostolic saying, a kind of part of commendation, or at least not a fault, now conversely having children is a great hindrance. The reason is that manners are now different, and the Church, though rich, cannot support those whom the poor Church should and could have sufficed for. And those children are not dutiful and under subjection, but wicked, holding the sceptre in a fatherly name. They are not born of lawful marriage, although these too are an obstacle and greatly hinder an election; they are bastards. Let Cardinal Savelli be an example. In the Conclave of Sixtus V there was no lack of those who objected to him: that they would object to him that he had a not small number of bastard sons, kept by him for a long time, along with many other secrets etc. Yet this would have harmed him most of all, and this alone would have made his election quite impossible, had he had lawful children by a lawful wife. The Papess fared so well that having one child is enough for all. Now, if age permits, Joan, Theodora, Marozia and so on (not to mention the Ganymedes) make up for the place of wives.

units.la: XXIV. Lubet heic apponere responsiones Ant. de Rosellis Monarch. p. 2. Cap. X. ad quaestionem: An Electio irrita reddatur, si electus forte conjugem habeat? Nimirum loquitur de Electione jam facta, & de conjuge, quam inopinato habere deprehenditur electus, & respondet: Nec quod uxorem habet, obstare potest; nam licet uxor possit eum vendicare in virum, quando non est de matrimonio dubium: (exemplum supra in tractatione de Johanna dedimus) & uxor non potest ad continentiam induci, tamen propter hoc non deseret Papatum, & erit Papa uxorem habens, ita vult glo. in d. c. si quis in pecuniam. 79. di. Nec est contra substantiam Papatus. Nam & Petrus uxorem habuit, & Graeci Presbyteri conjugant: unde tenebitur reddere debitum uxori, & erit Papa. Nescio tamen, an hanc Rosellis decisionem ex aequo probaturi sint. Illud saltem constat, eum non solum de isto casu Casus Antonio de Rosellis, si forte conjugem habeat electus; casu cogitâsse, neque solum eum casum istum ita decidisse. Quando enim alii alios casus fingunt, in quibus Electio R. Pontificis oppugnari aut rescindi possit v. g. Laymannus Quæst. Canon. de Prælat. Eccles. Elect. c. 12. qu. 132. p. 543. qui primò eam per objectionem excommunicationis, aut censuræ cujusque ab Electoribus contractæ oppugnari posse negat. Secundò eam irritam pronuntiat. α. Si electus in notoria hæresi fuerit; tum quia Papa ob hæresin & aliâs deponi possit; tum quia hæreticus membrum Ecclesiæ esse non possit, & multò minùs caput. β. Si ob alium defectum inhabilis sit, jure divino, aut naturali: ut si sit infans, amens aut mulier; (supponens adeò mulierem etiam eligi posse, stultum enim est agere de casibus impossibilibus.) γ. Si Simoniacè electus fuerit. δ. Si per metum gravem & injustum, præviâ Concilii generalis recognitione irritam futuram, quamvis hoc ultimo casu aliorum electiones irritæ non fiant. ε. Si non à Cardinalibus, vel non à justo eorum numero; Augustinus Triumphus Ancobitanus de potest. Eccles. p. 22. 23. casum de uxore supra positum quoque ponit, atque de eo pronuntiat; teneri Papam renuntiare nolentem debitum conjugale uxori continentiam servare nolenti reddere; quia continentia Clericorum sit consilium, & de jure positivo, reddere autem debitum uxori præceptum juris naturalis atque divini. Et si dicatur, quòd scandalum esset in populo, si sciretur, quòd Papa redderet debitum uxori, tale scandalum esse passivum, non activum: quod non sit demittendum propter veritatem doctrinæ & æquitatem justitiæ, & sanctitatem vitæ, ut dicat Hieronymus.
units.tr: XXIV. It is pleasing to set here the answers of Antonius de Rosellis, Monarch. p. 2. Cap. X., to the question: Is an election made void if the elected man perhaps has a wife? He is speaking, of course, of an election already made and of a wife whom the elected man is found to have unexpectedly, and he answers: Nor can the fact that he has a wife be an obstacle; for although a wife can claim him as her husband when there is no doubt about the marriage (we gave an example above in the treatment of Joan), and a wife cannot be induced to continence, yet on this account he will not abandon the Papacy, and he will be a Pope having a wife, as the gloss on the said chapter "si quis in pecuniam", 79 dist., wills. Nor is it against the substance of the Papacy. For Peter also had a wife, and Greek presbyters marry; hence he will be bound to render the marital debt to his wife, and he will be Pope. I do not know, however, whether those who support this ruling of Rosellis will approve it. At least this is clear: he had in mind not only that case, that the elected man might perhaps have a wife, and he did not only decide that case in this way. For when others invent other cases in which the election of a Roman Pontiff can be attacked or rescinded, for example Laymann, Quaest. Canon. de Praelat. Eccles. Elect. c. 12. qu. 132. p. 543., who first denies that it can be attacked on the objection of excommunication or of any censure incurred by the electors. Secondly, he pronounces it void: (1) if the elected man has been in notorious heresy; since the Pope can be deposed on account of heresy and otherwise, and since a heretic cannot be a member of the Church, much less its head. (2) If he is unfit by another defect, by divine or natural law: as if he were an infant, insane, or a woman (supposing, that is, that a woman can even be elected, for it is foolish to deal with impossible cases). (3) If he was elected by simony. (4) If by grave and unjust fear, the election being void after prior recognition by a general council, although in this last case the elections of others are not made void. (5) If he was not elected by the Cardinals, or not by a lawful number of them. Augustinus Triumphus of Ancona, de potest. Eccles. p. 22, 23., also puts the case of the wife stated above, and pronounces concerning it: that the Pope is bound to resign if he is unwilling to render the marital debt to his wife, or unwilling to keep continence; because continence of clergy is a counsel and of positive law, but rendering the debt to a wife is a precept of natural and divine law. And if it be said that there would be a scandal among the people if it were known that the Pope rendered the debt to his wife, such scandal is passive, not active, and must not be abandoned for the sake of the truth of doctrine, the equity of justice and the holiness of life, as Jerome says.

units.la: SECTIO SEXTA, In qua; De vitiis & næviis Electionis Pontificum Romanorum ratione ætatis agitur.
units.tr: SECTION SIX, in which the defects and blemishes of the election of Roman Pontiffs are discussed with respect to age.

units.la: Breviarium;
units.tr: Summary;

units.la: I. Quanam ætas jure requiratur; II. Defectus ratione ætatis nimis tenera. Prodromus in Ecclesia Rhemensis Archiepiscopo quinquenni. III. Exempla in sede Romana. Primum in Iohanne X. IV. Secundum in Iohanne XII. V. Cujus exempli nævus porrò detegitur. VI. Tertium in Benedicto IX. VII. Cujus vitium ulterius indicatur. VIII. Excessus ratione ætatis nimis
units.tr: I. What age is rightly required. II. A defect in respect of an age too tender: a forerunner in the Church of Reims, an archbishop of five years. III. Examples in the Roman see: the first in John X. IV. The second in John XII. V. The flaw of this example is further exposed. VI. A third in Benedict IX. VII. The fault of this is further indicated. VIII. Excess in respect of an age too advanced.

units.la: provecta; IX. Ex Aphorismis Azzolini, Conclavibus Urbani VI. Leonis X. Pauli IV. X. Pii V. Gregorii XIII. & XIV. XI. Clementis VIII. Pauli V. Gregorii XV. Urbani VIII. Alexandri VII. XII. Clementis IX. XIII. Ejusdem; XIV. Clementis X. XV. Hinc senectutis atque infirmitatum simulatio. Exemplum Sixti V. XVI. Respectu visitationum dilatarum; XVII. Mendacii de ætate dupl icis, & Consistoriorum raro, & cum simulatione frequentatorum; XVIII. Judicii aliorum, quos deceperat; XIX. Eorum quae ante Convivium apud S. Sixtum & in Convivio dicta fuerunt; XX. Simulationis mortem Pontificis proximè antecedentis; XXI. Simulationis, intellecto de morte Antecessoris nuntio, & occasione agilitatis Antecessoris; XXII. Judicii, Montaltium ob infirmitates nimias vix aptum esse, & verborum de Conclavi non ingrediendo; XXIII. Verborum ad Promotores; XXIV. Barba inordinata, actuum moribundi & incessus; XXV. Mutationis subita, judiciique de ea lati; XXVI. Exempla alia indigitantur; Testimonia generalia de senectutis commendatione afferuntur; XXVII. Vtilitas Electionis Senum; XXVIII. Incommodum ejusdem; XXIX. Annotatio ad commoda & in commoda; XXX. Vitium Electionis senum.
units.tr: IX. From the Aphorisms of Azzolino, the conclaves of Urban VI, Leo X and Paul IV. X. Of Pius V, Gregory XIII and Gregory XIV. XI. Of Clement VIII, Paul V, Gregory XV, Urban VIII and Alexander VII. XII. Of Clement IX. XIII. The same. XIV. Of Clement X. XV. Hence the feigning of old age and infirmities; the example of Sixtus V. XVI. With respect to delayed visitations. XVII. Of the lie about age, and of consistories rarely attended, and attended with pretence. XVIII. The judgment of others whom he had deceived. XIX. Of what was said before the banquet at St Sixtus's and at the banquet. XX. Of the pretence surrounding the death of the immediately preceding Pontiff. XXI. Of the pretence when news of the death of the predecessor was received, and on the occasion of the predecessor's agility. XXII. The judgment that Montalto was scarcely fit on account of excessive infirmities, and of the words about not entering the conclave. XXIII. Of the words addressed to the promoters. XXIV. Of an untidy beard, of the actions of a dying man, and of his gait. XXV. Of the sudden change, and of the judgment passed on it. XXVI. Other examples are pointed out; general testimonies in praise of old age are brought forward. XXVII. The usefulness of electing the aged. XXVIII. The inconvenience of the same. XXIX. A note on the advantages and disadvantages. XXX. The defect of electing the aged.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Progredimur ad ætatem eligendorum. In V. T. Levitæ ministrabant à trigesimo usque ad quinquagesimum ætatis annum Num. IV. 3. In N. T. ætas certa Ministrorum Ecclesiæ designata haud est. Juniores, seniores constitui possunt, modò idonei sint; Sed, cùm rarior sit in juventute requisitorum necessariorum complexio, ex illa maximè parte videndum, ne præmatura noceat electio; Quem in finem haud immeritò in Ecclesiis præscribitur certus annorum numerus, infrà quem subsistentes non facilè coetibus præficiuntur. Atque tales etiam constitutiones erant in Ecclesia primitiva, licèt pro locorum temporúmque diversitate diversæ. Prudentiæ interim semper relinquebatur atque æquitati Procerum heic, si quid aliter fieri debeat, providere, atque speciatim nonnunquam de rigore Legis aliquid remittere, vel temporis necessitate Ministrorúmque defectu, vel extraordinariâ juniorum quorundam atque matura aptitudine id ita volente, neque limites observare velle, ubi Spiritus S. gratia eos quasi primò transiliisse manifestè videtur; quâ ratione quoque Juvenis Timotheus atque forte (Tit. II. 6. 7.) etiam Titus multis aliis licèt ætate grandioribus ab Apostolo prælati fuerunt; De qualibus rectè Ignatius ad Magnesios scripsit: Neque etiam contemnenda est Episcopi juventus, sed secundùm voluntatem Dei Patris omnis ei reverentia tribuenda est, quemadmodum facere novi Sanctos Presbyteros, non respicientes ad eam, qua apparet, juventutem, sed ad prudentiam, quam in Deo habet. Quandoquidem annosi continuò sapientes non sunt, neque senes possident sident intelligentiam, sed spiritus, qui in hominibus est. Sed recte scripsit haec nonnisi de talibus rarioribus. Ab altera vero parte evidens quoque est, ad laboriosum Evangelii ministerium, vegetum corpus, memoriam firmam, ingenii judiciíque aciem [?]plane requiri, atque proin, licet naevis atque imbecillitati eorum, quibus forte ipsa in munere diligentia ista acceleravit, aliquid indulgendum atque modis omnibus succurrendum sit, ministerium illud decrepitis jam & corpore deficientibus, mente repuerascentibus de novo minime demandari, sed eo majorem quoad ista ab utraque parte curam adhiberi debere, quo majores sunt ministerii, quod conferendum est, partes, siquè de dominio absoluto in temporalibus & spiritualibus agatur, maximè rursus ab utraque illa parte cavendum esse, ne nomen sive juvenis, sive senis ineptii alienae tantum ambitioni atque libidini turpiter inserviat.
units.tr: We proceed to the age of those to be elected. In the Old Testament the Levites ministered from their thirtieth to their fiftieth year (Num. 4:3). In the New Testament no fixed age for the ministers of the Church is laid down. The younger may be appointed as elders, or the older, provided they are fit. But since the combination of the required gifts is rarer in youth, one must above all look to this, lest an premature election do harm. For this reason a certain number of years is rightly prescribed in the Churches, below which those who have not yet reached it are not readily set over congregations. Such regulations existed also in the primitive Church, though they varied according to place and time. Meanwhile prudence and the fairness of the leading men were always left free to provide here, if something ought to be done otherwise; and in particular, at times, to relax something of the rigour of the law, either because of the necessity of the time and a lack of ministers, or because of the extraordinary and mature fitness of certain young men, when this is what the grace of the Holy Spirit evidently wills, so that it seems to have leapt over the limits at the first. For this reason also the young Timothy and perhaps (Titus 2:6–7) Titus too were set over many others, though older in age, by the Apostle. Of such men Ignatius rightly wrote to the Magnesians: Nor is the youth of the bishop to be despised, but all reverence is to be given to him according to the will of God the Father, just as I know the holy presbyters did, not looking to the youth that appears, but to the prudence that he has in God. For the aged are not always wise, nor do the old necessarily possess understanding, but the spirit which is in men. But he wrote this only of such rarer cases. On the other hand, it is also plain that for the laborious ministry of the Gospel a vigorous body, a firm memory and a keen wit and judgment are required; and therefore, although some indulgence and every kind of help must be given to the weaknesses of those whom this very diligence in office has perhaps hastened, that ministry must by no means be newly committed to men already decrepit and failing in body, becoming childish again in mind. Rather, the greater the ministry to be conferred, the greater care must be taken on both sides in these matters. And if the question is of absolute dominion in temporal and spiritual affairs, one must again be especially on guard on both sides that the name either of a youth or of an old man should not shamefully serve the ambition and lust of others.

units.la: II. Primi per aliquot secula Episcopi Romani, ut à reliquis commendabantur, ita etiam ab aetate digna, neq; ullum reperiebatur hac in parte ἀπαξίας, labentibus novem primis seculis, vestigium. Sed demum seculo illo ferreo atque plumbeo, decimo currente aetatis extremum unum, nimia juventus magno Religionis ludibrio in sede etiam Romana Praesules foedare coepit electos. Atque praenuntia quasi calamitatis Romanae Rhemensis erat, puero quinquennii ibi ad Archiepiscopatum evecto. Illud planè tunc primum contigit in Ecclesia Dei, inquit Baronius ad an. 925. n. 9. videri monstrum, nunquam hactenus in orbe Christiano visum nec auditum, imò nec puto mente conceptum, cùm videlicet puer nondum quinquennis, nondum alicujus inferioris ordinis capax, vix ferula prima addiscens elementa, Rhemensis eligitur Archiepiscopus. Electione postmodum ex Frodoardo describit; atque Johannis X. confirmationem, tandemque suam subjungit querelam. Vidisti Lector, inquit, cujus auctoritate Pontificis (si tamen ipse Pontifex est dicendus) id primum fuerit introductum in Ecclesia Dei, Joannis X. quo turpior nullus, cujus sicut ingressus in Cathedram Petri infamissimus, ita & exitus nefandissimus. Non ista Nicolaus vel audire tulisset, aliquisve alius legitimè electus Pontifex, sed opus illo dignum, quem infamis femina, infami opere in Petri Solium intrusisset. Tales igitur dantur Episcopi Romani atque tam bene electi! Addit, ista in exemplum citò transisse; Et tandem Utinam, quod hoc saeculo ortum, cum eodem saeculo fuisset extinctum, & non in posteriora saecula propagatum tantum nefas, quo jura omnia Ecclesiastica sauciantur. III. Nòm
units.tr: II. For some centuries the Roman bishops were commended, as by the rest, so also for a worthy age; and in this respect no trace of any disgrace [ἀπαξίας] was to be found while the first nine centuries ran their course. But at last, in that iron and leaden age, when the tenth century was reaching its final decade, excessive youth began, to the great mockery of religion, to defile even the Roman See with elected prelates. And the Archbishop of Rheims, who was raised to his archbishopric there while a boy of five years, was a kind of harbinger of the Roman calamity. That was then the first time that such a thing happened in the Church of God, says Baronius at the year 925, n. 9, a monster never before seen or heard of in the Christian world, nor, I think, even conceived in the mind: namely, that a boy not yet five years old, not yet capable of any lower order, scarcely learning the first letters with the rod, should be chosen Archbishop of Rheims. He then describes the election from Flodoard, and adds the confirmation of John X and finally his own complaint. You have seen, reader, he says, by whose authority (if indeed he is to be called a pope) this was first introduced into the Church of God: John X, than whom none was more shameful, whose entrance into the chair of Peter was most infamous, and whose end most wicked. Nicholas would not have tolerated such things, nor would any other lawfully elected pontiff; but he was a man worthy of that, whom an infamous woman had thrust into the throne of Peter by an infamous deed. Such, then, are the Roman bishops, and so well chosen! He adds that these things quickly passed into a precedent. And at last: Would that this wickedness, which arose in this century, had been extinguished with the same century, and had not been propagated into later centuries, by which all ecclesiastical laws are wounded! III. No

units.la: III. Non diu certè posthac apparuit Ecclesiæ Romanæ hac etiam in parte dedecus. Idem enim Baronius ad an. 931. n. 1. narrat intrusionem Joannis, Sergii Pseudo-Papæ ex Marozia filii; (En fructum sub cœlibatûs necessitate electi!) Widonis Tuscia Marchionis & matris potentiâ factam, atque subjungit; Pseudo-Pontificem (omnes ipsi sunt Pseudo-Pontifices, neque tunc alios Roma habuit) adhuc ætate juniorem fuisse oportuit, qui matrem talem meretricem haberet ætate florentem, amoribus aptam, adeò ut suâ pulchritudine Hugonem Italiæ Regem post mariti Widonis obitum provocárit, & immenso ejus damno in urbem protraxerit. En igitur Pontificum ætatem cognoscendi rationem! Pontificis, à quo tanto monstro Rom. Ecclesia deformiter invasa conculcata fuit, inquit idem, Baronius, ibidem.
units.tr: III. Certainly not long after this, the disgrace of the Roman Church appeared in this respect too. For the same Baronius, at the year 931, n. 1, relates the intrusion of John, the pseudo-pope Sergius's son by Marozia (behold the fruit of those elected under the necessity of celibacy!), brought about by the power of Guy, Marquis of Tuscany, and his mother; and he adds: The pseudo-pontiff (all of them were pseudo-pontiffs, nor did Rome then have any others) must have been still younger in age, since he had a mother who was a harlot, in the bloom of her age and fit for love, so that by her beauty, after the death of her husband Guy, she provoked Hugh, King of Italy, and drew him to the city to its immense loss. Behold, then, the way of knowing the age of the pontiffs! Of the pontiff by whom the Roman Church was deformed, invaded and trampled by such a monster, says the same Baronius, in the same place.

units.la: IV. Aliud exemplum suppeditat ad an. 955. n. 2. 3. & 4. in Johanne XII. cujus pater Albericus munitione S. Angeli occupatâ atque Romanæ Urbis Principatu sibi vindicato filium hæredem habuit hunc, qui tyrannus duplex malorum consilio efficitur: dum etiam in Ecclesia, inquit Baronius, ambiens principatum summum Pontificatum usurpat, quò totius orbis Christiani Principibus spirituali regimine præsit. Addunt, ita pergit, faces homines factiosi insano puero, ut quæ ejus ætatem superant, audeat atque perficiat. An autem ipse hoc tempore, hæc porrò habet, plenam pubertatem expleverit, ex his, quæ Luitprandus, qui cuncta habebat pra oculis, scribit, possumus dubitare, dum recitat Imperatoris Ottonis verba de ipso dicentis: Puer est, facile bonorum mutabitur exemplo virorum. Hæc Otto, dum excusat in adolescentulo audita scelera, planè significans ejus ætatem, quum plenam ephœbiam non excesserit. Verùm & illud magnopere considerandum est, sic monet n. 3. ad rei veritatem investigandam, quòd quando Otto Imperator dicebat ista, octavum ipse agebat in Pontificatu annum. — At quot annorum Octavianus hoc tempore esse potuit, qui puer & puerilia gerens, nominatus fuit ab Imperatore post annos octo? Erit & hoc haud adeò difficile reperire, si nuptiarum patris & matris ejus recta ratio certi temporis habeatur. Constat quidem, Luitprando auctore & aliis, quòd pater ejus duxit uxorem Aldam Hugonis Regis filiam circa finem a. 936. adeò ut ipse etiam si primogenitus fuit, non potuerit nasci ante annum 37. qua ratione dicendum esset, ipsum ad summum nonnisi annos 18. habere potuisse, cùm invasit Pontificatum. Verùm ipsum non fuisse primogenitum, ex eo possumus intelligere, quòd, cùm constet, ante hac vitam clericalem amplexum esse, alium cui Principatus deberetur, natum esse ante ipsum, primòque conjugii anno natum, certè nonnisi nonnisi agentem 18. annum creatum Pontificem oportuit; certè non æta-te maturiorem, sed sine dubio juniorem; Ut puerum fuisse adhuc electionis vel intrusionis tempore certum quoque sit, quo quidem nomine eum octavo adhuc Pontificatûs sui anno ab Ottone appel-latum esse jam jam ex Luitprando & Baronio audivimus. Abortivum istum, pergit, tunc parturiit Roma tyrannis vi pollens & c. atque ita, qui nec ætate Diaconus esse potuit, ostensus est tanquam in scena mimus Pontificem agens. Attamen accedens consensus, hunc tolerandum utcunque perditissima illa tempora persuaserunt magis, quàm Ecclesiam schismate scindere, cujus vitandi causâ, utpote mali omnium pessimi, universa Catholica Ecclesia eum est venerata Pontificem, minoris sciens esse malí monstruosum quantumlibet caput ferre, quàm duobus capitibus infamari & secari corpus unum in duo.
units.tr: IV. He supplies another example, at the year 955, nn. 2, 3 and 4, in John XII. His father Alberic, having seized the fortress of St Angelo and claimed for himself the princely rule of the city of Rome, had this son as heir, who became a double tyrant by the counsel of evil: since he also, Baronius says, aspiring in the Church to the supreme principate, usurps the pontificate, so that he might preside over the princes of the whole Christian world with spiritual rule. They add, he goes on, that factious men goaded the mad boy so that he would dare and accomplish things beyond his age. But whether he himself, at this time, still held these things, had completed full manhood, we may doubt from what Liutprand, who had everything before his eyes, writes, when he recites the words of the Emperor Otto speaking of him: He is a boy; he will easily be changed by the example of good men. Thus Otto, while excusing the crimes heard of the young man, plainly indicates his age, since he had not yet passed the full age of youth. But this too must be greatly considered, as Baronius advises at n. 3 for investigating the truth of the matter: that when Emperor Otto said these things, he himself was in the eighth year of his pontificate. — But how old could Octavian have been at this time, who, being a boy and doing boyish things, was named by the Emperor after eight years? This too will not be very hard to discover, if the correct reckoning of the time of the marriage of his father and mother is taken. It is indeed established, on the authority of Liutprand and others, that his father married Alda, daughter of King Hugh, about the end of the year 936, so that even if he was the firstborn he could not have been born before his thirty-seventh year. By this reasoning it would have to be said that he could have been at most eighteen years old when he seized the pontificate. But that he was not the firstborn we can understand from the fact that, since it is established that before this he had embraced the clerical life, another to whom the principate was due was born before him, and born in the first year of the marriage; so he must certainly have been created pontiff, not in his more mature age, but, without doubt, while still younger, being in his eighteenth year. That he was still a boy at the time of the election or intrusion is also certain, since we have just heard from Liutprand and Baronius that he was named by Otto in the eighth year of his pontificate. Then Rome, powerful by violence and tyranny, gave birth to this miscarriage, he goes on, and so he who could not even be a deacon by age was displayed, like a mime on the stage, playing the pontiff. Yet the consent that followed persuaded those most desperate times to tolerate him somehow, rather than to split the Church by schism; and to avoid this, as the worst of all evils, the whole Catholic Church venerated him as pontiff, judging it a lesser evil to bear a monstrous head, however great, than to be disgraced by two heads and to have one body cut in two.

units.la: V. Quibus quidem omnibus Baronius prodit varios & magnos electionum Pontificum Romanorum, ratione eorum, qui eliguntur, nævos. Puer electus fuit, puer sceleratissimus, atque indies pejor, pejor in Pontificatu factus, vel in scelere à marito adulterae vel à Dæmone interfectus, & tamen in Concilio sub eo Romae habito, quod Baronio laudatissimum est, piissimus atque sanctissimus D. Papa; saepe audire meruit. Legitimusne Pontifex fuit, qui nec ætate Diaconus esse potuit? Non credidit Baronius, fuisse, sed mimum in scena tanquam Pontificem agentem. En igitur heic mimicam atque scenicam planè successionem! Sed consensus accessit, atque eum pro Pontifice venerata est Ecclesia; Consensus accessit ferentium, quod mutare non poterant, æquè in intrusione, quam tamen illegitimam fuisse ajunt, ac in Pontificatu, qui proin ejusdem valoris extitit; consensus accessit Romanorum in silentio suo monstrum detestantium, licèt cæterùm approbare visi sint, quos alii, parùm fortè de indignitate edocti, secuti sunt, in ignorantia atque ex errore suo, alio Papâ non existente præter hoc caput monstruosum. Consensus accessit, sed ita, ut indignitate moti duo Cardinales Imperatorem (narrat Platina in Joh. XIII.) literis obsecrârint, ut clerum populúmque Rom. è manibus Berengarii Joannisque duodecimi vindicare conaretur, aliter Christianam fidem unâ cum Imperio perituram; sed ita, ut mox Imperator cum Concilio alium suffecerit, duo adeóque capita extiterint, circa quæ hodienum fluctuant. Quid talis consensus pro Johanne potuit? Et quis Tyrannorum simili consensu non legitimatur? Præterea, ipsa illa perditissima respectu Capitum & Ecclesiæ Romanæ tempora
units.tr: V. Baronius sets out from all of this various great blemishes in the elections of Roman Pontiffs, with respect to the men who were elected. A boy was elected, a most wicked boy, and worse every day; he became worse still in the Pontificate, and was killed, either by the husband of an adulteress or by a demon. Yet in the council held at Rome under him, which Baronius calls most praiseworthy, the most pious and most holy lord Pope, he was often deserving of a hearing. Was he a lawful Pontiff, who could not even be a deacon by age? Baronius did not believe he was, but a mime acting the Pontiff on the stage. Here, then, is a wholly mimic and theatrical succession! But consent came in, and the Church venerated him as Pope. Consent came from those who bore what they could not change, equally in the intrusion, which they nonetheless say was illegitimate, and in the Pontificate, which was therefore of the same value. Consent came from the Romans, who in their silence detested the monster, although they seemed to approve; others, perhaps poorly informed about his unworthiness, followed them in ignorance and through their own error, since there was no other Pope besides this monstrous head. Consent came, but in such a way that moved by the unworthiness, two Cardinals (Platina tells it under John XIII) begged the Emperor by letter to strive to rescue the clergy and people of Rome from the hands of Berengar and John XII, otherwise the Christian faith would perish together with the Empire; but in such a way that soon the Emperor, with the Council, set up another, and so there were two heads, over which they still waver today. What consent could there be for John? And which tyrant is not legitimized by a similar consent? Moreover, those most wicked times, with respect to the Heads and the Roman Church,

units.la: Cuius exempli nævus magis detegitur. tempora cum hujus jactantia hodierna neutiquam consistere possunt, quibus sceleratissimos pueros atque pessimos invasores pro Patribus Patrum atque Vicariis Christi venerari necesse habuit; Atque si unquam schisma excitari debuit, & excitatum laudari meruit, tunc certe excitari debuisset, laudari meruisset; Quemvis magis, clamabant olim, cæso Bassiano, atque ei suffecto Macrino pacis turpis authore, quàm parricidam, quemvis magis quàm incestum, quemvis magis quàm impurum, quemvis magis quàm interfectorem senatûs & populi. Heic etiam (& multò magis, quia de Pontifice summo agebatur.) clamare debuissent; Quemvis magis quàm parricidam, respectu matris Ecclesiæ, quemvis magis quàm incestum, qui turpis adulter nefanda ratione spiritualis matris thorum conscenderat, quemvis magis quàm impurum; in sensu etiam proprio atque ratione corporis, si Bassianus unquam fuit, quemvis magis quàm interfectorem animarum, qui & memoratis Cardinalibus, re patefactâ, huic nasum, illi manum abscidit. Sic duo capita extitissent statim, sed unicum legitimum, alterum ab hoc, Deo assistente, statim deturbandum, neque corpus in duo secatum fuisset bonum, sed facile præstulisset purum impuro, virum puero, legitimum usurpatori; Ast quia bonum non fuit, atq; insuper sub continuâ tyrannide fuit, pars hunc tandem præstulit, præstulit ipse adhuc suo tempore (nefandum dictu) Baronius extra tyrannidis Albericianæ metum quidem constitutus, sed non extra metum perdendæ, abnegato Johanne, successionis, perdendæ superioritatis Pontificum respectu Conciliorum; & contrà admittendi Imperatorum in Ecclesiasticis, Conciliorum convocationibus, Papamm electionibus atque depositionibus, juris.
units.tr: The blemish of this example is further revealed. Times which cannot possibly agree with this present boasting of ours, when men thought it necessary to venerate most wicked boys and worst usurpers as Fathers of Fathers and Vicars of Christ. And if ever a schism ought to have been stirred up, and deserved praise once stirred up, then surely it ought to have been stirred up and deserved praise at that time. Anyone rather, they cried out long ago, when Bassianus was slain and Macrinus, the author of a shameful peace, was set in his place, than a parricide, anyone rather than an incestuous man, anyone rather than an impure man, anyone rather than the murderer of the senate and people. Here too (and much more so, since the matter concerned the supreme Pontiff) they ought to have cried out: anyone rather than a parricide, with respect to Mother Church; anyone rather than an incestuous man, one who as a shameful adulterer had mounted the bed of his spiritual mother; anyone rather than an impure man, even in the literal sense and in the reality of the body, if Bassianus ever was one; anyone rather than the murderer of souls, who, when the matter was revealed, cut off the nose of the aforesaid Cardinal and the hand of the other. So two heads would have appeared at once, but one would have been lawful, and the other, with God's help, would have been immediately cast down from that place. Nor would the body have been torn in two for good; rather, it would have easily preferred the pure to the impure, the man to the boy, the lawful to the usurper. But because it was not good, and moreover existed under continuous tyranny, one part at last preferred him, and Baronius himself, even in his own time (a thing shameful to say), set up outside the fear of Alberic's tyranny, yet not outside the fear of losing the succession, having denied John; of losing the superiority of the Popes over the Councils; and, on the contrary, of admitting the right of Emperors in ecclesiastical matters, in the convening of Councils, and in the elections and depositions of Popes.

units.la: VI. Tertium puerile monstrum exhibet Baronius ad an. 1033. n. 3. seqq.
units.tr: VI. Baronius presents a third puerile monstrosity at year 1033, n. 3 and following.

units.la: Prob nefas, inquit, cum tyrannide Alberici Comitis Tusculani ejus filius puer in Sacro-Sanctam Petri sedem intruditur, monstrum erigitur, statuiturque portentum. Cum enim morte duorum Germanorum Pontificum, Benedicti atque Johannis è domo sua Pontificatum, diu retentum egredi, agro animo ferret: ne id fieret, cum alium non haberet, filium, quem habebat, ætate puerum, malis artibus in Petri Cathedram Angelis reverendam idem Albericus intrusit &c. Et n. 5. Ut autem tantum nefas attentare præsumpserit: præcessisse diximus detestandum exemplum in puerulo electo Archiepiscopo Rhemensi, cui ad functiones Episcopales obeundas coadjutor fuerat datus Episcopus. Sic itaque, quod in primaria Gallinarum fuerat
units.tr: It was a wicked thing, he says, when, under the tyranny of Alberic, Count of Tusculum, his son, a boy, was thrust into the most sacred see of Peter; a monster was raised up and a portent set in place. For when, by the death of two German Pontiffs, Benedict and John, Alberic was grieved that the Pontificate, long kept in his house, was going out of it, then, so that this should not happen, since he had no other, the same Alberic thrust into the Chair of Peter, which is to be revered by Angels, the son he had, a boy in age, by evil arts, etc. And at n. 5: But that he presumed to attempt so great a wickedness, we have said that a detestable example had gone before in the boy elected Archbishop of Reims, for whom a bishop had been given as coadjutor to perform the episcopal functions. Thus, what had been done in the chief see of the Gauls

units.la: Tertium in Benedicto IX. fuerat sede male præsumptum, in Apostolica usurpari posse Cathedra execranda sibi persuadet ambitio. Quæ non audet furore percita dominandi libido &c. filium in thronum provehit (horrendum ac detestabile visu!) sedentem in eminenti Petri solio puerum. Etn. 6. Ingemuit ad aspectum Catholicus orbis, haud mediocre passus in electione adeo illegitima scandalum. Ubi etiam ex Glabro subjungit, modò decennem, modò duodecennem fuisse Benedictum IX, hoc enim intruso puero nomen datum. N. 7. primò declarat, cum absque controversia cognitum fuisse & habitum in Christiano orbe Rom. Pontificem. Postea verò quoad ætatem subjicit: Cæterùm quod pertinet ad ætatem, cùm testetur de ipso Petrus Damiani, ab exordio suæ creationis usque ad finem luxuriis inquinatum: plane possumus intelligere, haud adeò puerum adhuc impuberem fuisse, cui ex natura puritas adesl, sed ejus ætatis, quæ stimulis concupiscentiæ urgeretur. En igitur rursus dignam Capite Ecclesiæ ejus ætatem probandi rationem! Non puer fuit, quia semper luxuriis inquinatus. Neque tamen ætas à Glabro posita sic augetur. Luxuries varia est; ab exordio suæ creationis luxuriis inquinatus fuit, quoad ejus fieri potuit; Urit maturè, quod vult urtica manere.
units.tr: It had been done badly in the see of Benedict IX. Ambition persuades him that the execrable thing can be usurped in the Apostolic Chair. Lust, driven by the fury of domination, etc., raises his son to the throne (a horrible and detestable sight!), a boy sitting on the lofty throne of Peter. And at n. 6: The Catholic world groaned at the sight, having suffered no small scandal in an election so illegitimate. Here he adds, from Glaber, that Benedict IX was sometimes said to be ten years old and sometimes twelve, for that was the name given to the boy who was intruded. N. 7. he first declares that he was recognized and held without controversy as Roman Pontiff in the Christian world. Afterwards, however, he adds, as to his age: But as to age, since Peter Damian bears witness about him that from the beginning of his creation to the end he was defiled by luxuries, we can plainly understand that he was not so much a boy not yet of puberty, for whom purity comes by nature, but of an age that was urged on by the goads of concupiscence. Behold, then, once again a method of proving his age worthy of the Head of the Church! He was not a boy, because he was always defiled by luxuries. Yet the age set down by Glaber is not thereby increased. Luxury is varied; from the beginning of his creation he was defiled by luxuries, as far as that could be. Nettle that wants to remain, burns early.

units.la: VII. Quis jam tales legitimos Petri successores, Christi Vicarios, vera Ecclesiæ capita fuisse credat? Credat, quicunque velit, nos non obtusa adeò gestamus pectora. Ubi igitur tune genuinus Petri Successor, Christi Vicarius, Caput Ecclesiæ? Ubi à Petro ad nos usque continuâ serie deducta successio? Scilicet per mimos illos, per scenicos illos Pontifices! Quid judicandum de actionibus, decisionibus, ordinationibus, constitutionibus talium? Miseri Romanenses, conferte ista cum statutis & legibus vestris, quæ ad Sacerdotium inde à Bonifacio I. apud Stellam in Vita & LXXVIII. dist. c. si quis triginta, triginta, (qui & olim Senatorium ordinem petenti necessarii fuerunt;) ad Archidiaconatum, cum quo conjuncta animarum cura, Concil. Trid. Sess.24. c. 12. de Reform. vigintiquinque, ad professionem ordinum mendicantium viginti septem Extrav. c. un. de postul. Prælat. ad Generalatum & similia Episcopalibus apud Barbosam Collect. 15. n. 19. p. 19. rursus triginta, ad Abbatissæ dignitatem quadraginta apud Lezanam. Summ. quaest. Regul. T. III. verbo: Abbatissa n. 2. requirunt. Et cur non saltem tot annos etiam ad maximam Pontificatûs dignitatem? Conferte cum hypothesibus vestris aliis, & judicate quæso, qualis illa successio puerorum talium, & quid non æquè jactari, imò quid in ea jactari possit,
units.tr: VII. Who now could believe that such men were lawful successors of Peter, Vicars of Christ, true Heads of the Church? Let whoever wishes believe it; we do not bear such dull breasts. Where, then, was the genuine successor of Peter, the Vicar of Christ, the Head of the Church at that time? Where was the succession, traced from Peter down to us in an unbroken series? Clearly, through those mimes, those theatrical Pontiffs! What is to be judged of the actions, decisions, ordinations and constitutions of such men? Wretched Romans, compare these with your statutes and laws, which require for the priesthood, from the time of Boniface I, as Stella reports in Vita and LXXVIII dist. c. si quis, thirty years (which were once also required for one seeking the senatorial order); for the archdeaconry, to which the care of souls is joined, twenty-five, as in Council of Trent, Session 24, c. 12, On Reform; for the profession of the mendicant orders, twenty-seven, as in Extravagantes, c. un., On the Postulation of Prelates; for the generalate and similar offices equivalent to episcopal ones, again thirty, as in Barbosa, Collect. 15, n. 19, p. 19; for the dignity of abbess, forty, as in Lezana, Summa of Questions on the Rules, vol. III, under the word Abbess, n. 2. Why, then, not at least as many years also for the greatest dignity of the Pontificate? Compare with your other hypotheses, and judge, I beg you, what kind of succession of such boys it was, and what cannot equally be boasted of, indeed what can be boasted of in it,

units.la: Vitium perrò indicatur; sit, indicate; Nolite amplius dicere, semper Spiritum S. electionibus Pontificum speciali ratione assistere; Patimini tandem, ut adclamemus vobis: Væ Ecclesiæ, cujus Capita pueri extiterunt, scelerati pueri, nec in melius mutati; pueri, quibus non tantùm cura animarum, id est, de pæni. & re. cùm infirmitas. ars artium incumbebat, sed qui universales atque absoluti æternæ salutis humanæ arbitri existere debebant; Pueri, non antecessorum filii in regno hæreditario, sed invasores in electivo, invasores tamen, à quibus legitimam successionem ceu religionis fundamentum optimè scilicet derivatis.
units.tr: Further, a fault is pointed out; let it be pointed out. Do not say any longer that the Holy Spirit always assists the elections of Pontiffs in a special way. Suffer at last that we cry out to you: Woe to the Church, whose Heads were boys, wicked boys, and not changed for the better; boys to whom the care of souls, that is, concerning penance and repentance when there is weakness, the art of arts, was entrusted, but who ought to have been the universal and absolute arbiters of eternal human salvation. Boys, not sons of predecessors in a hereditary kingdom, but usurpers in an elective one; usurpers nonetheless, from whom, of course, a lawful succession was derived, as the very foundation of religion.

units.la: VIII. Saltum hic facere oportet à prima juventute ad ultimam senectutem, nam ut juvenes, imò pueros electos vidimus, ita hodie atque à longo tempore nonnisi senes, maximam partem decrepitos & quasi depontanos ad Pontificatum eligi videmus; Quæ extrema in eodem ambitionis sive propriæ, sive alienæ principio juncta, æquè etiam in se vitiosa sunt; quod de altero hoc, quoad senes nimirum repuerascentes, senes bis pueros eligi solitos, saltem propediem tales futuros, postquam tales eligi solere priùs probaverimus, mox ostendendum erit, vel ex eo, quod contingere solet, patebit.
units.tr: VIII. Here I must leap from early youth to old age. Just as we have seen young men, even boys, elected, so today and for a long time now we see only old men, for the most part decrepit and almost one foot in the grave, elected to the Papacy. These extremes, joined in the same beginning of ambition, whether one's own or another's, are equally faulty in themselves. That the latter, namely old men who become like boys again, and who are accustomed to being elected as boys twice over, or at least soon to become such, after we have shown that boys were elected before, will be shown shortly, and it will be clear from what usually happens.

units.la: IX. In supra allegato Cardinalis Azzolini Aphorismo æquè juventus ætatis ac Cardinalatûs inter obstacula ponitur. In Conclavi Urbani V. de Cardinali Ursino dicitur: Est nimis juvenis pro Papatu. In Conclavi Leonis X. memorantur i vecchi Papabili, senes Papabiles. In Conclavi Pauli IV. de Cardinale Perusino dicitur: Essacerbò col praticare questo alla scoperta, l'animo de' Cardinali vecchi, che già era per se stesso commosso, per l'invidia presente della fattione di Puteo di età più fresca di loro, per ciò che consideravano, che venisse dal tutto à toglier loro l'occasione, che potessero mai più reassumere le speranze del Papato. Id est: Exacerbavit sic aperte negotiando animos Cardinalium Senum, quos jam commoverat invidia præsens factionis Putei junioris, quia cogitabant sic planè sibi tolli occasionem ad reassumendam unquam spem de Papatu.
units.tr: IX. In the Aphorism of Cardinal Azzolini cited above, youth is set among the obstacles, equally with youth of age and of the Cardinalate. In the Conclave of Urban V. of Cardinal Ursino it is said: He is too young for the Papacy. In the Conclave of Leo X. there are mentioned the old Papabili, the old Papabiles. In the Conclave of Paul IV. of the Cardinal of Perugia it is said: He irritated the minds of the old Cardinals by openly pursuing this, which was already stirred up in itself, by the present envy of the faction of Puteo, who were younger than they, because they considered that this would altogether take from them the chance ever to revive their hopes of the Papacy. That is: Thus by openly negotiating he inflamed the minds of the older Cardinals, whom the present envy of the younger faction of Puteo had already stirred, because they thought that the opportunity to ever renew their hope of the Papacy was clearly being taken away from them.

units.la: X. In Conclavi Pii V. Cardinalis Farnesius putat, rogante Bor-romæo, ut hac vice & in hac juventute non cogitet de Papatu, che s'egli voleva ricordarsi degli obligi, che haveva con casa sua, poteva supplire all' età & à tutto il resto, che gli fosse d'impedimento; Si velit recordari debitorum domui suæ magnitudinem, posse supplere atatis & quemcunque cunque alium defectum. In Conclavi Gregorii XIII. Boromæo obstitit novitas — Quemadmodum etiam Creaturæ Pauli IV. fecerant, qui in Conclavi Pii V. noluerunt eligere creaturam Pauli III. dicentes, che era honesto che i Cardinali più antichi fussero preferiti a' più nuovi; id est; honestum esse, ut Cardinales antiquiores praferantur junioribus. In Conclavi Gregorii XIV. inter qualitates S. Gregorii adjuvantes numeratur, quòd fuit di età di 74. anni mal affetto & da non potere viver molto; annos 74. natus valetudinarius, & ineptus ad diu vivendum. Contra in eodem Conclavi inter qualitates Cremonæ ponitur, l'esser di fresca età non passando 56. anni; quòd fuit ætate præmatura, natus tantum 56. annos.
units.tr: X. In the Conclave of Pius V., Cardinal Farnese thinks, at Borromeo's request, that he should not think of the Papacy at this time and at this youthfulness: if he wished to remember the greatness of the debts he owed his house, he could make up for his age and whatever other defect; If he wishes to remember the magnitude of the debts to his house, he can make up for his age and whatever other defect. In the Conclave of Gregory XIII., novelty stood in Borromeo's way. In the same way the creatures of Paul IV. had acted, who in the Conclave of Pius V. would not elect a creature of Paul III., saying that it was fitting that the older Cardinals be preferred to the newer ones; that is, that it is right that the older Cardinals be preferred to the younger. In the Conclave of Gregory XIV., among the qualities of Gregory counted in his favour was that he was of seventy-four years of age, in poor health, and not able to live long; aged seventy-four, sickly, and unfit to live long. On the other hand, in the same Conclave, among the qualities of Cremona is listed his being of youthful age, not over fifty-six years; because he was of premature age, born only fifty-six years ago.

units.la: XI. In Conclavi Clementis VIII. non multùm de Cardinale Aldobrandino loquebantur, giudicandosi per l'età immaturo; immaturus enim respectu ætatis æstimabatur. In Conclavi Pauli V. Borghesius nunquam cogitavit, de se hac vice cum successu actum iri per la sua fresca età, ob ætatem suam vegetam. Atque in eodem Conclavi, cùm de eo eligendo ageretur, tardârunt senes, che vedevano troncar le loro aride speranze dalla vivida gioventù di questo Signore, qui videbant abscindi aridas suas spes à vegeta juventute hujus Domini; sed non eis satis concedebatur temporis ad consulendum contrà. Atque in Conclavi successoris, Gregorii XV. narratur, infinitos quasi Curiales, qui viderant Paulum V. tam vegetum, ut verisimile fuerit eum omnes Cardinales sepulturum eòdem aspirantes, spes suas depositsse. In Conclavi Urbani VIII. Borghesius senibus spem faciebat, ne accederent Ludovisio; In eodem nova Bulla videbatur omnia ordinâsse à favorede' Vecchi, in favorem senum: In eodem de Barberino non citius cœpta erat tractatio ob ætatem tantùm 55. annorum. In Conclavi Alexandri VII. multis displicuit quòd Rapaciolus quovis ferè momento dixit, ch'egli il non gravetur dell' età, se nimis juvenem esse, quasi verò, inquit Author, anni tantùm ei ad Papatum defuerint.
units.tr: XI. In the Conclave of Clement VIII., they did not speak much of Cardinal Aldobrandini, since he was judged immature by age; for he was reckoned immature with respect to his age. In the Conclave of Paul V., Borghese never thought that he would succeed this time on account of his youthful age, because of his vigorous age. And in the same Conclave, when his election was being discussed, the old men delayed, who saw their dry hopes cut off by the lively youth of this Lord, who saw their dry hopes cut off by the lively youth of this Lord; but they were not allowed enough time to deliberate against him. And in the Conclave of his successor, Gregory XV., it is related that countless Curialists, who had seen Paul V. so vigorous that it was likely he would bury all the Cardinals aspiring to the office, gave up their hopes. In the Conclave of Urban VIII., Borghese gave the old men hope that they would not go to Ludovisio. In the same a new Bull seemed to have arranged everything in favour of the old, in favour of the elders: In the same, the negotiation about Barberini had not begun sooner, because of his age of only fifty-five years. In the Conclave of Alexander VII., Rapaciolo displeased many because almost every moment he said that he was not troubled by age, if he were too young, as if indeed, says the author, only years were lacking to him for the Papacy.

units.la: XII. In Conclavi Clementis IX. erat Palotta, ma l'età di 70. anni, afflitta dalla podagra, non li poteva giovare; sed ætas 70. annorum podagra doloribus afflicta ei prodesse non potuit; quod indicat Author Cardinalismi p. 3. l. 3. p. 297. In eodem Durazzo nihil habebat, quod eum commendare poterat præter ætatem 75. annorum, infirmam & decrepitam, che sono mezi alle volte, inquit Author p. 3. l. 3. p. 299. che da loro stessi si aprono la porta al Pontificato, mentre i Cardinali pretendenti, quando veggono di non poter colpire, procurano di far qualche vecchio vecchio decrepito, per poter veder presto un' altra sede vacante, & le loro speranze sollevate; Id est; Qua sunt interdum media, qua ipsa aperiunt portam ad Pontificatum, nam Cardinales competitores, quando vident se non promotum iri, curant promoveri senem aliquem decrepitum, ut sedes citò denuò vacet, & sic spes sua renovetur. In eodem etiam erat Cardinalis Gabrielis, mà la sua età non gli servi per esser troppo robusta e sana la complessione, sed atas eum non juvit ob temperamentum sanum & robustum,p.301. Facchinetti verò considerans, se esser d'una età troppo fresca, atate non satis provectum, nihil ausus fuit de se præsumere in Conclavi, ubi erant tot alii seniores & meritis magis commendati. Ibidem præcipuus obex Odeschalchii ponitur nella sua età di soli 56. anni, robusto e sano al possibile, in atate ejus tantùm 56. annorum robusta & sana quantum quidem esse potuit; obex, qui quotiescunque de eo agebatur, in memoriam vocabat viginti duos annos Pontificatus Urbani, & proin tollebat ex mente Cardinalium bonam, quam de eo conceperant, opinionem & omne desiderium eum exaltandi; quia firmiter propositum erat Cardinalibus, nolle amplius videre claves rubigine in cujuscunque manu obduētas. p.302. Tunc etiam Farnesius plus quovis alio Papabilis habebatur, per essere in età sopra di 70. anni, di complessione debole, e di culto di vita stravagantissimo, pransando bene spesso à quell' hora, che gli altri dormono; e cenando quando gli altri si levano, quia erat jam septuagesimum atatis annum supergressus, temperamenti infirmi, & vita genere planè inordinato, sape prandium sumens, aliis dormientibus, & cœnam, aliis surgentibus. p 313. Tamen ibi p. 318. nempe Bonvisio Hispani favisse dicuntur juniori, per lo desiderio, che si trovava in loro, di veder un Papa giovine, per desiderium, quod habebant videndi Papam juvenem, ne quovis die expositi sint mutationum & variationum periculis; Mà la prima sua eccettione su quella della sua età di 62. anni e non più, e quel che più importa, robusto e sano, propria da poter vivere altri 20. anni massime per essere huomo assai dissaplicato, amando di goder del bel tempo, anco con iscapito de' negotii, onde gli altri Cardinali, che pretendono haver parte ne gli altri Conclavi, ad ogni altra cosa pensavano, che à dar le chiavi ad uno, che haverebbe aperto le porte dell' altra vita à tutti p.319. Id est: Sed ei primò obstitit atas sexaginta annorum tantùm, sana & vegeta, quod maximè impediebat, ut potuisset adhuc viginti annos vivere, præsertim quia non valde negotiis aut curis alligatus genio indulgere didicerat, etiam cum negotiorum dispendio, hinc alii Cardinales, qui volunt habere partem in alii[?] Conclavibus; omnia alia malebant potiùs quàm claves dare illi, qui aperuisset omnibus vitæ alterius portas.
units.tr: XII. In the Conclave of Clement IX. there was Palotta, but his age of seventy years, afflicted by gout, could not help him; but his age of seventy years, afflicted by the pains of gout, could not benefit him; as the author of the Cardinalism indicates, part 3, book 3, p. 297. In the same Durazzo had nothing that could recommend him except his age of seventy-five years, infirm and decrepit, which are sometimes means, says the author, part 3, book 3, p. 299, which of themselves open the door to the Papacy, while the Cardinal competitors, when they see that they cannot strike, take care to promote some decrepit old man, so that a different see may soon fall vacant and their hopes be raised; that is: There are sometimes means which themselves open the door to the Papacy, for when Cardinal competitors see that they will not be promoted, they take care to have some decrepit old man promoted, so that the see may soon be vacant again and their hope be renewed. In the same also was Cardinal Gabrielis, but his age did not serve him, since his constitution was too robust and healthy, but age did not help him, because of his sound and robust temperament, p. 301. Facchinetti, however, considering that he was of too youthful an age, not sufficiently advanced in years, dared to presume nothing about himself in the Conclave, where there were so many other seniors more commended by their merits. In the same place Odescalchi is named as the chief obstacle in his age of only fifty-six years, as robust and healthy as possible, in his age of only fifty-six years, as robust and healthy as it could be; an obstacle which, whenever he was discussed, called to mind the twenty-two years of the Pontificate of Urban, and therefore removed from the minds of the Cardinals the good opinion they had formed of him and every wish to exalt him; because it was firmly resolved by the Cardinals not to see the keys again covered with rust in anyone's hand. p. 302. Then too Farnese was held to be more electable than any other, since he was over seventy years of age, of weak constitution, and of a most irregular way of life, often taking lunch at the hour when others sleep and dining when others rise, because he had already passed the seventieth year of his age, of an infirm temperament, and of a thoroughly disordered way of life, often taking his meal while others slept, and his supper while others rose. p. 313. Yet there, p. 318, the Spanish are said to have favoured Bonvisi the younger, from the desire they had of seeing a young Pope, so that they should not be exposed every day to the dangers of changes and variations; but his first objection was that of his age of sixty-two years and no more, and what matters more, robust and healthy, able to live twenty more years, especially since he was a man rather lax, who loved to enjoy good weather, even to the detriment of business, so that the other Cardinals who claim a share in the other Conclaves thought of everything else rather than giving the keys to one who would open the gates of the other life to all, p. 319. That is: But his age of only sixty years, healthy and vigorous, first stood in his way, which especially prevented him from being able to live another twenty years, since, not being much bound by business or cares, he had learned to indulge his inclinations, even at the cost of business; hence the other Cardinals, who wish to have a share in the other Conclaves, preferred everything else to giving the keys to him who would have opened for all the gates of the other life.

units.la: XIII. In eodem Conclavi rumor, Rospigliosium Papam futurum, credebatur à multis, suppositò, velle sic Cardinales deponere Papatum apud hunc, il qual non potendo sopravivere al più lungo che 4. ò 5. anni, per i suoi attacchi, venendo in questo mentre à scemarsi probabilmente con le morti loro il numero de' Pretendenti più avanzati in età, ed avanzandosi sempre più gli altri, si sarebbe poi nell' elettione dell' altro incontrata minor difficoltà e facilitata la strada al resto de' Pretendenti p. 350. Id est; qui non ultrà quatuor aut 5. annos vitam continuare ob dura accidentia valens, interea temporis tamen mortem seniorum videre posset, simul quoq; numerum pratendentium diminutum, aliis contrà ætate & spe crescentibus, ut minor foret post in electione difficultas & via facilis redderetur reliquis pratendentibus.
units.tr: XIII. In the same conclave there was a rumour, believed by many, that Rospigliosi would become Pope. It was supposed that the Cardinals wanted to lay the Papacy on him, since he could not live longer than four or five years because of his attacks. Meanwhile the number of the older candidates would probably shrink through their deaths, while the others grew older and so the next election would meet less difficulty and the way would be made easier for the remaining candidates (p. 350). That is: because he could not continue living beyond four or five years, being weak from harsh ailments, yet in the meantime could see the death of the elders; at the same time the number of candidates would be reduced while others grew in age and hope, so that afterwards the election would be less difficult and an easy way opened for the remaining candidates.

units.la: Ginettus videns tunc negotia aliquantum intricata inter Farnesium & Rospigliosum, & male disposita pro Barberino ipse cœpit quandam tractationem pro se ipso. In eum finem se contulit ad Barberinum, rogans, ut se commendatum habeat, & rogatus à Barberino, quo auxilio niteretur, respondit: omnem spem suam in ejus Eminentia & 82. annis, quos humeris gestaret, sitam esse. Boni sunt anni, (excepit Barberinus) sed pessimum est, quòd alia etiam requiruntur, & 30. Cardinales Ipsi plús prodesse possent, quàm 82. anni; me quod attinet, non Ipsi deero, tanquam creaturæ meæ bene meritæ, sed dubito valdè, me multùm pro Ipsius persona facere posse, quando nihil pro me ipso efficere potui — Neque mentiebatur Barberinus Ginetto, poichè le sue pratiche morirono nella culla, molitiones pro ipso quasi in herba suffocatæ fuerunt. Licèt idem suaserit; Fa di mestieri tentar la fortuna, per non iscusarsi d'haver ignorato il bisogno p.354. 355. Id est; Fortunam tentare juvat, ne quis sibi defuisse putetur De eodem Ginetto ipsum Conclave habet, eum per l'età di 83. anni, per ætatem 83. annorum satis probabilem visum fuisse, juvante eum l opinione della breve durata del Pontificato, e che non togl ie le speranze ad altri, opinione brevis sic duraturi Pontificatûs, quique spem aliis non adimat; sed videtur, ita pergit author, famam sordidissimam avaritia & Nepotum genium multùm ipsi obfuturum unà cum opinione, Barberinum ipsi non adjumento futurum, videbatur enim, eum tempore praterito non invenisse in illo tantum gratitudinis respectum, ut exaquare censeri posset beneficia à Barberinorum familia in Ginettum collata.
units.tr: Ginettus, seeing that affairs were somewhat tangled between Farnese and Rospigliosi, and badly arranged for Barberini, himself began a certain negotiation on his own behalf. To that end he went to Barberini, asking that he hold him commended. When Barberini asked what help he relied on, he replied that all his hope lay in Your Eminence and in the 82 years he carried on his shoulders. "Good years they are," Barberini replied, "but the worst thing is that other things are also required, and thirty Cardinals could do you more good than 82 years. As for me, I shall not fail you, as my well-deserving creature, but I doubt very much that I can do much for your person, since I could do nothing for myself." Nor did Barberini lie to Ginetti, since his practices died in the cradle; attempts on his own behalf were smothered, as it were, in the grass. Although the same man advised: "It is necessary to try fortune, so as not to excuse oneself for having failed to recognise the need" (pp. 354, 355). That is: It helps to try fortune, lest anyone think he was wanting to himself. The Conclave itself holds of this same Ginetti that at the age of 83 he seemed fairly probable, helped by the opinion of a short duration of the pontificate, which does not take away hopes from others; but it seems, the author goes on, that his very foul reputation for avarice and his nepotistic bent would greatly harm him, together with the opinion that Barberini would not be of help to him; for it seemed that in past times he had not found in him such a sense of gratitude as could be deemed equal to the benefits conferred on Ginetti by the Barberini family.

units.la: XIV. Eundem ætatis respectum post mortem Clementis IX. obtinuisse, ex eo patet, quòd tunc ita canere potuit Febo Vaticinante L'Ambasc. di Rom. p.248. Conti, Nini, Roberto & Azzolini Chigi, Gualtier, Caraccioli, e Savelli, Pazzuli, Piccolomini, e Gorsini, Rospigliosi e Mancin sono di quelli, Che non havendo anco canuti i Crini, Non occorre di lor, che si favelli, Di leggeri per hor, dunque la passo, E per moltʼ anni lascio andarli à spasso. Id est:
units.tr: XIV. That the same regard for age prevailed after the death of Clement IX is clear from the fact that then one could sing, with Phoebus prophesying: "The Ambassador of Rome, p. 248. Conti, Nini, Roberto and Azzolini Chigi, Gualtieri, Caracciolo and Savelli, Pazzi, Piccolomini and Corsini, Rospigliosi and Mancini are of those who, not having their hair yet gone grey, there is no need to speak of them. Lightly for now I pass them by, and for many years I let them go their way." That is:

units.la: Contins &c. nondum canos crines habent, ne levis quidem de illis nunc mentio facienda, quare eos mitto & per multos annos animi gratia ambulare sino. Manet igitur ad hodierna usque tempora Lottini Dissert. de Concl. effatum: Quò quis senior, eò etiam est aptior.
units.tr: Conti etc. do not yet have grey hair; not even a light mention of them need be made now, so I send them off and let them stroll for many years for their own amusement. There thus remains, down to the present day, the saying from Lottini's Dissertation on the Conclave: "The older someone is, the fitter he is."

units.la: XV. Atque, quia sic ætas provecta commendat, hinc frequens Cardinalibus senectutem atque imbellem valetudinem simulare, feruntque, Cardinalem aliquando à Nobili Virgine de causa simulationis interrogatum causam quoque] aperuisse eandem cum illa, ob quam Virgines contraria quidem simulatione juniores videri velint: Hic quarit Sponsam, valdè cupit illa maritum.
units.tr: XV. And since advanced age thus recommends, it is frequent for Cardinals to feign old age and feeble health. They report that a Cardinal, once asked by a noblewoman about the reason for his pretence, also disclosed the cause, the same as that for which young women want to seem young by a contrary pretence: "He seeks a bride; she eagerly desires a husband."

units.la: Vide de hac simulatione L'Amb. di Rom. p.16. 21. 81. 103. 113. 235. 236. 239.244.245.255.257.294. Nec non Concl. Sixti V. ubi Savellius moribundum simulavit, sed creditum, che il suo male &c. malo unico, id est, nimio Papatus desiderio eum urgeri. Exemplum illustre, & quod omnium loco esse possit, damus Sixti V. quem & aliâs perfectum simulationis atque dissimulationis exemplar exhibuimus: Non si tosto si vide Cardinale, inquit Author Vita p. 1. l. 5. p.276. che comin- cio à caminare per quella strada, per dove si camina al Papato &c. Id est: Quam primum Cardinalis factus fuit, coepit illâ viâ incedere, qua ad Papatum itur; servans suum, quod jam ante conceperat, propositum claudendi oculos ratione negotiorum omnium, quae in mundo fiebant, nulli planè se addicens; ut co quietius vivere posset, vineam emit in vicinia S. Maria Majoris, ubi vivebat vivendi genere secretiori cum modesta familia. p.281. Fingebat, se multo magis provectum atate esse, quàm verò erat, & planè agrum atque infirmum, p.301.
units.tr: On this simulation see the Ambassador of Rome, pp. 16, 21, 81, 103, 113, 235, 236, 239, 244, 245, 255, 257, 294. See also the Conclave of Sixtus V, where Savelli pretended to be dying, yet was believed to be urged on by his one malady, that is, an excessive desire for the Papacy. We give, as an illustrious example that can stand for all, Sixtus V, whom we have already shown to be a perfect model of simulation and dissimulation. No sooner was he seen to be a Cardinal, says the author of the Life, p. 1, l. 5, p. 276, than he began to walk along that road by which one goes to the Papacy. That is: As soon as he was made Cardinal, he began to walk on that path by which one goes to the Papacy, keeping his purpose, already conceived, of closing his eyes to all the affairs going on in the world, committing himself to no one. So that he could live more quietly, he bought a vineyard in the neighbourhood of Santa Maria Maggiore, where he lived a more secluded life with a modest household. p. 281. He pretended that he was much older than he really was, and plainly feeble and infirm, p. 301.

units.la: XVI. Cùm invisendi essent Cardinales à Gregorio XIII. promoti, Montaltius, qui jam ultrà tres annos agrum atque languentem fimusimulaverat, & videri voluerat obnoxius mille infirmitatibus, sapendo benissimo, che i Cardinali ultimi, non cercano mai di promovere al Papato, che huomini non solo vecchi, mà di più infermatici, e di poca durata, per poter poi con la morte di quelli avanzar' ancor essi la loro fortuna; moltiplicò le sue infermità sinte ò le sintioni delle sue infermità, acciò &c. optimè gnarus, Cardinales ultimos semper promotionem senum imò decrepitorum & brevis durationis quaerere, ut iis mortuis & ipsi fortunam suam promovere queant; multiplicavit fictas suas infirmitates vel fictiones infirmitatum suarum, ut novi isti Cardinales eo facilius ad promotionem suam concurrerent, in casu sedis vacantis, qua brevi secutura videbatur, Gregorio de die in diem se pejus habente. p.305.306. In visitationibus non, aliorum ad instar, præceps erat, neque duorum mensium spatio 19. Cardinalium recens creatorum visitationes à se absolutas videbat, secundo aut tertio die nonnisi unicum invisens, plane languidum atque malesanum prę se ferens, atque apud quemvis se excusans, dicendo, che la debolezza delle sue gambe, cagionata del uso degli anni, che se gli erano augmentati su il dosso, non gli lasciavano libera quella buona Volontà, che haveva di rendere il suo debito; perche in fatti non gli restava altro di sano che la buona volontà: Id est: Infirmitatem pedum suorum, quam longus annorum usus effecerit, qui aucti sint super humeris suis, non sibi liberam reliquisse bonam illam voluntatem, quam habebat ad debitum reddendum; quia in facto non sibi aliquid sani restiterit præter bonam voluntatem.
units.tr: XVI. When the Cardinals promoted by Gregory XIII were to be visited, Montalto, who had for more than three years already feigned being sick and languishing, and wished to appear subject to a thousand infirmities, knowing very well that the newest Cardinals never seek to promote to the Papacy anyone but men not only old but also more infirm and of short life, so that with their death they themselves might advance their fortune; he multiplied his feigned infirmities, or the feignings of his infirmities, so that these new Cardinals would the more readily come together for his promotion, in the event of a vacant see, which seemed likely to come soon, Gregory getting worse from day to day. p. 305, 306. In visits he was not headlong, as others were; nor within two months did he complete the visits to the 19 newly created Cardinals himself. On the second or third day he would visit only one, showing himself plainly languid and sickly, and excusing himself to anyone, saying that the weakness of his legs, caused by the wear of years which had piled up on his back, did not leave him free that good will he had to render what he owed; for in fact nothing sound remained to him except good will. That is: The infirmity of his feet, which long use of years had produced, and which had grown on his shoulders, did not leave him free that good will he had to pay what was due, since in fact nothing sound remained to him except good will.

units.la: XVII. Observat etiam Author, Cardinalem 7. annos ætati suæ addidisse interrogatum, imò etiam non interrogatum de senectute sua locutum esse, ast Pontificem factum tot ademisse, forse, inquit Author, per far crepare i Cardinali; Id est: forte ut rumpantur Ilia Cardinalibus. Ob quam sermonis varietatem etiam ultrà quatuor ad nativitatis locum miserint, qui certum quid ibi cognoscerent. Atque ut eò magis omnes de sua ætate decrepita atque infirmitate persuaderet, non tantùm non cum ardore visitationes postulavit, sed neque ordinariò Consistorium frequentavit, atque illuc raro concedens modo brachio hujus, modò alterius inniti visus fuit, & quando per scalas ascendere aut descendere debuit, tanta, quanta concipi potest, arte usus est, quasi testaturus, se non amplius valere; Et quando exeundum fuit ex Congregationibus atque Consistoriis, ordine præcedentiæ planè neglecto, semper ultimus exivit, ad quoslibet quinque aut sex gradus quasi per quartam horæ partem quiescendo, quasi aerem captaturus, & quasi revera non plùs posset.
units.tr: XVII. The author also observes that the Cardinal, when asked, added seven years to his age, and even spoke of his old age when not asked, yet after becoming Pope took away as many years, perhaps, says the author, to make the Cardinals burst; that is, perhaps so that the Cardinals' sides might split. Because of this variation in his talk, they even sent more than four men to his birthplace to find out something certain there. And so that he might persuade everyone the more of his decrepit age and infirmity, he not only did not eagerly ask for visits, but also did not ordinarily attend the Consistory. When he did go there rarely, he seemed now to lean on one man's arm, now on another's; and when he had to go up or down stairs, he used such art as can be imagined, as if about to testify that he no longer had strength. And when he had to leave the Congregations and Consistories, neglecting the order of precedence entirely, he always left last, pausing at every five or six steps for about a quarter of an hour, as if about to catch his breath, and as if in truth he could do no more.

units.la: XVIII. Quod omnes maximâ admiratione replevit,eo in Pontificem electo, atque manifestato,arte omnia facta esse; revera enim omnia ex necessitate facere visus erat; Hinc omnes quasi ei commiserabantur, dicentes:Buon vecchio, havete fatto il vostro corso. Dio vi dia forza. Id est: Bone senex, absolvisti cursum tuum. Deus te confirmet ! Cúmque Cardinali Austriæ chartis unâ cum aliis ludenti nunciaretur,Montaltium adesse, respondit; Che va facendo questo Lazaro quatriduano ? Quid vult Lazarus ille quatriduanus ? Cúmque idem Montaltium in partes Hispanorum pertrahere vellet,hoc responsi tulit,che per lui non era più capace di far partito nel Mondo,per che gli suoi anni lo chiamavano di momento in momento nel Cielo; Id est; se non amplius capacem esse partium in Mundo sequendarum, cùm anni sui se singulis momentis in cœlum vocent. Multi Cardinales recens creati dicebant, quiescere debere,atque satis eum ab ætate excusari,neque amplius obnoxium esse debito tot visitationum Romæ consuetarum ; Ita etiam Torresius per scalam ascendentem cum tanta molestia,ac si halitus eum deficere velit,videns,manibus prehensum allocutus est ita : Monsignore voi siete carnifice con voi stesso, per voler esser generoso con gli altri: Domine, carnifex tuus es, dum aliorum ad instar generosus esse cupis. Ipse Castagnæ Cardinali dicenti: Monsignore,vi veggo molto cambiato di quello erate in Spagna ; Domine, multùm te video mutatum ab eo,quod in te erat in Hispania, respondit; La vecchiaia non ha discretione,mi tormenta più di quello vorrei ; Senectus in discreta est, me plus quàm quidem mihi gratum est,torquet, atque illo excipiente,videri sibi, se ex ore ejus audivisse, ambo n eodem anno natos esse, regessit; ad un huomo infermaticcio come me,dieci anni di vita sono venti; id est; homini valetudinario, qualis ego sum,decem anni sunt instar viginti.
units.tr: XVIII. This filled everyone with the greatest astonishment: once he had been elected and declared Pope, it was plain that he had done everything by art, since he had seemed to act out of sheer necessity. So everyone began to pity him, saying, Good old man, you have run your course. God give you strength! When the Cardinal of Austria was told, while playing cards with others, that Montalto was coming, he replied, What is this four-day-dead Lazarus up to? When the same Cardinal tried to draw Montalto to the Spanish side, he received this answer: that he was no longer capable of taking a side in the world, since his years were calling him to heaven every moment. Several Cardinals newly created said that he ought to rest, and that his age excused him well enough and that he was no longer bound to the many customary visits in Rome. Likewise Torres, seeing him climbing the stairs with such difficulty, as if he were about to lose his breath, took him by the hands and said: Monsignore, you are an executioner to yourself, by wishing to be generous to others. When the Cardinal Castagna said to him, Monsignore, I see you much changed from what you were in Spain, he replied: Old age has no discretion; it torments me more than I would like. And when Castagna answered that he seemed to have heard from his own lips that they were both born in the same year, he retorted: To a sickly man like me, ten years are as twenty.

units.la: XIX. Sic cùm à Cardinale Nepote S. Sixto licèt in speciem invitus,atque regerens,che non era più in stato di trovar si ne' Festini, se non amplius in eo statu esse,ut convivis interesse possit; ad convivium detineretur,bis deliquium animi (sed fictitium) passus est, ut dicto Cardinali de sua imbecillitate fidem faceret,quam & fecit, dum hic semel atque iterum dixit:Monsignore, si non mangiate, morirete prima d'esser Papa; Id est; Domine si non edis, morieris antequam Papa fias. Respondit Montaltius : E che si fanno Papa i moribundi ?
units.tr: XIX. Thus, when the Cardinal nephew of Sixtus invited him to a banquet, he at first pretended to be reluctant and replied that he was no longer in a state to be present at feasts; but when he was kept at the dinner, he twice suffered a fainting fit (though a feigned one), so that he might convince the Cardinal of his weakness. He succeeded, for the Cardinal said more than once, Monsignore, if you do not eat, you will die before you become Pope. Montalto replied: And do dying men become Popes?

units.la: Iudicii aliorum, quos deceperat;
units.tr: The judgments of others whom he had deceived;

units.la: Eorum, qua ante Convivium apud S.
