units.tr: Alphonsus, King of Aragon, in the Council of Siena, against Martin and for Benedict XIII, stirred up new dissolution and gave an occasion for it. VII. 1. 113.

units.la: Altempsius ex vindictæ studio in Concl. agit. VI 39. 1. de viab aliis illata queritur. 4 58. ejus in Concl. Sixti V. nimia de amicis amici fautoribus præsumptio, quam alii simulationem auxilii præstandi dixerunt, Sirleto nocuit. 3. 27.
units.tr: Altemps, from a zeal for revenge, acts in conclave. VI. 3. 9. He complains of the injury done to him by others. 58. His excessive presumption in the conclave of Sixtus V about the friends of his friend and his supporters, which others called a pretence of offering help, harmed Sirleto. 27.

units.la: Ambitio Prælatorum causa seditionum & discordiarum IV. 2. 106. principium in electione Pont VII. 1. 7. VI. 1. 7. olim aberat, nunc ordinaria est. 18 seq. atque in pluribus dum simul agit, Electionis negotium in longum protrahit. 22. abesse deberet. 30. suam dissimulare jubentur Papabiles. 3. 11.
units.tr: Ambition of prelates: the cause of seditions and discords. IV. 2. 106. The beginning of ambition in the election of the Pope. VII. 1. 7. VI. 1. 7. It was once absent, now it is ordinary. 18 and following. And in many cases, while acting at the same time, they drag out the business of the election at length. 22. It ought to be absent. 30. Those who may be made Pope are ordered to dissemble their wish. 3. 11.

units.la: d'Amboise Card. Legatus ambitiosus & temerarius. III. 2. 55. 57.
units.tr: d'Amboise, Cardinal, a Legate, ambitious and rash. III. 2. 55, 57.

units.la: Ambrosio quomodo Petrus Petra, & nomina alia modò Deo, modò hominibus tribuantur. 1. 3. 10. ejus de Elect. per Clerum & Pop. testimon IV. 1. 18.
units.tr: Ambrose: how Peter is a rock, and other names are given sometimes to God, sometimes to men. 1. 3. 10. His testimony about election by the Clergy and People. IV. 1. 18.

units.la: Amici in Conclavibus utiles, VI. 3. 11. Papabiles tamen amicitiam cum Nepotibus nimiam fugere jubentur. 5.
units.tr: Friends are useful in conclaves. VI. 3. 11. Yet those who may be made Pope are ordered to avoid too close a friendship with the Nephews. 5.

units.la: Ammonius sibi auriculam abscidit, ut non ordinaretur. V. 6.
units.tr: Ammonius cut off his own ear, so that he would not be ordained. V. 6.

units.la: Amoris bellum Cardinalium quorundam, VI. 1. 38.
units.tr: War of love among certain Cardinals. VI. 1. 38.

units.la: Anacletus. VI. 1. 5. seqq. quotus à Petro, & an idem cum Cleto. 1b.
units.tr: Anacletus. VI. 1. 5 and following. How many from Peter, and whether the same as Cletus. Ib.

units.la: Anacletus II, Schismaticus habitus, VII. 1. 66. ejus electio concors. VI. 4. 59.
units.tr: Anacletus II, regarded as a schismatic. VII. 1. 66. His election was harmonious. VI. 4. 59.

units.la: Anastasius Dicorus, Imp. Constantinop. Clodoveo R. Galliæ coronam mittit ab hoc deinceps S. Petro donatam, & Capiti Pontificum impositam. VIII. 1. 41.
units.tr: Anastasius Dicorus, Emperor at Constantinople, sends to Clovis, King of the Gauls, a crown, from then on given to St Peter, and placed on the head of the Pontiffs. VIII. 1. 41.

units.la: Anastasius III. P. in sola persecutionis antecessorum omissione laudabilis. VII 7. 19.
units.tr: Anastasius III, Pope, praiseworthy only for having omitted the persecution of his predecessors. VII. 7. 19.

units.la: Anastasius P. in Schism. electus. VII. 1. 27.
units.tr: Anastasius, Pope, elected during the Schism. VII. 1. 27.

units.la: Anastasius Historiæ Pontificum scriptor forte ex pluribus in unum conflatis constat, VII. 3. 13. genuinus Græcè & Latinè impensè doctus 1b. In quibusdam Codicibus habetur historia Johannæ Papissæ. 14. in Codicibus multis sunt fraudis quoad Johannam indicia. 12. hodiernòsque supposititios esse non frustrà conjicitur.
units.tr: The history of the Popes by Anastasius, the author, is perhaps made up of several pieces compiled into one. VII. 3. 13. Genuine, and very learned in Greek and Latin. Ib. 1. In some manuscripts there is a history of Pope Joan. 14. In many manuscripts there are signs of fraud concerning Joan. 12. And it is not without reason conjectured that they are spurious even today.

units.la: Andreæ Ap. quanta à Patribus tribuantur. 1. 6. 6.
units.tr: How much the Fathers attribute to Andrew the Apostle. 1. 6. 6.

units.la: Anicetus an Pio successerit, an ante eum fuerit, dubitatur. VI. 1. 7. ejus de Electione per Clerum & Populum testimonium. VI. 1. 14.
units.tr: It is doubted whether Anicetus succeeded Pius or came before him. VI. 1. 7. His testimony on election by the clergy and people. VI. 1. 14.

units.la: Annatarum semissis Cardinalibus obtingit. IV. 2. 52.
units.tr: A half share of the annates falls to the Cardinals. IV. 2. 52.

units.la: Antichristus in Ecclesia Rom. VII. 1. 67. 68. 71. elogium Innocentii IV. 7. 36. de Antichristis sui temporis Clericis queritur Bernhardus. VII. 7. 31.
units.tr: Antichrist in the Roman Church. VII. 1. 67. 68. 71. The praise of Innocent IV. 7. 36. Bernard complains about the clergy of his time as Antichrists. VII. 7. 31.

units.la: Antiochenì Episcopi non minori jure succederent Petro, quàm Romani. III. 25.
units.tr: The bishops of Antioch would succeed Peter with no less right than the Romans. III. 25.

units.la: Anti-Papæ quales. VII. 1. 126. hæretici etiam habentur cum asseclis. 127.
units.tr: What kind of anti-popes. VII. 1. 126. They are even regarded as heretics, with their followers. 127.

units.la: Antoninus quoad assertiones de Johanna Papissa refutatur. VII. 3. 5.
units.tr: Antoninus is refuted on his assertions about Pope Joan. VII. 3. 5.

units.la: Apostoli omnes extraordinarii fuerunt. I. 1. 10 omnes Vicarii Christi. 3. omnes fundamenta Ecclesiæ in certo sensu. 3. 10. non fuerunt Episcopi strictè dicti. II. 42. 43. non Cardinales. IV. 2. 7. eorum dignitas summa est dignitas Ecclesiastica humana & æqualis omnium. I. 1. 1. seqq. de eorum potestate mediata, vel immediata, discordia Monarchicorum. I. 4. 10. mitten-
units.tr: All the Apostles were extraordinary. I. 1. 10. All were Vicars of Christ. 3. All were the foundations of the Church in a certain sense. 3. 10. They were not bishops in the strict sense. II. 42. 43. Not Cardinals. IV. 2. 7. Their dignity is the highest human ecclesiastical dignity, and equal for all. I. 1. 1. ff. On their power, whether mediate or immediate, the disagreement of the Monarchists. I. 4. 10. Sending

units.la: mittentes Episcopos non sustulerunt electionem plebis IV. 1. 19. iis non succeditur simili potestate. III. 19. in sensu certo tamen. 21. sed non tam loci quàm doctrinæ & officii respectu. 22. non in donis personalibus. 23.
units.tr: sending bishops, they did not abolish the election by the people. IV. 1. 19. They are not succeeded by someone with the same power. III. 19. Yet in a certain sense. 21. But not so much in respect of place as of teaching and office. 22. Not in personal gifts. 23.

units.la: Apostolica sedis olim appellatio communis. III. 18.
units.tr: Apostolic see, formerly a common designation. III. 18.

units.la: Apostolorum Princeps non dicit Monarcham Ecclesiæ. I. 6. 5.
units.tr: Prince of the Apostles does not mean a monarch of the Church. I. 6. 5.

units.la: Appellationum in Rom. amor quantus. III. 47. abusivas Bernhardus severè notavit. IV. 2. 93.
units.tr: Appeals: how great was the love of them in Rome. III. 47. Bernard sharply censured abusive appeals. IV. 2. 93.

units.la: Aracœli ab Hispanis in Concl. impeditus. IV. 2. 27.
units.tr: Aracoeli: hindered in the Conclave by the Spaniards. IV. 2. 27.

units.la: Arcanum Regis Hisp. in Concl. VI. 2. 19.
units.tr: The secret of the King of Spain in the Conclave. VI. 2. 19.

units.la: Archiepiscopus Rhemensis puer nondum quinquennis. VII. 6. 2.
units.tr: The Archbishop of Reims, a boy not yet five years old. VII. 6. 2.

units.la: Ascanius Card. de mala in Concl. fide conqueritur. VI. 4. 3.
units.tr: Cardinal Ascanius complains of the bad faith in the Conclave. VI. 4. 3.

units.la: Athalaricus R. partes habuit in Elect. Pont. Rom. IV. 3. 31. dum aliquem deligere voluit, aliquando Schismati occasionem dedit. VII. 1-9. ejus epistola de Simonia. VI. 4. 46.
units.tr: King Athalaric took a part in the election of the Roman Pope. IV. 3. 31. When he wanted to choose someone, he sometimes gave occasion for Schism. VII. 1-9. His letter on simony. VI. 4. 46.

units.la: Athanasii de Elect. per populum testimonium. IV. 1. 20.
units.tr: Athanasius: testimony on election by the people. IV. 1. 20.

units.la: Atheismo occasionem præbent Pontifices Rom. VII. 7. 40.
units.tr: The Roman Pontiffs provide occasion for atheism. VII. 7. 40.

units.la: Athena an Seculo IV. fuerint, vel plane obscurae. VII. 3. 50.
units.tr: Athens: whether they were in the fourth century, or are altogether obscure. VII. 3. 50.

units.la: Audacia in Concl. requiritur. VI. 3. 17.
units.tr: Audacity is required in the Conclave. VI. 3. 17.

units.la: Aventinus primus Johannæ historiam palam fabulam esse dixit. VII. 3. 25.
units.tr: Aventinus was the first to say openly that the history of Joan is a fable. VII. 3. 25.

units.la: Augustinus quomodo illustria aliqua Petro tribuat. I. 4. 8. ejus de Petra sententiæ l. 3. 5. de Elect. per Clerum & Populum testimonium. IV. 1. 21.
units.tr: Augustine: how he attributes certain illustrious things to Peter. I. 4. 8. His opinions on the Rock. I. 3. 5. Testimony on election by the clergy and people. IV. 1. 21.

units.la: Avignonium Babylon ad Rhodanum. VII. 7. 49.
units.tr: Avignon, the Babylon on the Rhone. VII. 7. 49.

units.la: Avignonensis commoratio Italis captivitas Babylonica audit. I. 1. 4. quantum Galliæ nocuerit. VII. 7. 49.
units.tr: Avignon: the sojourn there is called by the Italians the Babylonian captivity. I. 1. 4. How much it harmed France. VII. 7. 49.

units.la: Avignonensis Card. instrumentum Simoniacarum Rhotomagensis in Concl. Pii II. artium. VI. 4. 33.
units.tr: Avignon, Cardinal: a record of the simoniacal arts of Rouen in the Conclave of Pius II. VI. 4. 33.

units.la: Avila Card. Aldobrandinum ad vendendas creaturas citat. VI. 2. 8. pœnitentiâ ducitur, quod eidem non baculo responderit. VI. 2. 37.
units.tr: Avila, Cardinal: cites Aldobrandini on selling creatures. VI. 2. 8. He is led to repentance because he did not answer him with a staff. VI. 2. 37.

units.la: ejus in Concl. pertinacia. 26. 4. 61.
units.tr: His obstinacy in the Conclave. 26. 4. 61.

units.la: Austria Card. non statim admissus de nullitate protestatur. IV. 3. 17.
units.tr: Austria, Cardinal, not admitted at once, protests about the nullity. IV. 3. 17.

units.la: Azorii Jes. de Elect. per Clerum & populum testimonia. IV. 1. 19. 21. 24. 16.
units.tr: Azorius, Jesuit: testimonies on election by the clergy and people. IV. 1. 19. 21. 24. 16.

units.la: B.
units.tr: B.

units.la: Babylon in Apoc. est Roma, ipso volente Bellarmino. II. 4. seqq. non Roma Gentilis, sed Pseudo-Christiana. Ib. 6. sed Roma non est Babylon in Epistola Petri, ubi sive Ægyptiaca, sive Chaldaica innuitur.
units.tr: Babylon in the Apocalypse is Rome, as Bellarmine himself wishes. II. 4. ff. Not pagan Rome, but pseudo-Christian. Ib. 6. But Rome is not Babylon in the Epistle of Peter, where either Egypt or Chaldea is meant.

units.la: Babylonica Captivitas N. T. commoratio Avignonii Pontificum. I. 1. 4.
units.tr: Babylonian captivity of the New Testament: the sojourn of the Popes at Avignon. I. 1. 4.

units.la: Babylonii Reges nomina mutare soliti. VIII. 1. 18.
units.tr: Babylonian kings were accustomed to change names. VIII. 1. 18.

units.la: Barba Sec. IV. seqq. apud Italos nullæ. VII. 3. 51.
units.tr: Beards from the fourth century onward were unknown among the Italians. VII. 3. 51.

units.la: Barbarii Philippi in Præfura Successor ob servilem conditionem non numeratur. VII. 3. 9.
units.tr: Barbarius Philippus, in the prefecture: his successor is not counted, because of his servile condition. VII. 3. 9.

units.la: Barberinorum regnum injustitiæ, avaritiæ &c. VIII. 2. 22. Quod non fecerunt Barbari, fecerunt Barberini. Ib tituli & insignia numerosa. Ib eorum Palatium sanctissimus Romæ locus. 35.
units.tr: Barberini: the kingdom of injustice, avarice, etc. VIII. 2. 22. What the barbarians did not do, the Barberini did. Ib. Their numerous titles and insignia. Ib. Their palace, the most holy place in Rome. 35.

units.la: Barberinus Nepos fraudulenter cum Rege Galliæ agit in Elect. Innoc. X. VI. 2. 27. agit ex vindictæ. 1. 39. ex contrariandi studio. 41. ex metu pœnæ. Ib. exercitii gratiâ proponit. VI. 4. 13. discordiam Chigianorum quærit. VI. 4. 14. respectibus Simoniacis indulget. 42. Simoniam adhibet. 1. 27. 4. 43. partes D. Olympiæ propugnat. V. 31. pertinax est. III. 4. 61. eligi cupit. VI. 1. 27. rursus ambit. 28. ob aptitudinem rejicitur. VII. 8. 16. atque satis sub Barberinis fuerunt Romani. VIII. 1. 35.
units.tr: Barberini, nephew: deals fraudulently with the King of France in the election of Innocent X. VI. 2. 27. He acts out of a desire for revenge. 1. 39. Out of a spirit of contradiction. 41. Out of fear of punishment. Ib. He proposes it for the sake of practice. VI. 4. 13. He seeks discord among the Chigi. VI. 4. 14. He indulges simoniacal considerations. 42. He resorts to simony. 1. 27. 4. 43. He defends the cause of Donna Olimpia. V. 31. He is obstinate. III. 4. 61. He desires to be elected. VI. 1. 27. He canvasses again. 28. He is rejected because of his unfitness. VII. 8. 16. And the Romans were quite enough under the Barberini. VIII. 1. 35.

units.la: Barlaam Monachus qualis & quando floruerit. VII. 3. 22.
units.tr: Barlaam, monk: what sort of man he was and when he flourished. VII. 3. 22.

units.la: Barnabas an primus Romæ prædicârit. II. 22.
units.tr: Barnabas: whether he first preached at Rome. II. 22.

units.la: Baronius Card. conqueritur de Simoniaca Pontificum electione VI. 4. 21. seqq. de intrusis per infames mulieres. V. 10. de intrusis invasoribus VI. 4. 58. seq. refutatur, quatenus intrusiones Ecclesiæ Rom. sine nævo ejus passio-
units.tr: Baronius, the cardinal, complains of the simoniacal election of popes, VI. 4. 21 sqq.; of intruders brought in through infamous women, V. 10.; and of intrusive invaders, VI. 4. 58 sq. He is refuted, in so far as he called the intrusions into the Roman Church its sufferings, without blemish.

units.la: nes vocavit VII. 1. 46. 47. quoad minorenni- | lb. I. 4.5. tanquam Jesuita scrupulosus in Con-
units.tr: ...called them sufferings, VII. 1. 46, 47; as regards minority (ibid. I. 4, 5); as a scrupulous Jesuit, he is rejected in the Conclave.

units.la: tatem, Joh. XII. 6. 5. respectu Bened. IX. 6. in- | clavi rejicitur, VII. 7. 4. an, quod effigiei adscri-
units.tr: ...minority, John XII. 6. 5.; with respect to Benedict IX. 6. ... is rejected in the Conclave, VII. 7. 4. whether, because it was ascribed to the effigy...

units.la: tuitu praejudicii a Joh. Papissa Rom. Ecclesiam | ptum, nullius per totam vitam mendacii sibi
units.tr: ...in view of the prejudice caused by Pope Joan, who oppressed the Roman Church; ...ascribed to the effigy, that throughout his whole life he was conscious to himself of no lie.

units.la: prementis. 3. 5. ex parte nugarum de nova Vi- | conscius fuerit. I. 3. 7. larvis Curiae veritatem
units.tr: ...oppressing the Roman Church, 3. 5.; on the side of trifles, concerning the new election and change of Pope Vigilius P. ... he is said to have been conscious of it; I. 3. 7.; he is said to have preferred the truth to the masks of the Curia.

units.la: gilii P. electione & mutatione. I. 15. seq. in eo, | anteposuisse dicitur VI. 4. 71. damnatis annu-
units.tr: ...Vigilius P. ... I. 15 sq., in that the popes excuse their wicked men; he is said to have preferred ...; VI. 4. 71.; he counts among the condemned...

units.la: quod Pontifices. 13. suos malos excusare, sal- | merat Sixtum V. VIII. 2. 9. non vult noctu eli-
units.tr: ...in that the popes excuse their wicked men, 13.; ... VI. 4. 10.; he counts Sixtus V among the condemned; VIII. 2. 9.; he does not wish that anyone be chosen at night, since the Pope was not made.

units.la: tem praejudicium ab iis imminens amoliri vo- | gere VI. 4. 16. contra eum in Concl. Pauli V.
units.tr: Cardinal Bembo: an atheistic reply given by Leo X. VII. 7. 58.

units.la: luit. 7. 87. operum ipsius impressio prohibi- | ex odio multa dicta VI. 4. 11 felicem aestima-
units.tr: Benedict II, Pope: to some extent the necessity of imperial confirmation is remitted after election by clergy and people. IV. 1. 8. VIII. 1. 27.

units.la: ta. VI. 4. 10 quaenam odiosa in Concl. Leonis | vit, quod Papa noa factus sit. VIII. 2. 9.
units.tr: ...VI. 4. 10.; what odious things were spread against him in the Conclave of Leo XI, ... ; VIII. 2. 9. ... that the Pope was not made.

units.la: XI. contra eum disseminata sint, quod 4. aut 5. | Bellum amoris Cardinalium quorundam.
units.tr: ...XI. ... that he wrote four or five histories; the War of Love among certain Cardinals.

units.la: historias descripserit; libri ejus mendaciis pleni | VI. 2. 38.
units.tr: ...histories; his books are full of lies; VI. 2. 38.

units.la: sint, aculeatus Scriptor sit, Cato, cum multa af- | Bembo Card. responsum Atheisticum a Leo-
units.tr: ...are full of lies, he is a biting writer, Cato; although he wrote much with great affectation about the affairs of Sicily; Bembo, the cardinal: an atheistic answer given by Leo X.

units.la: fectatione de rebus Siciliae scripserit, in S. Ja- | ne X. datum VII. 7. 58.
units.tr: ...with great affectation about the affairs of Sicily, he is wrong with regard to St James; VII. 7. 58.

units.la: cobum injurius sit, ineptus, difficilis iracundus, | Benedictus II. P. quadantenus remittitur ne-
units.tr: ...wrong with regard to St James, he is inept, difficult, irascible; Benedict II, Pope: the necessity of imperial confirmation after the election by the clergy and people is somewhat relaxed; IV. 1. 8.; VIII. 1. 27.

units.la: quasi tyrannicus, quo meliores dentur, cujus | cessitas confirmationis Imperatoriae post ele-
units.tr: ...he is like a tyrant, so that better men may be given; whose election they foresee will bring about schism or war; ...the necessity of imperial confirmation after the election of the clergy and people...

units.la: electionem Schisma aut bellum parituram | ctionem Cleri & Populi IV. 1. 8. VIII 1. 27.
units.tr: ...foresee will bring about schism or war; VI. 4. 10. 11.; VI. 2. 26.; ... the election of the clergy and people, IV. 1. 8.; VIII. 1. 27.; Benedict III, Pope, elected in a schism; VII. 1. 27.

units.la: praevideant. VI. 4. 10. 11. VI. 2. 26. ejus con- | Benedictus III. P. in Schismate electus. VII.
units.tr: ...they foresee; VI. 4. 10. 11.; VI. 2. 26.; his conscience ... Benedict III, Pope, elected in schism; VII. 1. 27.

units.la: scientiam rigidam timebant in Conclavi. VII. | 1. 27. a Clero & populo. IV. 1. 18. ab Imperato-
units.tr: …feared the rigid science in the Conclave. VII. 1. 27. By the clergy and people. IV. 1. 18. Confirmed by the Emperor. IV. 1. 33.

units.la: 7. 4. fortiter se opposuit Tosco Cardinali. 7. 6. | re confirmatus. IV. 1. 33.
units.tr: 7. 4. He boldly opposed the Tuscan Cardinal. 7. 6. ...confirmed. IV. 1. 33.

units.la: mendacio in Capellam perductus. VI. 4. 9. ejus | Benedictus IV. defecit a pietate primorum
units.tr: Brought into the Chapel by a lie. VI. 4. 9. His... Benedict IV. fell away from the piety of the first bishops.

units.la: simulatio. 7. praesumtio, de eo quoque in de- | Episcoporum. VII. 7. 16.
units.tr: Pretence. 7. Presumption, also concerning him, in the... of the bishops. VII. 7. 16.

units.la: terius mutando. VIII. 1. 6. ejus electio Simo- | Benedictus V. per tumultum eligitur. VI. 4.
units.tr: Benedict V. was chosen by tumult. VI. 4. 58. In the schism. VII. 1. 40. He is legitimate for Baronius, indeed a martyr; illegitimate for Onuphrius. Ib.

units.la: niace quaesita. VI. 4. 39. pro eo obligationes | 58. in Schismate. VII. 1. 40. Baronio est legiti-
units.tr: Benedict VI. Pope in the schism. VII. 1. 41. Removed by Boniface VII. VI. 4. 17.

units.la: emptae 2 contra eum conjuratio facta. lb. cur | mus, imo Martyr, Onuphrio illegitimus. lb.
units.tr: Benedict VI. so called, Pope in the schism. VII. 1. 41. What kind he was. Ib.

units.la: eligi debuisset ex joco Conclavistarum. III. 3. | Benedictus V. dictus VI. Papa in Schismate
units.tr: Benedict VIII. from the laity. VII. 5. 4. Pope in the schism. 1. 45. Carried on a black horse after death, he appears. Ib.

units.tr: Benedict IX., a boy. V. 28. VII. 6. 6. By force. V. 28. By simony. VI. 4. 23. In the schism. VII. 1. 46, 47. Made Pope; what kind. VII. 7. 25. Guilty of magic. V. 33.

units.la: ipsemet. V. 4. 65. | Benedictus VI dictus VII. Papa in Schisma-

units.tr: Benedict X. in the schism. VII. 1. 91. Simoniacal, VI. 4. 29; an usurper. VI. 4. 58.

units.la: VII. 1. 113 Vide etiam Eugenium IV. | Benedictus VIII ex Laico VII. 5. 4 Papa in
units.tr: Benedict XII. by his own judgment an ass. VII. 8. 7. Author of the triple crown. VIII. 1. 42. His detestable lust and epitaph. VII. 7. 41. He pursued his nephews with hatred and even denounced them with words. VIII. 2. 27.

units.la: Basilius P. imaginarius. VII. 1. 2. | Schism. 1. 45. equo nigro vectus post mortem
units.tr: Basil, Pope, imaginary. VII. 1. 2. Schism. 1. 45. Carried on a black horse, he appears after death. Ib.

units.la: Bellayus Card. non vult fieri Papa, id est, fi- | apparet. lb
units.tr: Cardinal Bellay does not want to become Pope, that is, the son of perdition. VIII. 2. 9.

units.tr: Benedict IX, a boy. V. 28. VII. 6. 6. By force, V. 28.

units.tr: Boanerges, an appellation. I. 3. 46.

units.tr: ...in the diplomas. 6. 24. etc. With respect to the confession... VI. 4. 29. usurper. VI. 4. 58.

units.tr: ...for himself. I. 4. 7. 8. The passage John XXI. I. 5. seqq. of the superiority of the Cardinals. IV. 2. 29, 30, 31. Benedict XII, by his own judgment an ass. VII. 8.

units.tr: The heads of factions are necessary in conclaves. VI. 2. 2. Some Neutralists think otherwise, though sometimes. Ib. By their authority they oppose freedom of election. 3. This is shown also from their names. 4. Yet their authority is not absolute. 6. If soldiers are sometimes led by inexperienced commanders among experienced soldiers, Ib. does the secret scrutiny hinder their authority? 7. What authority remains. 8. The vicious qualities of most men increase the vice that the election acquires from their excessive authority. 9. The requisites of the heads. 3, 17. Their ministers. 18. They sometimes lack virtue. 19. How far they ought to share their counsels with the creatures. 20, 25. Not to exclude the creatures. 22. Sometimes to divert elections. Ib. To take care that friends are chosen, or are chosen without their cooperating. 23. Always to keep watch. 27. Not to neglect the moments of time. 28. If there is a dispute between two, to propose a third. 32. To oppose one adversary to another. 34. To seek discord in the opposing party. 35. Sometimes to transfer the election to opposing heads. 38. To proceed by different ways. 39. To meet difficulties in different ways. 40. Sometimes to propose a new law. 41. Not to think easily of one's own exaltation. 42 and 43. To oppose skilfully. 44. To strive to conquer, 45, and to fear, 46. Not to concede victory; and they are bidden at last not to oppose too much those who deserve it. The heads of nations, however, are the emperors' brothers and the kings' kinsmen. Ib. Princes

units.tr: They wish, however, to be placed before princes. 34, 35, 56. To be esteemed. 92. Whether they perform their office. 94. Protectors of the kingdoms. 36. How they ought to conduct themselves in respect of the Pope. 97. The most holy ones indeed appear base on one side and ought to be so. Ib. and 98. But they live badly. 99. While they serve only as a pretext and assent to their luxury (noted by Urban VI, VII. 1), they ought not to be heard when they advise well. 37, 90. This is illustrated by the poverty of many bishops. 101, 102. They live very badly. 103 ff. 40, 42 f. They are not on that account worthy of the illustrious title of the Church. 41. They waste the princes' time by playing, with comedies etc., and deceive. 106. Sometimes very badly. 107, 108. Their bad life is further treated in prison etc. 40. On the other side, they bear no reproof. 109, 110. (They appear very much honoured and endowed with great power.) VI. 2, 28. VII. 1, 90, 91. Elections by the cardinals. 111 ff. See Election. Cardinal bishops formerly took precedence over others in elections. 117. Cardinal brothers-german, contrary to the canons. VIII. 2. 14, 21. They are members bound by blood to support the pope. VI. 2, 23. Some have a war of love. 38. For those, according to Bellarmine's mind, some hope remains. VIII. 2. 9. Why they wish to appear old: VII. 6. 15. They must court the favour of princes. 52. Protections of orders. Ib. The power to free a malefactor from punishment. Ib. Legations. See Legates. Why the Pope wishes cardinals to be honoured. 58. Their prerogatives, most of which. IV. 3. 18. Their manners must be pleasing to the Pope; they fear the emperors greatly in matters of right. 59. Their dress. 60, etc. The causes and mysteries of their peculiar dress. 63. Cardinals who are soldiers. 64. The creation of cardinals should not take place without the consent of the cardinals. It did not happen formerly. 67. It sometimes happens from not a few years. 69. Not to subject oneself too importunately to the inconstant, to say the election has already been made. 57.

Cardinalibus imberbibus in Concl. Votum datur 4. 12. Cardinales in Conclave hilari vultu sibi male volunt 60. unus alterum mendacii arguit 2. 37. Siculus probus electionis negotio denuo interesse non vult 4. 71. alii petunt indulgentiam irregularitatum in Conclavi 1. 15.
units.tr: to investigate others (52, 56), and what sort they would be if elected and what kinsmen they have; to look into the timing (54); to promote men like themselves (Ib.); not to allow some people time to deliberate on the contrary (57); not to have faith in appearances only, as with those who beg for votes (58); to hold everyone's reasoning to be against them and to fear everyone (59); that it is not allowed to sin twice in the Conclave, so they must consider (60); to avoid the vehemence of the passions and haste (61); they ought to be free from inconstancy and negligence (62). Beardless Cardinals in the Conclave: a vote is given (4, 12). Cardinals in the Conclave wish ill to one another with a cheerful face (60). One accuses another of lying (2, 37). The upright Sicilian does not wish to take part again in the business of the election (4, 71). Others seek indulgence for irregularities committed in the Conclave (1, 15).

units.la: Carolus M. & Ludovicus Filius de electione per Clerum & populum decernunt IV.1.22.

units.la: Chigius Card. Nepos quos honores jure perere possit in Galliam mittendus IV. 2.56. ejus spurii ex meretricibus diversis & voluptatibus, neglecta negotiorum cura VIII. 2.24. ab Aesopi lectione ad Ecclesiae regimen vocatus 32. vivente Pontifice tractat VI. 2. 43. ejus pertinacia 4.61. de verbis illius, se nolle nisi creaturam, judicium 2.10. simulatam protectionis promissionem ab Hispanis accipit 29. quantae authoritatis in Conclavi. 3.
units.tr: Cardinal Chigi, nephew: what honours he can rightly hope for, to be sent into France, IV.2.56. His bastards by various prostitutes and his pleasures, with neglect of business, VIII.2.24. Called from reading Aesop to the governing of the Church, 32. Treats of matters while the Pope is alive, VI.2.43. His obstinacy, 4.61. On his words that he would not wish to be anything but a creature, judgment, 2.10. He receives from the Spanish a feigned promise of protection, 29. How great his authority in the Conclave, 3.

units.la: Christus quomodo se talem probarit I. 1.57. non tanta in terris habuit & exercuit, quanta Pontifici Rom. tribuuntur 3.4. quasi primus constituitur Pont. Rom. Ib. est Petra, fundamentum Ecclesiae 3. 6. a Nepotismo alienus fuit VIII. 2; 25. Christi Vicarii & Petri Vicarii quam inconvenienter simul esse velint Pontifices 1. 10. Christi apparitio, quae dicitur Romae Petro ante mortem facta II. 48. processiones in omnibus dissimiles Pontificum processionibus VIII. 1. 48 in processionibus Pontificum Christus minus honoratur ipsis Pontificibus 45. prout etiam, qui personam Christi Dominicae Palmarum gerit, Papae pedes osculari debet. 9.
units.tr: Christ: how he showed himself to be such, I.1.57. He did not have or exercise on earth as much as is attributed to the Roman Pontiff, 3, 4. He is established as, so to speak, the first Roman Pontiff, Ib. He is the Rock, the foundation of the Church, 3, 6. He was free from nepotism, VIII.2, 25. How inconsistently Pontiffs wish to be at once Vicars of Christ and Vicars of Peter, 1.10. The apparition of Christ, said to have been made at Rome to Peter before his death, II.48. Processions wholly unlike the processions of the Pontiffs, VIII.1.48; in the processions of the Pontiffs Christ is less honoured than the Pontiffs themselves, 45. Likewise, he who plays the person of Christ on Palm Sunday must kiss the Pope's feet, 9.

units.la: Christi imagines specie differentes apud Pontificios I. 6.26.
units.tr: Images of Christ differing in appearance among the Papists, I.6.26.

units.la: Chrysostomus qualem Petro Primatum tribuerit. I. 6. 16.

units.la: Claves Petro Matth. XVI.19 tantum promissae I 4 2. non soli Ib 4.8. communes Apostolis 5. & aliis 16. praeter solvere & ligare nihil significant 12. seq. jurisdictionis & ordinis

units.tr: Clement VI, changed for the worse, VIII.2.6; commands angels, 1.4.22; what sort he was towards Bridget, VII.7.50.

units.tr: Clement VII, promoted himself by pretence, VI.4.13; what sort he was, VII.7.61; introduced an under-age Cardinal, IV.2.83; a nepotism hardly fitting, VIII.2.14; sold the Cardinal's galero, IV.2.85.

(VII. 8.14) mœror ex indigna Cardinalium creatione lethalis. 2. 86 Nepotismus VIII. 2. 18. Nepotem vocavit idolum cordis sui. Ib. ejus familia spelunca Leonum IV. 3. 8.
units.tr: In the election of Clement VIII something similar to the Schism happened, VII.1.125. Crimes attributed to him, 7.67. His goodness according to Sandys, 1.79. Delirium, IV.3.8 (VII.8.14). Deadly grief from the unworthy creation of Cardinals, 2.86. Nepotism, VIII.2.18. He called his nephew the idol of his heart, Ib. His family a den of lions, IV.3.8.

units.la: Columna Card. in Concl. Clem. VIII. vim patitur. VI. 4. 58.
units.tr: Colonna, Cardinal, in the Conclave of Clement VIII, suffers violence, VI.4.58.

units.la: Commoda propria principium in Electionibus Pontificum VI. 1. 30. seq. 3. 43.
units.tr: Private advantages as a principle in papal elections, VI.1.30 seq.; 3.43.

units.la: Compatres in Concl. prosunt VI. 2. 21.
units.tr: Compatres in the Conclave are useful. VI. 2. 21.

units.tr: The institution of the Conclave has been violated on several occasions.

Conclave Caput exaltationi suae studens non nimis prolongare debet 3. 43. Conclavis taedium 4. 63. facit Papam 64. Conclave post electionem diripitur VIII. 1, 15. 23.
units.tr: How often: 20. Instituted and restored because of discord in elections. 4. 60. The place of the Conclave. 3. 21. Questions about it. 22. Entry into the Conclave. 32. The freedom of the first day as regards entry for anyone whatever. 33. This is followed by the necessity of leaving; it is not permitted to live or stay in the Conclave. 34. The closing of the Conclave and the document concerning it. 35. Communication with outsiders is forbidden; sometimes it is set up, sometimes it is hindered. 36. Searching of food. 37. It is not permitted to go out; the custom of going out on the first day has been abolished. 38. Yet the sick may go out and return. 39. Twice everyone has gone out before the election. The going out of many and of all. 40. Concerning the going out of the Conclavists. 41. Guards of the Conclave. 42. Laws on provisions. 43. Practice. 44. The law on clothing. 45. Peculiarities. Ib. The chapel. 46. A brief outline of the Conclave. VI. 4. 71. What the Conclave of Peter was like. II. 56. The Conclave takes on various forms. VI. 3. 27. 40. In the Conclave the first assault is most fierce. VI. 3. 15. What the conclavial promise is like. VI. 4. 3. seq. Conclavial stratagems. VI. 3. 32. 34. 35. 36. 50. 51. 57. In the Conclave, as in war, one may not err twice. VI. 3. 60. How the Cardinals pass the time in the Conclave. IV. 2. 108. The terms of the Conclave are partly nautical, partly military. VI. 2. 37. In the Conclave discord, hence its length. VI. 2. 43. 4. 60. 61. seq. 2. 31. The Conclave: the head, striving for his own exaltation, ought not to prolong it too much. 3. 43. The tedium of the Conclave. 4. 63. It makes a Pope. 64. After the election the Conclave is plundered. VIII. 1. 15. 23.

units.la: Conclavista IV. 3. 25. quot singulis concedantur Ib. eorum privilegia 26. Capitula Ib. units.tr: The Conclavist. IV. 3. 25. How many are granted to each. Ib. Their privileges. 26. Chapters. Ib. The complaint of the Tridentines about their privileges. 27. Their authority (VI. 2. 3.), the time for deceiving, the way, and the art of speaking with those who live outside the Conclave. 28. Annoyances. Ib. They are mostly the authors of the Conclaves. 29.

units.la: Conclavium etiam nonnullorum authores sunt Cardinales Ib. relationes imperfectae Ib. non tamen nullius planè ponderis. 30.

units.la: Conclaviarii ministri praeter Conclavistas alii IV. 3. 31.
units.tr: Conclavial ministers, other than the Conclavists. IV. 3. 31.

units.la: Confessioni inaedificati fideles I. 3. 4.

units.la: Congregationes Cardinalium Sede vacante IV. 3. 15.

units.la: Conscientia delicatae in Concl. rejiciuntur. VII. 7. 4.
units.tr: Delicate consciences are rejected in the Conclave. VII. 7. 4.

units.tr: Conrad, Emperor, asks about Popes whose names do not fit. VIII. 1. 21.

units.tr: The Council of Constance: what it did with the Popes. VII. 1. 106. seq. Its silence about Joan the Pope in the condemnation of Hus. 3. 26. It prescribes and dissolves the times of other councils. 1. 111.

units.la: Constantinus adolescens quomodo ad dextram Diocletiani I. 6. 44. de Imperatoris humilitate respectu Pontificis figmentum I, 1. 2. Mandat Antiochenis, ut Episcopum eligerent. IV. 1. 20.

units.la: Gregorius I. invitus electus VI. 1. 19. confirmationis jus Imperatoribus asserit VIII. 1. 27. juxta de Dominis primus Cardinalium meminit IV. 2. 1. units.tr: Gregory I, elected unwillingly VI. 1. 19. Asserts the right of confirmation for the emperors VIII. 1. 27. Near the passage on the Dominis, he is the first to mention cardinals IV. 2. 1. Hints at the misery of the Popes VIII. 2. 9. Among good Popes the last, among bad the first I. 5. 13. Said to have struck down his successor, who opposed his acts and wished to burn his writings, by appearing after death VII. 7. 10.

units.la: Gregorius VII. sub antecessoribus simpli-cioribus quasi Papa VII. 8. 10. Papa in Schismate VII. 1. 56. a Clero & Populo electus IV. 1. 18. sed & accusatus, quòd per Magiam ad Papatum pervenerit, Diabolo suadente V. 33. qualis fuerit VII. 7, 28 Henricum Imp. de Simoniacis electionibus admonuit VI. 4. 53. solius Papæ pedes osculandos esse dixit VIII. 1. 8. de successore & hic de suo disponit IV. 1. 7. à Roberto Calabriæ Duce petit, ut à Clero & populo successor designetur IV. 1. 18. deponitur VII. 1. 56 decreti conclusio, in qua, qualis ille fuerit, docetur 57
units.tr: Gregory VII, under simpler predecessors, as it were a Pope, VII. 8. 10. Pope during the Schism, VII. 1. 56. Elected by the clergy and people, IV. 1. 18. But also accused of having come to the papacy by magic, at the Devil's urging, V. 33. What sort of man he was, VII. 7, 28. He warned Emperor Henry about simoniacal elections, VI. 4. 53. He said that only the Pope's feet are to be kissed, VIII. 1. 8. On the successor, and here he disposes of his own: IV. 1. 7. He asks Robert, Duke of Calabria, that the successor be designated by the clergy and people, IV. 1. 18. Deposed, VII. 1. 56. Conclusion of the decree, in which it is taught what sort of man he was, 57.

units.tr: Gregory XII, during the Schism; what sort he was; he refuses to step down, against his oath, VII. 1. 101. 102. He is said to have been absolved by the Devil, 7. 51. He warns the cardinals to avoid simony, VI. 4. 55. Being absent, he abdicates himself, 108.

units.la: Gregorius XIII juris Divini ignarissimus VII. 8. 8. lætatur de Laniena Parisi 7. 66. ejus bonitas qualis fuerit 79. Simulatores odio habuisse dicitur VI. 4. 6. eum occidere tentanti quidam, ut alius melius eligeretur VII. 8. 17. Nepotismū pessimum introduxit, revera Buon compagno, bonum socium se exhibuit VIII. 2. 16.
units.tr: Gregory XIII, most ignorant of divine law, VII. 8. 8. He rejoices at the slaughter in Paris, 7. 66. What his goodness was like, 79. He is said to have hated flatterers, VI. 4. 6. Some tried to kill him so that another, better man might be elected, VII. 8. 17. He introduced the very worst nepotism; in truth he showed himself a "buon compagno," a good fellow, VIII. 2. 16.

units.la: Gregorius XIV. Vestitum Cardinalium Religiosorum constituit IV. 2. 61. ejus Nepotismus pessimæ notæ VIII. 2. 18.
units.tr: Gregory XIV. He established the dress of religious cardinals, IV. 2. 61. His nepotism was of the worst kind, VIII. 2. 18.

units.la: Gregorius XV. legem de vestitu Cardinalium fert IV. 2. 61. à Nepote, neglectâ rerum curâ dependere voluit, avidissimo VIII. 2. 19. distulit aliquando tractationem arduam, donec Nepos magis exercitatus esset 32. imò à fœmina se regi passus est VII. 8. 15.
units.tr: Gregory XV. He brings in a law on the dress of cardinals, IV. 2. 61. Most greedy, he wished the care of affairs to depend on his nephew, neglecting them, VIII. 2. 19. He once put off a difficult business until his nephew had gained more experience, 32. Indeed, he allowed himself to be ruled by a woman, VII. 8. 15.

units.la: Hispani diligentes in retinendo & augendo VI. 23. amant Pontifices quietos 16. 21. humilis conditionis Ib. 15. nolunt optimis qualitatibus instructos 19. Hispaniæ Rex jus præsentationis habet in Regno suo 23. Hispaniæ Regis interventus in electionibus Pontificum 17. &c. quintæ authoritatis apud Pontifices aliquando Ib nunquam amatur, à Pontificibus VIII. 24. falsò prætexitur in Conclavi VI. 2. 26. Hispanorum erga Sixtum V. odium & contrà eum calumniæ VII. 7. 67. Chigio falsò promittunt 1. protectionem VI. 2. 29. Hispani excluduntur in Concl. VII. 4. 10. Hispanis grati, vel addicti 11.
units.tr: The Spanish are diligent in keeping and increasing, VI. 23. They love quiet popes, 16. 21. Of humble condition, Ib. 15. They do not want men furnished with the best qualities, 19. The King of Spain has the right of presentation in his kingdom, 23. The intervention of the King of Spain in papal elections, 17. etc. Fifth in authority with the popes; sometimes Ib., never loved by the popes, VIII. 24. Falsely pretended in the Conclave, VI. 2. 26. The Spaniards' hatred of Sixtus V and their slanders against him, VII. 7. 67. They falsely promise Chigi protection, VI. 2. 29. The Spaniards are excluded from the Conclave, VII. 4. 10. Those pleasing to or devoted to the Spaniards, 11.

units.la: Jesuita mali suasores VII. 7. 68. viperæ Ib. Jesuitam etiam Papam regunt 5. 19. unus Papa, omnes Papæ; ex specie pietatis & eruditione faciunt instrumenta ambitionis, eorum onus intolerabile Ib. & 20. Jesuitæ non facile eliguntur 21. videri volunt dignitates respuere Ib. Authorum Castratores 3. 10. opus habent Confessore Pontifice 7. 67. & Dominicani præcipui in Papatu Ordines Religiosi 5. 15. in electionibus & aliâs se opponunt Dominicanis Ib. eorum machinationes contrà S. Clementem Card. Dominicanum in Concl. VII 5. 17. magna ubique authoritas Ib. calumniæ contrà S. Clementem 18. de Sixto V. & odium erga eundem 7. 67. erga Innocentium XI 1. 7. 17 potentioribus adulantur Ib. eorum Theologia moralis ab Innocentio XI. damnata Ib. Generalis gubernat mundum VII. 5. 21.
units.tr: Jesuits, evil persuaders, VII. 7. 68. Vipers, Ib. The Jesuits also rule the Pope, 5. 19. One pope, all popes; by the appearance of piety and learning they make instruments of ambition; their burden is intolerable, Ib. and 20. Jesuits are not easily elected, 21. They wish to seem to reject dignities, Ib. Castrators of authors, 3. 10. They need a confessor who is a pope, 7. 67. And the Dominicans, the leading religious orders in the papacy, 5. 15. In elections and elsewhere they oppose the Dominicans, Ib. Their machinations against St. Clement, the Dominican cardinal, in the Conclave, VII. 5. 17. Great authority everywhere, Ib. Slanders against St. Clement, 18. On Sixtus V and hatred toward him, 7. 67. Toward Innocent XI, 1. 7. 17. They flatter the more powerful, Ib. Their moral theology was condemned by Innocent XI, Ib. The General governs the world, VII. 5. 21.

units.la: cessionem Pontificum argumentorum.1. Pontificios contrà grave urget ex veritate historiæ illius præjudicium, partim intuitu qualitatum electæ & turpitudinis facti 4. partim intuitu incapacitatis ordinis §.6.7.8. veram esse historiam, probatur, non obstante primorum Scriptorum silentio, cujus causæ panduntur 9. quod tamen silentium incertum est ob Authorum corruptionem & interitum. Testimonia pro Johanna varia adducuntur antiquiora 23. Pontificum etiam, magnorum & Pontificibus sua dicantium virorum 23. Platinæ, Poetarum 24. quorum omnium testimoniis per aliquot secula nemo contradixit 25. argumentum ex Concilii Constantiensis in damnatione Hussi silentio 26. ex eo, quod occasio hinc nata Occamo Ecclesiam erroris redarguendi 27. ex Pontificiorum post Reformationem scribentium testimoniis 28. conclusiones ex testimoniis & argumentis adductis 29 argumentum ex imaginibus 30. statuis 31-36. Sella perforata 36-40. ex anfractuosis Pontificum ab illo tempore processionibus 40. 41 Objectiones solvuntur 42. seqq. ex nominis, numeri, temporis, in Pontificatu durationis, patriæ, diversa assignatione &c. 50. ex eo, quod Athenæ tunc non, & Romæ literæ bonæ contemptæ fuerint 51. ex statu gravidæ 52. à minùs verisimili, quòd gravida procedere voluerit 53. à Vaticano à Pontificibus tunc non inhabitato 54 à silentio Eccl. Rom. adversariorum 55. ex eo, quod Leo IX. talia Græcis exprobrare ausus sit 56. &c. gesta Johannæ 58. Origines quasi fabulæ assignatæ confutantur variæ 59. &c. conclusio de historiæ veritate 66.
units.tr: Concession of the Popes' arguments. 1. The Papists press against it a grave prejudice from the truth of that history, partly with regard to the qualities of the woman elected and the baseness of the deed 4; partly with regard to her incapacity for orders §. 6. 7. 8. That the history is true is proved, notwithstanding the silence of the earliest writers, whose causes are set out 9; yet that silence is uncertain because of the corruption and loss of the authors. Various older testimonies for Joan are adduced 23; also those of Popes and of great men who dedicated their works to Popes 23; Platina and the poets 24. By the testimonies of all of them no one contradicted for some centuries 25. Argument from the silence of the Council of Constance in condemning Hus 26; from the fact that the occasion arising from this allowed Ockham to refute the Church for error 27; from the testimonies of Papists writing after the Reformation 28. Conclusions from the testimonies and arguments adduced 29. Argument from images 30; from statues 31-36. The perforated chair 36-40. From the winding processions of the Popes from that time 40. 41. Objections are solved 42 seqq.: from the name, number, time, the length of the papacy, homeland, differing assignment, etc. 50; from the fact that Athens then did not, and in Rome good letters were despised 51; from the condition of pregnancy 52; from the less probable supposition that she wished to process while pregnant 53; from the Vatican not then being inhabited by Popes 54; from the silence of the adversaries of the Roman Church 55; from the fact that Leo IX dared to reproach the Greeks with such things 56; etc. The deeds of Joan 58. Various origins assigned, as if fables, are refuted 59 etc. Conclusion on the truth of the history 66.

units.la: Johannes XII. al. XIII, non est Johanna VII. 3 61. in schismate VII. 1 40 minorennis VII. 6. 4. Pseudo-Papa 1b. invasor VI. 4. 58. Alberici mancipium V. 28. indoctus VII. 8. 7. omnium scelleratissimus, venator, perjurus, libidinosus, concubinarius, fœminarum oppressor insatiabilis, Imperatoris, quia bona agebat, inimicus, ut Diabolus Dei. Templorum neglector, scelera manifeste patrans, Simoniacus, Spiritualis Patris occæcator, in amorem Diaboli vinum bibere, ejus auxilium in alea poscere solitus, miles, incestuosus, monstrum nulla virtute redemtum. in Synodo tamen piissimus, coangelicus, deponitur, digne perit VII 7. 21.
units.tr: John XII, al. XIII: is not Joan VII. 3 61. In schism VII 1 40. A minor VII. 6. 4. Pseudo-Pope, ibid. Usurper VI. 4. 58. Slave of Alberic V. 28. Unlearned VII. 8. 7. The most wicked of all: a hunter, perjurer, lustful, concubinary, insatiable oppressor of women; an enemy of the Emperor because he did good things; like the Devil to God. A neglecter of temples, manifestly committing crimes, simoniacal, blinding his spiritual father, accustomed to drink wine to the love of the Devil and to seek his help at dice; a soldier, incestuous, a monster redeemed by no virtue. Yet in the Synod most pious, a fellow angel; deposed, and rightly perishes VII. 7. 21.

units.la: Legati Pontificum à Latere I V. 2 53. sunt Legati avaritiæ Ib. definiuntur 54, cur non semper, vel diu maneant. Ib. inserviunt augendæ authoritati Pontificiæ cum subjectione Episcoporum, Conciliorum, & Regum Ib. Minus tamen ista in Gallia obtinuerunt Ib quomodo ibi ab initio & quàm parùm honorificè habiti Ib. quando multùm honorari coeperint. 55. Pontificum ars in deligendis gratissimis, non amplius Gallis in Gallia; Legatorum superbia & securus Caratsæ de Numine animus 56. Legatorum à facie appellatio 87. eorum prærogativæ Ib. Legatum in alio Regno Reges nolunt VI. 2. 27. 30.
units.tr: Legates a latere of the Pontiffs. IV. 2. 53. They are legates of greed. Ib. They are defined. 54. Why they do not always, or for long, remain. Ib. and 57. Why they do not wish to be called "des Ambassadeurs." Ib. What the words "a latere" mean, and whether there are others a latere; how they differ from nuncios. Ib. On what conditions they are received in France. Ib. They serve to increase papal authority, with the subjection of bishops, councils and kings. Ib. These things, however, obtained less in France. Ib. How they were held there at first, and how little honoured. Ib. When they began to be greatly honoured. 55. The Pontiffs' skill in choosing the most welcome men, no longer Frenchmen in France. The arrogance of the legates and Caraffa's carefree mind concerning the Divine Power. 56. The appellation of legates "a facie." 87. Their prerogatives. Ib. Kings are unwilling to have a legate in another kingdom. VI. 2. 27. 30.

units.tr: Leo X negotiates the papacy with Cardinal St. George. VI. 4. 38. What his coronation cost. VIII. 1. 47. What sort of man he was. VII. 7. 58. What kind of nepotism was his. VIII. 2. 14. He died, not without suspicion of poison. VI. 4. 57.

units.la: Leo XI. cito absumptus. VIII. 2. 9. & morte prævenus Nepotismum vocatum introducere haud potuit VIII. 2. 19.
units.tr: Leo XI, quickly taken off. VIII. 2. 9. Prevented by death, he could not introduce what is called nepotism. VIII. 2. 19.

units.la: Levita non fuerunt Cardinales I V. 2. 7.
units.tr: The Cardinals were not deacons (levitae). IV. 2. 7.

units.la: Liberalitas commendatur Papabilibus VI.
units.tr: Generosity is commended to Papabiles. VI.

units.la: Liberius P. in Schismate VII. 1. 4.
units.tr: Liberius, Pope, in the schism. VII. 1. 4.

units.la: Linus quotus à Petro VI. 1. 5. seqq.
units.tr: Linus, how many from Peter. VI. 1. 5. ff.

units.la: Litta Papabili obstant Hispani VI. 2. 29. 32.
units.tr: The Spaniards oppose Litta, a Papabile. VI. 2. 29. 32.

units.la: Longobardi vix Papabiles VII. 4. 13.
units.tr: The Lombards are scarcely Papabiles. VII. 4. 13.

units.la: Lotharius ad Schisma componendum VII. 1. 26. & statum Reipublicæ à Pontificibus corruptum corrigendum in Italiam mittitur VII. 7. 11. cujus decretum de electione per Clerum & populum IV. 1. 18.
units.tr: Lothair is sent into Italy to settle the schism and to correct the state of the republic, corrupted by the Pontiffs. VII. 1. 26. VII. 7. 11. His decree on election by clergy and people. IV. 1. 18.

units.la: Lucenses non sunt Papabiles VII 4. 19.
units.tr: The men of Lucca are not Papabiles. VII. 4. 19.

units.la: Ludovicus Imp. Pius vestes sericas coccineas Clericis decreto aufert IV. 2. 65.
units.tr: Louis the Pious, Emperor, by decree removes scarlet silk garments from clerics. IV. 2. 65.

units.la: Ludovicus XI. Galliæ Rex Bessarionem Pontificis Legatum parum honoratum remisit IV 2. 55.
units.tr: Louis XI, King of France, sent back Bessarion, the Pontiff's legate, poorly honoured. IV. 2. 55.

units.la: Ludovicus XII. destruere vult Babylonem VII. 7. 57.
units.tr: Louis XII wishes to destroy Babylon. VII. 7. 57.

units.la: Ludovici XIV. epistola ad Cardinales in Conclavi Alex. VII. VI. 2. 28. ad Legatum Chamontium de electione Innocentii X. VI. 1. 27.
units.tr: Letter of Louis XIV to the Cardinals in the Conclave of Alexander VII. VI. 2. 28. To the legate Chamont, on the election of Innocent X. VI. 1. 27.

units.la: Ludovisius & Borghesius in Concl. inimici vix se invicem salutant VI. 4. 60.
units.tr: Ludovisi and Borghese, enemies in the Conclave, scarcely greet each other. VI. 4. 60.

units.la: Lugdunensis Concilii pessimus fructus VII. 7. 36.
units.tr: The worst fruit of the Council of Lyons. VII. 7. 36.

units.la: Lugo Jesuitæ Card. se opponunt Dominicani in Conclavi Alex. VII. VII. 5. 15. seq.
units.tr: Lugo, a Jesuit, opposes Cardinal Dominicans in the Conclave of Alexander VII. VII. 5. 15. ff.

units.la: M.
units.tr: M.

units.la: Madruccium Card. ambit VI. 1. 25. nomine Regis Hispaniæ agit 2. 19 ab Hispanis adjutus VI. 2. 22. 21. unicè nominatus 24. 25. promissis non vult satisfacere VI. 4 3.
units.tr: Madruccio, Cardinal, canvasses. VI. 1. 25. Acts in the name of the King of Spain. 2. 19. Helped by the Spaniards. VI. 2. 22. 21. Named alone. 24. 25. Unwilling to satisfy promises. VI. 4. 3.

units.la: Magistratus jus in vocandis Ministris IV. 1. 34. magistratus alius, quàm quem præ se tulit privatus VIII. 2. 5. 6.
units.tr: The magistrate's right in calling ministers. IV. 1. 34. A magistrate other than the one a private person displayed. VIII. 2. 5. 6.

units.la: Maimburgius, judice Cœlest. Sfondrata, veritatem turpissimis factis fœdavit I. 7. 17. præmii amore scripsit; Pontifice urgente ex-Jesuita factus; indignè ejectionem tulit; 10000. libras reliquit; requiem nunquam habuit, forte damnatus; infesto calamo scripsit, neutri parti gratus 1b.-20. non veritati, sed Regi 20. injustè & mala fide Calvinum persecutus; argumenta à Reformatis mutuatus; compilator, cujus mala fides satis describi nequit 21. Industriâ peccavit 1b odio aut amore peccandi 1b. ejus mors subitanea 1b.
units.tr: Maimburg, in the judgment of Coelestinus Sfondrata, defiled the truth by most shameful acts. I. 7. 17. He wrote for love of reward; made an ex-Jesuit at the Pontiff's urging; bore his expulsion badly; left 10,000 pounds; never had rest, perhaps damned. He wrote with a hostile pen, pleasing neither side. Ib. 20. Not devoted to truth, but to the King. 20. He persecuted Calvin unjustly and in bad faith; borrowed his arguments from the Reformed; a compiler whose bad faith cannot be sufficiently described. 21. He sinned by diligence. Ib. From hatred or love of sinning. Ib. His sudden death. Ib.

units.la: Malatesta Carolus nomine Gregorii XIV. in Concilio Constantiensi abdicat VII. 1. 108.
units.tr: Carlo Malatesta, in the name of Gregory XIV, abdicates at the Council of Constance. VII. 1. 108.

units.la: Maldachinus minorennis, ineptus, nimio erga Olympiam amore ab Innocentio X. invitis Cardinalibus Cardinalis factus IV. 2. 69. 85.
units.tr: Maldachini, a minor, unfit, made Cardinal by Innocent X against the wishes of the Cardinals, from excessive love for Olympia. IV. 2. 69. 85.

units.la: Manasses Arelatensis pluralitatem beneficiorum suorum exemplo Petri excusat II. 53.
units.tr: Manasses of Arles excuses the plurality of his benefices by the example of Peter. II. 53.

units.la: Marcella ob cognitionem Theologicam judex delecta VII 3. 51.
units.tr: Marcella, chosen as judge on account of her theological learning. VII. 3. 51.

units.la: Marcellinus P. Idolis sacrificavit V. 32.
units.tr: Marcellinus, Pope, sacrificed to idols. V. 32.

units.la: Marcellus I. Cardinales instituisse dicitur IV. 2. 1.
units.tr: Marcellus I is said to have instituted Cardinals. IV. 2. 1.

units.la: Marcellus II. fraude promotus VI. 3. 57. nomen mutare VIII. 19. & pro more jurare 21. non vult; Nepotismum detestatur VIII. 2. 29. non videt, quomodo Pontifex salvari possit VIII. 2. 9.
units.tr: Marcellus II, promoted by fraud. VI. 3. 57. Changes his name. VIII. 19. And does not wish to swear according to custom. 21. He condemns nepotism. VIII. 2. 29. He does not see how the Pontiff can be saved. VIII. 2. 9.

units.la: Marcinus Imp. necessitate penuriaque præsente electus VI. 4. 71.
units.tr: Marcian, Emperor, chosen from present necessity and want. VI. 4. 71.

units.la: B. Maria Virginis imagines variæ I 6. 16. conceptio immaculata in monumento Alexandri VII. de pietà IV. 3. 14. maculatam à Pontifice decerni posse credunt Jesuitæ VII. 5. 18.
units.tr: Images of the Blessed Virgin Mary, various. I. 6. 16. The immaculate conception in the monument of Alexander VII, concerning piety. IV. 3. 14. The Jesuits believe that a maculate woman can be decreed by the Pontiff. VII. 5. 18.

units.la: Mariani Scoti de Johanna P. testimonium VII. 3. 17.
units.tr: Marianus Scotus's testimony about Pope Joan. VII. 3. 17.

units.la: Marozia Theodoræ filia, scortum Sergii Papæ, uxor Widonis, mater Johannis Papæ aliis etiam Pontificibus prostituta intrusit Pontifices V. 19. 30.
units.tr: Marozia, daughter of Theodora, a harlot of Pope Sergius, wife of Guy, mother of Pope John, also prostituted others, thrust Pontiffs in. V. 19. 30.

units.la: Marinus, sive Martinus II. vi intrusus V. 28.
units.tr: Marinus, or Martin II, intruded by violence. V. 28.

units.la: Martinus II. violentus erga Præde-cessorem malis artibus promotus VII. 7. 18.
units.tr: Martin II, violent towards his predecessor, advanced by wicked arts. VII. 7. 18.

units.la: Martinus IV. pessimus VII. 7. 38.
units.tr: Martin IV, most wicked. VII. 7. 38.

units.la: Martinus V. in Concilio Constantiensi peculiari ratione electus IV. 3. 87. VII. 1. 109.
units.tr: Martin V, elected at the Council of Constance in a peculiar manner. IV. 3. 87. VII. 1. 109.

units.la: Martinus Polonus de Johanna P. testatus VII. 3. 21.
units.tr: Martin of Poland testifies concerning Pope Joan. VII. 3. 21.

units.la: Matthæi Historici Regii in Gallia error Chronologicus respectu Silvestri P. IV. 2. 1.
units.tr: The chronological error of Matthew, the royal historian in Gaul, concerning Pope Silvester. IV. 2. 1.

units.la: Mathildis Ecclesiæ Romanæ addictissima VII. 1. 54.
units.tr: Matilda, most devoted to the Roman Church. VII. 1. 54.

units.la: Maximiliani I. de Julio II. & Pontificibus aliis testimonium VII. 7. 57. vult conjungere Papatum cum Imperio Ib.
units.tr: The testimony of Maximilian I concerning Julius II and other Popes. VII. 7. 57. He wants to join the Papacy with the Empire. Ib.

units.la: Medicai ex ambitione VI. 1. 34. vindictæ 39. contrariandi studio 40. & commodis propriis in Conclavibus agentes 31. 33. cùm debe- rent,ex Hispanorum mente, unicè Hispaniæ commoda spectare Ib.
units.tr: The Medici, out of ambition, VI. 1. 34; for revenge, 39; from a zeal for opposition, 40; and acting in conclaves for their own advantage, 31, 33; although, in the mind of the Spanish, they ought to regard only the advantages of Spain. Ib.

units.la: Medici Politici in Conclavi IV.3.39.
units.tr: The Medici politicians in conclave. IV. 3. 39.

units.la: Mela Card. in & post electionem Pauli II. pertinacia VI.4.61.
units.tr: Cardinal Mela, in and after the election of Paul II: obstinacy. VI. 4. 61.

units.la: Mendacium Conclaviarium VI. 4. 3. seq.9. 3. 56.
units.tr: Conclave lies. VI. 4. 3 seq.; 9. 3. 56.

units.la: Methodius Patr. Constantinop. stupri reus arefacta genitalia ostendit VII. 1. 37.
units.tr: Methodius, Patriarch of Constantinople, accused of fornication, showed his withered genitals. VII. 1. 37.

units.la: Mezerai de electione per Clerum & populum testimonium IV, 1. 21.
units.tr: Mezeray's testimony on election by the clergy and people. IV. 1. 21.

units.la: Militares in Concl. termini VI.2.37.
units.tr: Soldiers in conclave, their limits. VI. 2. 37.

units.la: Mina in Concl. VI.4. 1. seq.
units.tr: Threats in conclave. VI. 4. 1 seq.

units.la: Ministri extraordinarii ordinis majores I.2. 10. ad Ecclesias plantandas missi quales IV. 1. 19. Ministrorum ætas VII. 6. 1. vocatio; Vide; Electio Reformatorum circa eam consuetudinem IV. 1.23. Ministerium quatenus appetere liceat,& non VI. 1.29. non ambiebant olim IV. 2. 78.
units.tr: Extraordinary ministers of the greater orders, sent to plant churches: what sort they were. IV. 1. 19. The age of ministers. VII. 6. 1. Calling; see Election. The reformed custom concerning it. IV. 1. 23. The ministry: whether it is lawful to seek it, and whether it is not. VI. 1. 29. Formerly they did not canvass. IV. 2. 78.

units.la: Miraculis suam potestatem confirmare debent Pontifices; quod tamen præstare non possunt I. 1. 6. miracula à Schismaticis in Papatu jactata VII. 1. 59.
units.tr: Popes ought to confirm their power by miracles, yet they cannot perform them. I. 1. 6. Miracles boasted of by schismatics in the Papacy. VII. 1. 59.

units.la: Modena Duci,qui in Conel.Alex.VII. grati, ideò Hispanis exosi fuerunt VI. 2. 28.
units.tr: Modena, the duke, who was pleasing in the conclave of Alexander VII, and therefore was hated by the Spanish. VI. 2. 28.

units.la: Molitiones artificiosas in Conclavibus vide VI. 2. 39. &c.
units.tr: Artful schemes in conclaves: see VI. 2. 39 etc.

units.la: Monachi vix Papabiles VII. 5.14. superbi seq. invidi,odio flagrantes Ib. 21.
units.tr: Monks are scarcely papable. VII. 5. 14. Proud, then envious, burning with hatred. Ib. 21.

units.la: Mondovium Card. ab Hispanis sine causa exclusus VI. 2. 22.
units.tr: Cardinal Mondovi, excluded by the Spanish without cause. VI. 2. 22.

units.la: Monopoli Card. non sine resistentia & lacrymis ad votum Baronio dandum adigitur VI. 1. 37.
units.tr: Cardinal Monopoli is compelled, not without resistance and tears, to give his vote to Baronius. VI. 1. 37.

units.la: Montaltius Card. Nepos commodum & honorem suum spectat VI. 1. 34. pluribus terrenis respectibus simul agitur 30. Hispanis semel fortiter oppositit 2. 13. quòd porrò facere ob terrenos respectus neglexit 25. à Cœna ad electionem surgere noluit 4. 16.
units.tr: Cardinal Montalto, the nephew, looks to his own profit and honour. VI. 1. 34. He is driven by several earthly considerations at once, 30. He once strongly opposed the Spanish, 2. 13. That he neglected to do this on account of earthly considerations, 25. He was unwilling to rise from supper to the election, 4. 16.

units.la: Montanus Card. Legatus in Concilio Tridentt. denon-Residentia conqueritur, II. 54.
units.tr: Montano, cardinal legate at the Council of Trent, complains of non-residence. II. 54.

units.la: Montepulciani in Concl. Pii V. Calumniis impeditus VI. 4. 11.
units.tr: Montepulciano in the conclave of Pius V, hindered by calumnies. VI. 4. 11.

units.la: Montium pietatis inventor Paulus II. VII. 7. 53.
units.tr: Paul II, inventor of the Monti di Pietà. VII. 7. 53.

units.la: Moronis Card. affectata civilitas VI. 47. vindicta in Papatu timetur VIII. 1. 6.
units.tr: Cardinal Moroni: affected courtesy. VI. 47. Revenge is feared in the Papacy. VIII. 1. 6.

units.la: Mores corrupti fidem etiam corrumpunt. VII. 7. 90 mores Pontificum in pejores mutantur, vide Pontifices.
units.tr: Corrupt morals also corrupt faith. VII. 7. 90. The morals of Popes change for the worse; see Popes.

units.la: Moses & Aaron non favent exemplo suo relationi Petri & Pauli apud Pontificios I. 6. 41. Moisis exemplum an non probat electionem per præde cessores. V. 1 11.
units.tr: Moses and Aaron do not, by their example, support the account of Peter and Paul among the Papists. I. 6. 41. Does the example of Moses not prove election by predecessors? V. 1. 11.

units.la: Munera non tantum argentea dantur VI. 4. 19
units.tr: Gifts are not given only in silver. VI. 4. 19.

units.la: Munera, in quibus nævos suos prodere possent, Papabiles vitare jubentur VI. 3. 3.
units.tr: Gifts in which they could betray their blemishes: papable men are ordered to avoid them. VI. 3. 3.

units.la: Musca numerosæ in insignibus Urbani VIII. VIII. 2. 21.
units.tr: The fly, numerous, in the arms of Urban VIII. VIII. 2. 21.

units.la: Mysterium Tiaræ Pontificiæ olim inscriptum VIII. 1. 44.
units.tr: The mystery of the Papal tiara, formerly inscribed. VIII. 1. 44.

units.tr: N

units.la: Narbonensis Synodus purpuram decreto Clericis aufert IV. 2. 65.
units.tr: The Synod of Narbonne takes the purple from clerics by decree. IV. 2. 65.

units.la: Nationum in electionibus Pontificum respectus vitiosus VII 4. 1---28.
units.tr: The partiality of nations in the elections of Popes, a faulty consideration. VII. 4. 1–28.

units.la: Neapolitani non sunt Papabiles VII. 4 14. Turcis quàm Barberinis servire malunt VIII. 2. 22.
units.tr: Neapolitans are not papable. VII. 4. 14. They prefer to serve the Turks rather than the Barberini. VIII. 2. 22.

units.la: Negotiationes in Concl Vide; Molitiones.
units.tr: Negotiations in conclave: see Schemes.

units.la: Nepotismus Seculo X. demum notabiliter introductus VIII. 2. 25. exemplis illustratur 10. seq. à multis seculis paucissimi eo carere voluerunt,brevioris fere vitæ 25 seq.causæ hodiernæ quorundam abstinentiæ Ib. Nepotum quanta sit potestas 31.qui tamen minus apti,aliquando plane inepti sunt 32. auri cupidissimi 33. multum sibi ipsis nocent 34. eorum desperata salus Ib. tractatio cum Nepotibus negotia procrastinat Ib. Pontificibus sunt damnationis causa Ib. quantum Ecclesiæ noceant 35. Nepotum Cardinales sunt mancipia IV. 2. 41. quomodo tractent Episcopos 28. faciunt Cardinales,cósque indignos 87--91. quot sunt,tot sunt Pontifices VIII. 2. 13.22. perdunt,& tamen benefactorum gloriam accipiunt IV. 2.
units.tr: Nepotism was only notably introduced in the tenth century. VIII. 2. 25. It is illustrated by examples, 10 seq. For many centuries very few wished to be without it; the causes of the present abstinence of some are shorter lives, 25 seq. The present causes of some men's abstinence, Ib. How great is the power of nephews, 31. Those who are less suitable, and sometimes plainly unfit, 32. Most greedy for gold, 33. They greatly harm themselves, 34. Their salvation is desperate, Ib. Negotiation with nephews delays business, Ib. They are a cause of damnation for Popes, Ib. How much they harm the Church, 35. Nephews make cardinals who are mere slaves, IV. 2. 41. How they treat bishops, 28. They make cardinals, and these unworthy, 87–91. As many as there are, so many are the Popes, VIII. 2. 13, 22. They ruin, and yet receive the glory of their benefactors, IV. 2.

units.la: 40. Nepotum in Clonclavibus respectus habetur, iique saepe impedimento sunt Papabilibus VIII. 2. 37. VI. 2. 33. 54. Nepotum gloria brevis VIII. 2. 36. puniuntur Ib. & IV. 3. 8. IV. 3. 9. opus habent locis refugii mortuo Pontifice Ib. Nepotismus Urbani VI. VII. 1. 97. Clementis VIII. VIII. 2. 35. Nepotum Factiones in Conclavibus VII. 2. 10. quando ortae Ib. potentissimae sunt Ib. Nepotum scopus Ib. & VI. 3. 14 non nisi creaturam bene cognitam propnere jubentur 48. Nepotes succedentes 2. 16. cum iis non debent nimiam amicitiam contrahere Papabiles VI. 3. 5. vitium in Nepotismo propius notatur VIII. 2. 38.
units.tr: 40. Regard for nephews is had in conclaves, and they are often an impediment to papable men, VIII. 2. 37; VI. 2. 33, 54. The glory of nephews is brief, VIII. 2. 36. They are punished, Ib.; IV. 3. 8; IV. 3. 9. They need places of refuge when the Pope dies, Ib. The nepotism of Urban VI; VII. 1. 97. Of Clement VIII, VIII. 2. 35. Factions of nephews in conclaves, VII. 2. 10. When they arose, Ib. They are most powerful, Ib. The aim of nephews, Ib.; and VI. 3. 14. Papable men are ordered to propose only a creature well known, 48. Succeeding nephews, 2. 16. Papable men ought not to form too close a friendship with them, VI. 3. 5. The fault in nepotism is more closely noted, VIII. 2. 38.

units.la: Nestor in Concl. VI. 2. 37.
units.tr: Nestor in conclave. VI. 2. 37.

units.la: Neutralistarum Factiones VI. 2. 35. 36. Vide etiam Squadronistas; se habere caput & pedes, respondent 2. commodum proprium sequuntur 1. 32.
units.tr: Factions of the neutralists. VI. 2. 35, 36. See also the Squadronists; they reply that they have a head and feet. They follow their own advantage. 1. 32.

units.la: Neutrales in Schismate VII. 1. 118.
units.tr: Neutrals in the Schism. VII. 1. 118.

units.la: Neutralista in Religione nulli esse possunt I. 7. 20.
units.tr: Neutralists cannot be anyone in religion. I. 7. 20.

units.la: Niceni I. Conc. de electione per Clerum & populum IV. 1. 20. Monarchiae Romanae contrarium III. 42 decreta; Canon a Romanis jam olim suppositus III. 43.
units.tr: The Council of Nicaea I on election by the clergy and people. IV. 1. 20. Decreed contrary to Roman monarchy. III. 42. A canon long ago falsely put forward by the Romans. III. 43.

units.la: Nicolaus I. Genebrardo Sanctus, qualis Episcopis Germaniae VII. 7. 13.
units.tr: Nicholas I, called holy by Genebrard; what sort he was towards the bishops of Germany. VII. 7. 13.

units.la: Nicolaus II. in Schismate ab Imperatore datus VII. 1. 51. ejus de electione per Imperatores IV. 1. 32. per Clerum & populum decreta 33. de male electis judicium VII. 8. 18.
units.tr: Nicholas II, given by the Emperor in the Schism. VII. 1. 51. His decree on election by the emperors, IV. 1. 32; by the clergy and people, 33. His judgement on the badly elected. VII. 8. 18.

units.la: Nicolaus III. injustus VII. 7. 37. Nepotismi pessimi author VIII. 2. 10.
units.tr: Nicholas III, unjust. VII. 7. 37. Author of the worst nepotism. VIII. 2. 10.

units.la: Nicolaus V. in Schismate VII. 1. 80. non ambiens electus dicitur VI. 1. 23, ejus gesta in Cardinalatu VII. 1 118.
units.tr: Nicholas V, in the Schism. VII. 1. 80. He is said to have been elected without canvassing. VI. 1. 23. His deeds as cardinal. VII. 1. 118.

units.la: Nobiliores vix Papabiles VII. 4. 25. 27.
units.tr: Nobles are scarcely papable. VII. 4. 25, 27.

units.la: Non-Residentia II. 54.
units.tr: Non-residence. II. 54.

units.la: Nomina eadem quomodo Deo & hominibus tribuantur I. 3. 10
units.tr: How the same names are attributed to God and to men. I. 3. 10.

units.la: Nominibus mutatis interdum homines appellantur II. 12.
units.tr: Men are sometimes called by changed names. II. 12.

units.la: Nominum mutatio in Pontificibus Romanis; ejus origo VIII. 1. 17. annotationes ad ea, quae in investigatione originis reperta fuerunt 18. nullus. Petrus Ib, consuetudo Regum Babyloniae eadem Ib, quidam mutare nomen runt IV. 3. 82. VIII. 1. 19. quod in sequiorem partem acceptum Ib. quaenam in mutatione respici soleant 20. aliquando repudiata adoptata, aliquando a Cardinalibus imposita, Ib. non respondent egregiis nominibus 21. mutantur Ib.
units.tr: Change of name among the Roman Popes; its origin. VIII. 1. 17. Notes on those things which were found in investigating the origin, 18. None (Peter), Ib. The custom of the kings of Babylon, the same, Ib. Some changed their names, IV. 3. 82; VIII. 1. 19, which was taken in a worse sense, Ib. What is usually considered in a change, 20. Sometimes names were rejected, sometimes adopted, sometimes imposed by cardinals, Ib. They do not correspond to distinguished names, 21. Changed, Ib.

units.la: Novatianus P. in Schismate VII. 1. 3.
units.tr: Novatian, Pope, in the Schism. VII. 1. 3.

units.la: Numerus XXV. in Ecclesia Rom. mysticus II. 38.
units.tr: The number 25 is mystical in the Roman Church. II. 38.

units.la: O.
units.tr: O.

units.la: Occasiones in Concl. captandae VI. 3. 18. 29. 60.
units.tr: Occasions in conclave to be seized. VI. 3. 18, 29, 60.

units.la: Odium electionis principium VI. 1. 38.
units.tr: Hatred, the beginning of an election. VI. 1. 38.

units.la: Odoacer Rex se immiscet electionibus Pontificum IV. 1. 31.
units.tr: Odoacer the king meddles in the elections of Popes. IV. 1. 31.

units.la: D. Olympia vita compendiose tradita VII. 7. 70. Innocentium X. futurum simulare docuit VI. 4. 7. Domina Papae, Papissa fuit, & melior Cognatismo ipsius pessimus Barberinorum Nepotismus VIII. 2. 23. 31. ei adscripta omnia mala sub Innoc. X. patrata V. 31. haeres odii ipsius etiam Ib. de omnibus male locuta, spurcissimis etiam verbis adhibitis Ib. ejus partes in electione Pontificis. Ib. S. Clementem invidia erga Principem Rossanensem noluit Ib. contra Innocentio XI. promotionis ad Cardinalatum author extitit donis invocata Ib.
units.tr: Lady Olympia, her life briefly related. VII. 7. 70. She taught Innocent X to feign the future. She was the Lady of the Pope, and was a Papess; worse than her kinship, the Barberini nepotism was the worst. VIII. 2. 23, 31. All the evils done under Innocent X are ascribed to her. V. 31. She was also the heir of his hatred, Ib. She spoke ill of everyone, even with the filthiest words, Ib. Her part in the election of a Pope, Ib. She refused to favour St Clement out of envy towards the prince of Rossano, Ib. She was the author of the promotion to the cardinalate of one who was against Innocent XI, invoked by gifts, Ib.

units.la: Omina in electionibus Pontificum, & de illis judicium VII. 2. 4. seqq.
units.tr: Omens in papal elections, and judgments on them: VII. 2. 4. seqq.

units.la: Cnuphrius de appellatione Cardinalium refutatus IV. 2. 3.
units.tr: Cnuphrius on the appeal of Cardinals, refuted: IV. 2. 3.

units.la: E. poni debuit ad dextram; argumentatio Bellarmini I. 6. 52. ejus dignitas extraordinaria non relinquit Petri Monarchiam integram I. 6. 40. praerogativae ex Scriptura a Patribus explicatae 17. elogia ex Patribus Ib. 18. elogia in comparatione cum aliis Ib. 20. cum Petro Ib. 21. est per antonomasiam Apostolus 21. quod Monarchiae Petri contrariari ostenditur Ib. 23. ad dextram collocatur in diplomatibus Pontificum 24. seqq.
units.tr: E. ought to have been placed on the right hand; Bellarmine's argument: I. 6. 52. His extraordinary dignity does not leave Peter's monarchy intact: I. 6. 40. Prerogatives from Scripture as explained by the Fathers: 17. Praises from the Fathers: Ib. 18. Praises in comparison with others: Ib. 20. With Peter: Ib. 21. He is the Apostle by antonomasia: 21. That this is shown to be contrary to Peter's monarchy: Ib. 23. He is placed at the right hand in papal diplomas: 24. seqq.

units.la: Montium pietatis author Ib. Virtutis & litterarum inimicus has dissuadet Romanis VII. 8. 9. Magistratibus iniquus, investibus luxuriosis splendidus, superbus facie fucata IV. 2. Cybelem turritam referens VIII. 1. 43. lege vetuit, ut non nisi ex Cardinalibus legerentur Pontifices VII. 5. 9. quo praetextu, quo jure Ib. 10. 15. ejus de absoluta sua potestate jactantia IV. 2. 38.
units.tr: Founder of the Monti di Pietà: Ib. An enemy of virtue and learning, he dissuades the Romans from them: VII. 8. 9. Unjust to magistrates, splendid in luxurious vestments, proud with a painted face: IV. 2. Depicted as Cybele crowned with towers: VIII. 1. 43. By law he forbade that popes be chosen except from among the Cardinals: VII. 5. 9. By what pretext and what right: Ib. 10. 15. His boasting of his absolute power: IV. 2. 38.

units.la: Paulus III. quam indigno pretio Cardinalis factus sit IV. 2. 85. Papatum ambit VI. 1. 24. arte se insinuandi circa Concilia quoque adhibita Ib. de successione sua quid judicarit III. 9. qualis fuerit VII. 7. 62. Magiae reus V. 33. units.tr: Paul III. At what unworthy price he became Cardinal: IV. 2. 85. He ambitions the Papacy: VI. 1. 24. The art of insinuating himself, also employed with regard to Councils: Ib. What he judged about his succession: III. 9. What sort he was: VII. 7. 62. Accused of magic: V. 33. He introduced an unsuitable nepotism: VIII. 2. 14. He created minor Cardinals: IV. 2. 83. After his death he was less approved: IV. 3. 7.

units.la: Paulus IV. a pertinacibus & frustra timentibus praeter voluntatem eorum electus IV. 3. 45. 46. erga Moronem Card. ingratus VI. 3. 55. quam indigne Cardinales tractarit IV. 2. 40. primus iis suffragandi jus in creationibus Cardinalium infregit 69. multa antecessorum sustulit VIII. 2. 39. mortis & veneni metu non nisi ciborum reliquias assumsit VIII. 2. 9. ejus dictum: Uxorem non habentes, saepe verberant VIII. 2. 6. qualis fuerit pluribus VII. 7. 64. ejus Nepotismus VIII. 2. 15. mors commune gaudium IV. 3. 6. statua ignominiose habita 7. Schola a principiis Hispaniae aliena VI. 2. 31.
units.tr: Paul IV, elected against the wishes of the obstinate and needlessly fearful: IV. 3. 45. 46. Ungrateful towards Cardinal Morone: VI. 3. 55. How unworthily he treated the Cardinals: IV. 2. 40. He first broke their right to vote in the creation of Cardinals: 69. He abolished many of his predecessors' measures: VIII. 2. 39. From fear of death and poison he took only the leftovers of food: VIII. 2. 9. His saying: those who have no wives often beat them: VIII. 2. 6. What sort he was, according to many: VII. 7. 64. His nepotism: VIII. 2. 15. His death a common joy: IV. 3. 6. A statue set up in ignominy: 7. A school alien to the principles of Spain: VI. 2. 31.

units.la: Paulus V. Gallis addictus Hispanorum tamen admittit largitionem annuam VII. 2. 19. gaudet de obtinendo Papatu VI. 1. 26. qualis fuerit VII. 7. 68 ejus Nepotismus absolutam potestatem habens, immensas divitias sibi, nec obelum quidem Ecclesiæ, corradens VIII. 2. 20. ejus verba ad Nepotem de male ab eo coeptorum gloria, si bene ab aliis finiantur, ei tribuenda IV. 2. 40. creator minorennium Card 83.
units.tr: Paul V. Devoted to the French, yet he admits the annual Spanish bounty: VII. 2. 19. Rejoices at obtaining the Papacy: VI. 1. 26. What sort he was: VII. 7. 68. His nepotism: having absolute power, he heaped up immense riches for himself, and not even an obol for the Church: VIII. 2. 20. His words to a nephew, that the glory of things begun badly by him is to be ascribed to him if others finish them well: IV. 2. 40. Creator of minor Cardinals: 83.
