I. 1. 8. 9. confessionem communi nomine edidit I. 4. 6. 7. à Nepotismo alienus fuit VIII. 2. 25. cum Romæ non fuisse, probatur ex Scripturarum silentio II. 23. infertur, non esse de fide præsentiam, & quæ inde consequi dicantur 24. testimonia adesse debe rent ob rei dignitatem, ex hypothesi 25. in rei veritate 26. ob occasionum varietatem 27. 28 29. probatur ex iis, quæ in Scripturis contrà illam præsentiam occurrunt 30. seq. ex silentio authorum profanorum 33. objiciunt Patrum consensum 34. qui tamen neque Pontificiis sufficit 36. multa in relationibus contrariantur Pontificiorum hypothesibus 36. multa in iis incerta, contraria 37. etiam tempus adventus 1b. commorationis 38. Si Romæ fuisset, illud non sufficeret II. 2. Romæ fuisse, ex Scriptura probari debet 3. ante eum, si Romam venisset, Christiani ibi fuerunt II. 17 seqq. de Petri morte contraria Authorum testimonia 39. ejus Romæ reliquiæ 1b. de ejus præsentia dubitârunt, eam negârunt Pontificii quidam 1b. ex præsentia & commoratione nihil sequitur 1b. 40. nihil etiam ex morte 41. ejus partes Romæ non fuissent Episcopales 44. ejus Episcopatus rationis & Scripturæ fundamentis destituitur; Respondetur ad rationes Bellarmini 45. 46. urgetur Scripturæ silentium atque ex Bellarmino illustratur 47. Episcopatus minus cum quibusdam Antiquorum narrationibus convenit 48. sic etiam Petrum Episcopum facientes eum ignominiâ afficiunt 49 ei fœdifragium tribuunt 50 eum authorem abusuum Ecclesiasticorum faciunt, translationis ab uno loco ad alium 51. pluralitatis Beneficiorum 52. 53 non-Residentiæ 54. ei sic dimidium saltem Episcopatum tribuunt 55. Petrus communicare non potuit, quæ nunquam habuit I. 7. 22. II. 1. ei non in omnibus iis, quæ habuit, succeditur III. 19. 24. de ejus Successore contraria VI. 1. 5. seqq. Petri processiones Pontificum processionibus VIII. 1. 48. Petrus sic dictus in Constitutionibus Apostolicis de electione per Clerum & populum testatur IV. 1. 20.
units.tr: Peter the Apostle, chosen by Christ: IV. 1. 6. 7. 12. His Conclave, what sort it was: II. 56. Whether he was called first, whether he was the greatest in age, and whether he loved more: I. 6 3. Whether and how he is the Rock: I. 3. 7. This appellation does not prove a monarchy: 8. Nor does the praise "Prince of the Apostles" prove it: I. 6. 5. Scripture in no way proves it: I. 5. 4. He was not such a pope as Roman popes want to be: I. 2. 1 seqq. Not even according to the mind of the Gallican Church: I. 7. 1. seqq. He did not exercise a monarchy: I. 5. 37. He did not feed as popes feed: 15. seqq. He had no temporal power: 21. seqq. He was the Apostle of the Jews: II. 50. 51. Whether John 21 specially appointed him so: I. 5. 29 seq. Whether the Apostles were extraordinary, while he was ordinary: I. 2. 10. What primacy he had: I. 6.-1. seqq. How greatly the Papists boast of him, and why: I. 1. 8. 9. He published the confession in the common name: I. 4. 6. 7. He was free from nepotism: VIII. 2. 25. That he was not at Rome is proved from the silence of Scripture: II. 23. It is inferred that his presence is not a matter of faith, and what consequences are said to follow from it: 24. Testimonies ought to be present because of the dignity of the matter, on the hypothesis: 25. In the truth of the matter: 26. Because of the variety of occasions: 27. 28. 29. It is proved from those things in Scripture which stand against that presence: 30. seq. From the silence of profane authors: 33. They object the consensus of the Fathers: 34. Which nevertheless does not suffice even for the Papists: 36. Many things in the accounts contradict the Papist hypotheses: 36. Many things in them are uncertain and contrary: 37. Also the time of his arrival: Ib. Of his sojourn: 38. If he had been at Rome, that would not suffice: II. 2. That he was at Rome must be proved from Scripture: 3. Before him, if he had come to Rome, there were Christians there: II. 17 seqq. Contrary testimonies of authors about Peter's death: 39. His relics at Rome: Ib. Some Papists doubted his presence and denied it: Ib. Nothing follows from presence and sojourn: Ib. 40. Nothing follows from his death either: 41. His functions at Rome were not episcopal: 44. His episcopate lacks the foundations of reason and Scripture; answer to Bellarmine's arguments: 45. 46. The silence of Scripture is pressed and illustrated from Bellarmine: 47. The episcopate agrees less with some ancient accounts: 48. Thus those who make Peter a bishop also bring disgrace upon him: 49. They attribute a breach of faith to him: 50. They make him the author of ecclesiastical abuses, such as transfer from one place to another: 51. Of plurality of benefices: 52. 53. Of non-residence: 54. Thus they attribute to him at least half an episcopate: 55. Peter could not communicate what he never had: I. 7. 22. II. 1. He is not succeeded in all those things which he had: III. 19. 24. Contrary things about his successor: VI. 1. 5. seqq. Peter's processions compared with the processions of the popes: VIII. 1. 48. Peter, so called in the Apostolic Constitutions, bears witness to election by clergy and people: IV. 1. 20.

He introduced a worse practice: he wished to decree that a Pope could not choose his own successor IV. 1. 11.

units.la: Pius V. qualis fuerit VII. 7. 66. quodnam bonitatis genus habuerit 79. alia in Papatu credere coepit VIII. 2. 8. à Pontificibus nihil sine timore accipi posse censuit 9. in declaratione contrà Elisabetham Reginam inconvenienter locutus est I, 2. 7. occlusionem oris

units.tr: The title Pontifex Maximus III. 2. It must be quite certain about him that he is the Vicar of Christ I. 1. 5. How he wishes to be the Vicar of Christ 3. They attribute to him greater things than Christ had and exercised on this earth 3. 4. units.tr: The qualities of Popes to be elected are unknown in Scripture VII. 2. 1, though the requirements for bishops, deacons and widows occur there 1. Those to be elected ought at least to be endowed with the common qualities, and that to a greater degree 9. The first Popes shone forth in these 10. From the beginning other things were not considered either 11. The first elections were excellent also in other respects 12. Men were elected unwillingly 13, 14. The Papists cannot boast of the goodness of the first Roman bishops 15. Today a man ought to be elected, although monsters and beasts were afterwards called not a few, and some also appeared after death 16. Physically and in terms of the bodily members, not wholly unfit for their functions, they ought to have feet and hearing 17. They ought not to be too weak, nor always entirely ill VII. 1. 83, 18, although they are loved even when not well in their minds VII. 6. 8. And although in this matter who proposes the candidate counts for much, yet other things are further required: they ought to be from the bosom of the Church, rarely absent, in turbulent times, always Spanish (VI. 2. 15), quiet, skilled at hiding lofty spirits, not severe, not manifestly avaricious, not too splendid, neutral, neither too pleasing nor too hateful to princes VII. 2. 19, 19. Of the male sex 3. 1, although the woman Joan was elected 2 seqq. Formerly they were taken from every people 4. 1, and regard for nations was rejected, but now for a long time it has held 3. 4, and Ultramontanes etc., etc., are excluded 23. Regard for certain families also holds 24, and in general it is harder to elect nobles 25, whereas a humble birth commends 26. VI. 2. 15. A restless disposition, mostly among the French, ibid. Popes were formerly mostly chosen from deacons 5. 1; in the course of time from elders, often also from laymen 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; VIII. 1. 31; from bishops VII. 5. 7; non-Cardinals also elected 8; now only those long since promoted to celibacy 12, 13, scarcely monks 14. Minors elected VII. 6. 2 seq., and how great the fault in the election of such ibid. seq. Today and for a long time only old men are elected VII. 6. 8 seq., which is useful on one side 27 and very harmful on the other 28. Annotation on advantages and disadvantages 29. they are sometimes generous towards writers, and why VII. 7. 75.; their life is written up in flattering terms, ib.; to write otherwise about them is dangerous, ib.; not a few are only there to mark the times of writing, according to Baronius V. 30.; according to Platina, no differently than how tyrants stand alongside kings, and so that opposites placed side by side shine out more VI. 4. 21.; unworthy to be counted VII. 7. 14. 15.; Aporacti 18. 20. 22.; the wicked are vainly excused by their small number 8.; nor does the sharing of merits, which they feign, help them 84.; nor do the wicked make the Roman Church more glorious by it 85.; nor can they be excused by the smallness of their blemishes 86.; nor are the other defences of Baronius good 87.; nor is the evil removed by saying that such men were badly elected 88.; which is also increased while they are not counted 89.; finally, from the fact that wicked morals corrupt faith 90.

units.la: Pontifices electi non fiunt infallibiles VIII. 2. 7. licet alia credere incipiant, sunt enim
units.tr: Popes once elected do not become infallible, VIII. 2. 7, although they begin to believe other things, for they become worse. 8.

VIII. 2. 39.
units.tr: On infallibility see also VII. 7. 58. Enthusiasm is attributed even to atheists, §. 22. It is not believed by the Jesuits, 18. It is easily refuted from nepotism, VIII. 2. 35, and from corruption of life, 7. 10. Their boasting is a sign of Babylon, VII. 7. 13. They disapprove and abolish the acts and decrees of their predecessors, 1. 30. 36. 7. 10. 12. 15. 18. 19. 20. VIII. 2. 39.

units.la: Pontifices sunt miseri VII. 7. 65 VIII. 2. 9. ex judicio P. IV. non possunt esse pingues Ib. venenum sollicite cavent & insidias, quibus expositi sunt Ib. non sunt satis divites Ib. curæ eorum anxiæ Ib. brevis vita Ib. in Seculo maximè X. quot in singulis Seculis, & unde vita brevior Ib. & VIII. 2. 9 Papatus solo odore morbum efficit IV 3. 40. mors violenta VIII. 2. 9. desperatio de salute Ib. corrumpuntur & damnantur ob Nepotes Ib. & 34. corum renunciatio & depositio IV. 3. 2. mors; Vide Sede vacante; Et ibidem mortis circumstantias; gaudio excipitur IV. 3. §. &c. funebria; Constitutio de iis 13. praxis 14. exequiæ Ib.
units.tr: Popes are wretched, VII. 7. 65; VIII. 2. 9. By the judgment of Pope IV they cannot be fat, ib. They anxiously guard against poison and the plots to which they are exposed, ib. They are not rich enough, ib. Their cares are anxious, ib. Their life is brief, ib., especially in this age, X. How many in each age, and whence a shorter life, ib., and VIII. 2. 9. Papacy produces disease by its very smell, IV. 3. 40. Violent death, VIII. 2. 9. Despair of salvation, ib. They are corrupted and damned on account of nephews, ib., and 34. Their renunciation and deposition, IV. 3. 2. Death; see Sede vacante; and in the same place the circumstances of death. It is received with joy, IV. 3. §. etc. Funeral rites; the constitution concerning them, 13. Practice, 14. Funeral rites, ib.

units.la: Pontifices adorantur VIII. 1. 4. quando §. maximè in electione & coronatione 6. huc etiam pertinet, quòd humeris portantur 7. quod specialiùs refutatur 12. adorationis præter alia signum est osculum pedum 8. qui primi acceperint; accipiunt ab ipsis etiam Imperatoribus; de Patriarcha Constantinopolitano lis in Concilio Florentino Ib. accipiunt ipsa Cadavera Ib. adorationem illam religiosam & Idololatricam esse probatur 9. exhibetur ab eo etiam, qui Christi personam gerit 9. exhibetur in quibusdam major Pontificibus honor, quàm ipsi Christo VIII. 1. 9. 45 Caput detegitur auditis eorum, non Dei, nominibus Ib. in ejus sanitatem à geniculis bibitur Ib. 49. Pontifex personatus VII. 1. 84. est Idolum VIII. 1. 9. & quicunque loco Papæ cultum accipit, etiam Schismaticus Ib. Pontificum familiæ cur non diu floreant VIII. 2. 36.
units.tr: Popes are adored, VIII. 1. 4, especially §. in election and coronation, 6. To this also belongs that they are carried on shoulders, 7, which is refuted more specifically at 12. Among other signs of adoration is the kissing of the feet, 8. Those who first received it; they receive it even from emperors themselves. On the Patriarch of Constantinople there was a dispute at the Council of Florence, ib. They receive it even from corpses, ib. That this adoration is religious and idolatrous is proved, 9. It is offered even to one who bears the person of Christ, 9. Among some, greater honour is shown to the Pontiffs than to Christ himself, VIII. 1. 9. 45. The head is uncovered at the hearing of their names, not God's, ib. Their health is drunk on bended knees, ib., 49. A Pope in disguise, VII. 1. 84, is an idol, VIII. 1. 9, and whoever receives worship in place of the Pope, even a schismatic, ib. Why the families of the Popes do not flourish for long, VIII. 2. 36.

units.tr: Princes do not wish to be deceived by others unless it is well known to them, VI. 2. 29. Princes are advised not to meddle in the elections of Popes, 2. 32. Romæ dignitas & Majestas promovit fastum & usurpationem Pontificum III. 44. Romæ Basilicæ V. præcipuæ IV 2. 12. in Romam versus Bernh. Morlinensis & Hild. Cenomanensis VII. 7. 33. units.tr: Rome: whence it is named. II. 10. Cabalistically IV. 2. 53. It is Babylon, VII. 1. 60; 7. 13. 33. In the Apocalypse II. 4 seq.; not 1 Pet. V. 13; 8 seq. The tables of Babylon are in Rome, VII. 5. 16. The dignity and majesty of Rome promoted the pride and usurpation of the popes, III. 44. The chief basilicas of Rome, IV. 2. 12. Turning towards Rome: Bernard of Morlaix and Hildebert of Le Mans, VII. 7. 33. The corrupt state of Rome, VII. 7. 76. Everything is for sale, 58. Neglect of good letters in the ninth century, VIII. 3. 51; as it pleased Philip of Burgundy, IV. 2. 106. Impiety reigns there, ibid. The whole state of the so-called Church is most wretched, VIII. 2. 35. Its desolation by Antichrist in the last days is believed by the Papists, III. 32.

units.la: Schismata Rom. Pontificum VII. 1. seqq. singulorumque vitia atque incertitudines Ib. seq. eorum causa luxus & divitiæ Pontificum 5. in Schismate Damasi & Ursicini in Basilica 1,7. interfecti Ib. Cædes etiam Cleri & S. Virginum in Schismate Laurentii & Symmachi 8. quod præ aliis ex Confessione Baronii dubium fuit ib. Vigilii, juxta eundem, priora omnia superavit 13. illud Gregorii VII. rursus priora omnia 59 mala qu nquagenarii illius 115. tres simul Pontifices, triceps bestia, juxta Baronium 49. 50. in Schismatibus prælia & gravia bella VII. 1. 54. 59.67.78. 93. de Schismatum numero observatio 122. Schismatum extenuator quidam refutatur 123. 124. vitia in genere notantur 126. 127. seq. cur ex tam longo tempore nulla 125. non sine culpa Ecclesiam Rom. relinquunt 46. 47.
units.tr: The schisms of the Roman popes, VII. 1 seqq., and the vices and uncertainties of each of them, ibid. seq.; their cause, luxury and the riches of the popes, 5. In the schism of Damasus and Ursinus in the basilica, 7; those killed, ibid. Also the slaughter of clergy and holy virgins in the schism of Laurence and Symmachus, 8; which, above the others, according to the confession of Baronius, was doubtful, ibid. Of Vigilius, according to the same, he surpassed all the earlier ones, 13. That of Gregory VII again surpassed all the earlier evils of that fifty-year period, 59; 115. Three popes at once, a three-headed beast, according to Baronius, 49, 50. In the schisms, battles and grave wars, VII. 1. 54, 59, 67, 78, 93. Observation on the number of schisms, 122. A certain minimiser of the schisms is refuted, 123, 124. Vices are noted in general, 126, 127 seq. Why, over so long a time, none, 125. Some left the Roman Church not without fault, 46, 47.

units.la: Scriptura S. debet testari de Pontificibus, si tales dari debent 1. 1. 6. de Scripturæ perspicuitate & perfectione sententia Pontificiorum 1. 1. 7. absurditas sententiæ illorum ib. Pontificiorum cum hac sua sententia Ib. Sententia Reformatorum Ib.
units.tr: Holy Scripture ought to testify about the popes, if such are to be given, 1. 1. 6. The opinion of the Papists on the perspicuity and perfection of Scripture, 1. 1. 7. The absurdity of their opinion, ibid. The Papists with this their opinion, ibid. The opinion of the Reformed, ibid.

units.la: Scriptura silentium de electionibus Pontificum, Vide titulum Electionis.
units.tr: Scripture's silence about papal elections: see the title Election.

units.la: Scriptorum corruptio & interitus VII. 3. 10. erga Scriptores liberalitas quo fine instituatur interdum VII 7. 75.
units.tr: The corruption and destruction of writings, VII. 3. 10. Liberality towards writers, and for what end it is sometimes instituted, VII. 7. 75.

units.la: per Scrutinium eliguntur Rom Pontifices; ubi primò antescrutinium IV. 3 48. 49. actus; Schedularum praeparatio 50. Schedularum figura ib. extractio scrutatorum 51. Schedularum scriptio 52 complicatio 53. obsignatio. 54. Scrutinium ipsum 55. ubi delatio schedulae, juramenti praestatio, positio schedulae in calice 56. quid resp-ctu infirmorum observari soleat 57. infirmarii 58 sch dularum permissio, numeratio 59 publicatio Scrutinii 60. schedularum in filum insertio, depositio seorsim 61. postscrutinium 62. Scrutinium secretum an valde obsit Capitum authoritati VI. 2.7. in Scrutinio fraus VI. 4. 17. Scrutinium primum initium praelii VI. 1. 57.
units.tr: Roman popes are chosen by scrutiny. Where, first, the pre-scrutiny act, IV. 3. 48, 49; the preparation of the ballots, 50; the shape of the ballots, ibid.; the extraction of the scrutineers, 51; the writing of the ballots, 52; their folding, 53; their sealing, 54. The scrutiny itself, 55: where the delivery of the ballot, the taking of the oath, and the placing of the ballot in the chalice occur, 56; what is usually observed with regard to the sick, 57; the infirmarians, 58; the handing out and counting of the ballots, 59; the publication of the scrutiny, 60; the threading of the ballots and their separate deposit, 61; the post-scrutiny, 62. Whether the secret scrutiny greatly harms the authority of the chapters, VI. 2. 7. Fraud in the scrutiny, VI. 4. 17. The first scrutiny is the beginning of the battle, VI. 1. 57.

units.la: Seculum IX; quale V. 1. 7. 11. quales in eo Pontifices & Principes ib. Seculum X. quale VII 3 18. 7 14 seq. & quales in eo Pontifices ib idem de Seculo XI. 13, XII. 31. XIII. 35. seq. XIV 41. XV. 51. XVI. 57. XVII. 64.
units.tr: Century IX; what it was like, V. 1. 7. 11. What Popes and Princes there were in it, ib. Century X: what it was like, VII 3 18. 7 14 seq., and what Popes there were in it, ib. The same for the eleventh century, 13; twelfth, 31; thirteenth, 35 seq.; fourteenth, 41; fifteenth, 51; sixteenth, 57; seventeenth, 64.

units.la: Sedes diu vacans; Vide Electionis dilationem. Sede vacante qualis Romae status IV. 3. 2. seq regimen Politicum, Ecclesiasticum quale 9. tumultus 12.
units.tr: Vacant see. See Postponement of the election. The state of Rome while the see is vacant, IV. 3. 2 seq.; the political and ecclesiastical government, how it is conducted, 9; tumults, 12.

units.la: Sella perforata de Johanna P. VII. 3. 36. seq. stercoraria VII 1 46.
units.tr: Chair with a hole: concerning Joan the Popess, VII. 3. 36 seq.; the stool-chair (stercoraria), VII 1 46.

units.la: Senectutis simulatores Papabiles VII. 4, 17. 20 &c.
units.tr: Feigners of old age, the papabiles, VII. 4, 17. 20 etc.

units.la: Senense Concilium Pontifici periculosum solvitur VII. 1. 113.
units.tr: The Council of Siena, dangerous to the Pope, is dissolved, VII. 1. 113.

units.la: Senes nonnisi decrepiti Pontifices eliguntur VII 6. 8. seq.
units.tr: Only decrepit old men are elected Popes, VII 6. 8 seq.

units.la: Sergius I. à Clero & Populo electus IV. 1. 18. confirmatus ab Imperatore 53.
units.tr: Sergius I, elected by the clergy and people, IV. 1. 18; confirmed by the Emperor, 53.

units.la: Sergius II. an primus nomen mutarit VIII. 1. 17.
units.tr: Sergius II: whether he was the first to change his name, VIII. 1. 17.

units.la: Sergius III, in Schismate VII. 1. 21. alio 28. non fuit author facinoris in cadavere Formosi patrati 29. in alio Schismate 34 35. judice Baronio illegitimus 36. invasor VI. 4. 58. an primus nomen mutarit VIII. 1. 17. noluit Petrus porro vocari ib turpis vitae V. 19. nefandus, omnium vitiorum servus VII. 7. 18. ejus malus ingressus, deterior progressus, pessimus egressus ib.
units.tr: Sergius III: in the schism, VII. 1. 21; elsewhere, 28; he was not the author of the crime committed on the corpse of Formosus, 29; in another schism, 34, 35; by Baronius' judgment illegitimate, 36; a usurper, VI. 4. 58; whether he was the first to change his name, VIII. 1. 17; he refused to be called Peter any longer, ib.; a shameful life, V. 19; wicked, a slave to every vice, VII. 7. 18; his bad entrance, worse progress and worst exit, ib.

units.la: S. Severina Card Papa certò praesumitur, VI. 2. 5. ab Hispanis & Legato summo studio adjutus 21 valde ambiens quoque 1. 26 & Papa Diaboli vocatus ib adoratus, electus, ejus etiam cella jam direpta. VIII. 1. 16. neque tamen obtinuit IV. 3. 81. VII. 1. 125. ob fraudem in numerandis adorantibus VI. 4. 17.
units.tr: Cardinal S. Severina was certainly presumed to be Pope, VI. 2. 5; he was helped with the greatest zeal by the Spaniards and the legate, 21; he was also very ambitious, 1. 26, and was called the Devil's Pope, ib.; he was adored and elected, and his cell had already been plundered, VIII. 1. 16. Yet he did not obtain the papacy, IV. 3. 81; VII. 1. 125; on account of a fraud in counting those who adored him, VI. 4. 17.

units.la: Sforza Card in Concl. inimicos habuit & expertus est VI. 1. 39. ejus de Papa futuro responsum VII. 7. 79. de divitiis Olympiae judicium.
units.tr: Cardinal Sforza had enemies in the conclave and found them out, VI. 1. 39; his answer about the future Pope, VII. 7. 79; his judgment on Olympia's riches.

units.la: Sigebertus Gemblacensis de Johanna P. testatur VII. 3. 19.
units.tr: Sigebert of Gembloux bears witness concerning Pope Joan, VII. 3. 19.

units.la: Silverius P. in Schismate VII. 10. 11. violenter electus, & Simoniace, reus fit, in exitium mittitur ejus ad Vigilium Anti-Papam epistola, cum Baronii epiphonemate ib.-15. vi sublatus VI. 4 57.
units.tr: Pope Silverius, in the schism, VII. 10. 11. He was elected by violence and by simony, becomes guilty and is sent into exile; his letter to the antipope Vigilius, with Baronius' epiphonema, ib.-15; removed by force, VI. 4. 57.

units.la: Silvester I, Cardinales instituisse dicitur IV. 1, 1.
units.tr: Silvester I: he is said to have instituted cardinals, IV. 1, 1.

units.la: Silvester II. Diaboli ope V. 32. Simoniace VI. 4. 22. ab Imperatore etiam IV 1. 32. malis, judice Baronio, artibus, & qualis electus VI. 4. 70. alia in Papatu credere incipit VIII. 2. 8. horrendum finem habuit V. 32.
units.tr: Silvester II: by the help of the Devil, V. 32; by simony, VI. 4. 22; also by the Emperor, IV. 1. 32; by evil arts, according to Baronius' judgment, and how he was elected, VI. 4. 70; he begins to believe other things about the papacy, VIII. 2. 8; he had a dreadful end, V. 32.

units.la: Silvester III, Simoniace VI. 4. 24. 26. in Schismate intrusus VII. 1. 48.
units.tr: Silvester III: by simony, VI. 4. 24, 26; intruded in the schism, VII. 1. 48.

units.la: Simonia quàm late se extendat VI. 4. 19. in electionibus Pontificum exemplis probata 20 &c. Simoniaca consilia VI. 2. 34. 3. 8. portò locum habuerunt VI. 1. 27. 28. 2. 15. VII. 1. 21. 53. 70. in Simoniacis electionibus quantum vitium VI 4. 40 de Simonia Bulla legitur VI. 4. 38. Simoniacae promissiones non semper servantur 40. Simoniaci quomodo excusari velint 41. nullam potestatem habent, nihil bene agunt, iis nulla obedientia debetur. VI. 4 56. VII. 1. 51. Vide etiam Nepotismum.
units.tr: How far simony extends, VI. 4. 19; proved by examples in papal elections, 20 etc. Simoniacal counsels, VI. 2. 34, 3. 8; they have had their place, VI. 1. 27, 28, 2. 15, VII. 1. 21, 53, 70. How great a vice is simony in elections, VI. 4. 40. A bull on simony is read, VI. 4. 38. Simoniacal promises are not always kept, 40. How simonists wish to excuse themselves, 41. They have no power, they accomplish nothing good, and no obedience is owed to them, VI. 4. 56; VII. 1. 51. See also Nepotism.

units.la: Simulatio in Conclavi VI 3. 52 58 4 5. seq. humanitatis 1. 13. humilitatis, & modestiae 3. 4. 12 virtutis in genere VII 7 1. commendatur, suadetur. Simulatio zeli VI. 3. 41. in propositione. Vide propositionem. Simulatio causa mutationis sequentis VIII. 2. 3.
units.tr: Simulation in the conclave, VI. 3. 52, 58; 4. 5 seq.; of humanity, 1. 13; of humility and modesty, 3. 4. 12; of virtue in general, VII. 7. 1. It is recommended and urged. Simulation of zeal, VI. 3. 41, in the proposal. See Proposal. Simulation as the cause of the change that follows, VIII. 2. 3.

units.la: Sirleto Card. obfuit nimis cito proponi VI 28. obfuit peritiae rerum mundanarum defectus VII, 8. 6.
units.tr: Cardinal Sirleto was harmed by being proposed too early, VI. 28; he was harmed by his lack of skill in worldly affairs, VII. 8. 6.

units.la: Sixtus IV. author confusionis ordinis Cardinalium impia fraus in praetextu solvendorum Eccles. debitorum ib. plane indignos Cardinales creavit V 2.84 spurium ib. meretricio tributo gaudet, Sodomiam permittit, luxuriosus, Concubinarius VII. 7. 54 literarum initnicus VII 8 9. pacis, unice suis promovendis intentus, moerore ex pacis nuntio accepto obiit, execratio omnium, ejus Epitaphium IV 3.7.
units.tr: Sixtus IV: the author of the confusion of the order of cardinals; an impious fraud under the pretext of paying the church's debts, ib.; he created entirely unworthy cardinals, V. 2. 84; a spurious one, ib.; he enjoyed the tribute of prostitutes, permitted sodomy, was lustful and kept concubines, VII. 7. 54; hostile to literature, VII. 8. 9; intent only on promoting peace and his own interests, he died of grief on receiving news of peace; the execration of all; his epitaph, IV. 3. 7.

units.la: Sixtus V mendaciis & simulationibus suis I. 6. 36. VI 4. 5. aliorum etiam 9. suo etiam ratione aetatis, quod aliud ab altera parte subsecutum est VI. 6 16.17 seq. promotus, id est, adoratus, ante scrutinium subsequens clamari curat: sine praejudicio; IV. 3. 81 non vult acceptare Papatum, quia jam acceptarit, & adhuc unum acceptare vellet VIII. 1 2 simulare desinit IV 3 82. metamorphosis ratione aetatis VII. 6. 25. cur Cardinalis adhuc vultum terram versus direxerit ib. quantum mutatus VIII. 2. 3. quantopere unicitatem Pontificis urserit I. 6 36 quam sollicite venenum evitare studuerit, gratias agit, quod semel sine timore cibum sumere potuerit VIII 2. 9. sine consensu Cardinalium Cardinales fecit IV 2.69 e us Nepotismus, & corrasae ad eo divitiae VIII 2.17. qualis ipse fuerit VII. 7. 7. ejus bonitas quadris 79 a Jesuitis & Hispanis commercium cum Diabolo, qui & eum de mala Daemonis fide querentem strangularit, habuisse dicitur V 14 a Bellarmino damnatis annumeratur VII 2 9.
units.tr: Sixtus V, by his lies and simulations, I. 6. 36; VI. 4. 5; those of others also, 9; also by his feigned age, which was followed by the other party, VI. 6. 16, 17 seq.; promoted, that is, adored; before the scrutiny he takes care to have it proclaimed afterwards: without prejudice, IV. 3. 81; he does not want to accept the papacy, because he has already accepted it, and still wishes to accept one, VIII. 1. 2; he ceases to pretend, IV. 3. 82; his metamorphosis on account of age, VII. 6. 25; why, as cardinal, he still directed his face towards the ground, ib.; how much he changed, VIII. 2. 3; how earnestly he pressed for the unity of the Pope, I. 6. 36; how carefully he tried to avoid poison; he gives thanks that once he could eat food without fear, VIII. 2. 9; he made cardinals without the consent of the cardinals, IV. 2. 69; his nepotism, and the riches gathered by it, VIII. 2. 17; what sort of man he was, VII. 7. 7; his goodness (quadris 79); by the Jesuits and Spaniards; he is said to have had dealings with the Devil, who also strangled him when he complained of the Devil's bad faith, V. 14; he is counted among those condemned by Bellarmine, VII. 2. 9.

units.la: Soto in Concilio Tridentino Residentiam Episcoporum ursit I. 54.
units.tr: Soto at the Council of Trent urged the residence of bishops, I. 54.

units.la: Spada Card solo Papatus odore aeger IV. 3. 40 Conclave egressus apud D. Olympiam tr. stasse dicitur V.
units.tr: Cardinal Spada, sick merely at the smell of the papacy, IV. 3. 40; he is said to have left the conclave and stayed with Donna Olympia, V.

units.la: Spiritus S. peculiari gratiosa assistentia electionem Pontificis Romani dirigere dicitur V. 11.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is said to direct the election of the Roman Pontiff by a special and gracious assistance, V. 11.

units.la: Squadronista quando orti & quales sint VI. 2. 35. impediunt lectionem epistolae quasi a Rege Poloniae missae 36. alio nomine Acephali dicti 6. nolunt hominem probum ibid. 40, 41. commodis suis inserviunt VI. 1. 33, ex vindictae
units.tr: Squadronists: when they arose and what sort they are, VI. 2. 35; they prevent the reading of a letter supposedly sent by the King of Poland, 36; otherwise called Acephali, 6; they do not want an honest man, ibid. 40, 41; they serve their own interests, VI. 1. 33; they act out of a desire for revenge...

units.la: Sixtus IV ... (ordering as printed; right column continues:) studio agunt 39. Gallica liberalitate devinctus ... Statua Rom. de Johanna P. testatur VII. 3. 3. 33. Senensis 34. 35
units.tr: Sixtus IV ... they act with zeal, 39; bound by Gallic generosity ... a Roman statue bears witness concerning Pope Joan, VII. 3. 3, 33; the Sienese, 34, 35.

units.la: Stephana Joh XII. concubina VII. 7. 21. in effusione concepti obit Ib.
units.tr: Stephana, John XII's concubine, VII. 7. 21; she died in giving birth to the child she had conceived, ib.

units.la: Stephani Wintonicnsis testimonium Pontificibus III. 49.
units.tr: The testimony of Stephen of Winchester to the Popes, III. 49.

units.la: Stephanus III. al. II. primus humeris portatus legitur VIII 1. 7.
units.tr: Stephen III (al. II): he is read to have been the first carried on men's shoulders, VIII. 1. 7.

units.la: Stephanus IV. al III, in Schismate electus VII 1. 43 decernit de Papa nonnisi ex Cardinalibus eligendo IV. 2. 11.
units.tr: Stephen IV (al. III), elected in the schism, VII. 1. 43; he decreed that the Pope should be chosen only from the cardinals, IV. 2. 11.

units.la: Stephanus V. al VI. Simoniace VI. 4. 21. electus ante Formosum, non patravit facinus in ejus cadavere VII. 1. 28.
units.tr: Stephen V (al. VI): simoniacal, VI. 4. 21; elected before Formosus; he did not commit the crime on his corpse, VII. 1. 28.

units.la: Stephanus VI. al. VII. intrusus ab intruso pulsus VI. 4. 48 quae in cadavere Formosi patrarit, & annon facinus fallibilitatem Pontificum probet; VII. 1. 29. 30. 31. 32. indignus, qui numeretur 33.
units.tr: Stephen VI (al. VII): intruded, and expelled by an intruder, VI. 4. 48; what he did to the corpse of Formosus, and whether the deed proves the fallibility of Popes, VII. 1. 29, 30, 31, 32; unworthy to be counted, 33.

units.la: Stephanus Clementem II. vi sustulit VI. 4. 57.
units.tr: Stephen removed Clement II by force, VI. 4. 57.

units.la: Stephanus IX. ab Imperatore electus IV 1. 32. de electione per Imperatores decernit 6.
units.tr: Stephen IX, elected by the Emperor, IV. 1. 32; he decrees about election by emperors, 6.

units.la: Stratagemata Conclaviaria VI. 2. 41. 4. 8.
units.tr: Conclave stratagems, VI. 2. 41; 4. 8.

units.la: Vide Conclave; Fraudes &c.
units.tr: See Conclave; Frauds etc.

units.la: Subdiaconi ordinatio VIII. 1. 32.
units.tr: The ordination of subdeacons, VIII. 1. 32.

units.la: Successionem Pontificum quantopere jactent V. 2 Vide Pontifices; localis sine successione officii & doctrinae non sufficit III. 49. seq. Sanctitatis quatenus requiratur VII. 7. 82.
units.tr: How much they boast of the succession of Popes, V. 2. See Popes. A local succession without succession of office and doctrine is not enough, III. 49 seq. To what extent holiness is required, VII. 7. 82.

units.la: S. Sujanna Card. in Concl. mendacibus Calumniis impetitus VI. 4. 10.
units.tr: Cardinal S. Sujanna, in the conclave, was attacked by lying calumnies, VI. 4. 10.

units.la: Symmachus P. in Schismate VII. 1 8. adulteri accusatus Ib. contra ambitum decernit in Synodo VI. 1. 29.
units.tr: Symmachus, Pope, during the schism (VII. 1 8.). Accused of adultery (Ib.). Decrees against bribery in a synod (VI. 1. 29.).

units.la: T.
units.tr: T.

units.la: Talus, Consistorii Regii Galliae Consiliarius & Advocatus in Senatu Parisiensi Generalis, quid in controversia de potestate Papae egerit I. 2. 4.
units.tr: Talus, General Advocate of the King's Council of Galicia and Advocate in the Parisian Senate: what he did in the controversy about the power of the Pope (I. 2. 4.).

units.la: Tertius in electionibus Pontificum, duobus litigantibus, gaudet VI. 3. 32. 4. 65. seq. VII. 4. 40. 41.
units.tr: Tertius: in papal elections, when two litigants contend, he rejoices (VI. 3. 32. 4. 65. seq. VII. 4. 40. 41.).

units.la: Theodato Rege iubente Silverius P. factus VII. 1. 10.
units.tr: Silverius was made Pope at the command of King Theodatus (VII. 1. 10.).

units.la: Theodora Augusta Vigilium impiis contrà Silverium P. molitionibus promovit V. 29. VII. 1. 11.
units.tr: Theodora Augusta promoted Vigilius, by impious schemes, against Silverius, Pope (V. 29. VII. 1. 11.).

units.la: Theodora scortum Monarchiam Romæ obtinens, Pontifices intrudens V 29. filia matri simillima ib & 30
units.tr: Theodora, a prostitute who held sway over Rome, thrusting Popes upon it (V. 29., a daughter most like her mother, ib. and 30.).

units.la: Theodoricus Rex in Schismate Symmachi & Laurentii iudex VII 8 illum confirmat. IV. 1. 31. Concilium Romanum VII. 1. 8. Felicem Pontificem facit IV. 1. 31.
units.tr: King Theodoric, judge in the schism of Symmachus and Laurentius, confirmed the former (VII. 8.). The Roman Council (VII. 1. 8.). He made Felix Pope (IV. 1. 31.).

units.la: Theodorus bis Anti-Papa VII 1. 20. 21.
units.tr: Theodorus, twice an anti-Pope (VII. 1. 20. 21.).

units.la: Theodorus P vestigia seditiosorum sequitur VII. 7. 16. à quibusdam non numeratur VII. 1. 2.
units.tr: Pope Theodorus follows the footsteps of seditious men (VII. 7. 16.). He is not counted by some (VII. 1. 2.).

units.la: Theologi Cardinalium IV. 2. 109.
units.tr: The theologians of the Cardinals (IV. 2. 109.).

units.la: Theologorum minor in Pontificiis promotionibus Ecclesiasticis ratio habetur VII. 8. 5. seq.
units.tr: Among the Papists, less regard is paid to theologians in ecclesiastical promotions (VII. 8. 5. seq.).

units.la: Theophylactus P. in Schismate VII. 1. 22.
units.tr: Theophylact, Pope, during the schism (VII. 1. 22.).

units.la: Thiota Prophetissa Moguntina VII. 3. 65.
units.tr: Thiota, the prophetess of Mainz (VII. 3. 65.).

units.la: Thomas Aquinas cur non Cardinalis, factus sit IV. 2. 93.
units.tr: Why Thomas Aquinas was not made a Cardinal (IV. 2. 93.).

units.la: Tituli Cardinalium Presbyterorum IV. 2. II. 12.
units.tr: The titles of the presbyter Cardinals (IV. 2. II. 12.).

units.la: Tosco Card. adoratus IV. 3. 81. sed, resistente Baronio VII. 7 6. non electus.
units.tr: Cardinal Tosco was adored (IV. 3. 81.), but, Baronius resisting, he was not elected (VII. 7. 6.).

units.la: Toto Dux Nepesinæ cum fratribus fratrem intrudit VII. 1. 23.
units.tr: Toto, Duke of Nepi, with his brothers, thrusts his brother in (VII. 1. 23.).

units.la: Traditiones incertæ I. 1. 6. non probant sufficienter potestatem Pontificum ib.
units.tr: Uncertain traditions (I. 1. 6.) do not sufficiently prove the power of the Popes (ib.).

units.la: Transitio ab una sede ad aliam vitiosa. II. 51.
units.tr: A transfer from one see to another is faulty (II. 51.).

units.la: Tridentinorum Patrum querelæ de Privilegiis Conclavistarum IV. 3. 27. iuribus Regiis & Gallicanæ Ecclesiæ libertatibus Concilium variè contrariatur IV. 2. 57.
units.tr: The complaints of the Tridentine Fathers about the privileges of the conclave-men (IV. 3. 27.). The Council is variously at odds with the royal rights and the liberties of the Gallican Church (IV. 2. 57.).

units.la: Turcarum prætextus fraudulentus Nepotum VIII. 2. 35.
units.tr: The fraudulent pretext of the Turks for nephews (VIII. 2. 35.).

units.la: Turrecremata argumentum ex speciali Petri alloquio refutatur I. 3. 13.
units.tr: Turrecremata's argument from the special address to Peter is refuted (I. 3. 13.).

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Valentinianus Imp. confirmat Damasum IV, 1. 31.
units.tr: Valentinian the Emperor confirms Damasus (IV. 1. 31.).

units.la: Valentinus P. pedum oscula admittit jam VIII. 1. 8.
units.tr: Pope Valentinus already admits kisses on his feet (VIII. 1. 8.).

units.la: Valentinus Dux, Nepos vendit Papatum Julio II. VI. 4. 37.
units.tr: Valentinus, Duke, nephew, sells the Papacy to Julius II (VI. 4. 37.).

units.la: Valeriano M. Capucino non est de fide, Pontificem esse successorem Petri III, 6. 7. 8.
units.tr: That the Pope is the successor of Peter is not a matter of faith, according to the Capuchin Valerianus (III. 6. 7. 8.).

units.la: Valerii Hipponensis Episcopi non Concionantis exemplum non favet Pontificibus I. 5. 17.
units.tr: The example of Valerius, Bishop of Hippo, who did not preach, does not favour the Popes (I. 5. 17.).

units.la: Valetudinarii fiunt Pontifices VII. 6. 8. seqq.
units.tr: Popes are made from invalids (VII. 6. 8. seqq.).

units.la: Vannocia Alexandri V. scortum VII. 7. 56.
units.tr: Vannozza, a prostitute of Alexander V. (VII. 7. 56.).

units.la: Velitationes in Conclavi VI 2 37.
units.tr: Skirmishes in the conclave (VI. 2. 37.).

units.la: Veneti non sunt Papabiles VII. 4. 15. Cardinales commoda Reipubl. in Conclavi promovent VI. 2. 35. Legatus primo se immiscet negocio electionis 31. Venetorum Patriciatus à Marcello II. pro cognatis unicè expetitus. VI. 1. 2. 29.
units.tr: The Venetians are not papabiles (VII. 4. 15.). Cardinals promote the advantages of the Republic in the conclave (VI. 2. 35.). The legate first meddles in the business of the election (31.). The Venetian patriciate was sought solely by Marcellus II for his relatives (VI. 1. 2. 29.).

units.la: Verbera in Conclavi VI. 2. 37.
units.tr: Blows in the conclave (VI. 2. 37.).

units.la: Vestes rubræ. Vide Cardinales, & IV. 1. 64. militares ib. mutantur à Pontifice electo VIII. 1. 13. priores cedunt Ceremoniarum Clericis VIII. 1. 15. Sacerdotales V T. non defendunt luxum Cleri Pontificii IV. 2. 65.
units.tr: Red robes. See Cardinals, and IV. 1. 64. Military dress (ib.) is changed by the Pope when elected (VIII. 1. 13.). The former give way to the clerks of ceremonies (VIII. 1. 15.). Priestly vestments do not defend the luxury of the Papist clergy (IV. 2. 65.).

units.la: Vicariatuum collatio fraudulenta Pontificum III. 47.
units.tr: The fraudulent conferring of vicariates by the Popes (III. 47.).

units.la: Victoris I. P. conatus alios subjugandi III. 36.
units.tr: Victor I, Pope: his attempts to subjugate others (III. 36.).

units.la: Victor II. ab Imperatore electus IV. 1. 32. Simoniacos depositus VI. 4. 52.
units.tr: Victor II was elected by the Emperor (IV. 1. 32.). He deposed simonists (VI. 4. 52.).

units.la: Victor III. in Schismate VII. 1. 56. Anti-Papa Victor III, P. in Schismate VII. 1. 71. à Clero & populo IV. 1. 18. invitus electus dicitur VI. 1. 19.
units.tr: Victor III, during the schism (VII. 1. 56.). Victor III, anti-Pope and Pope, during the schism (VII. 1. 71.). Elected by clergy and people (IV. 1. 18.). He is said to have been elected against his will (VI. 1. 19.).

units.la: Vidonius Card. ab Hispanis exclusus VI. 2. 31.
units.tr: Cardinal Vidonius was excluded by the Spanish (VI. 2. 31.).

units.la: Vigilius P. in Schismate Simoniacè & malis artibus VII. 1. 10. 14. VI. 4. 70. summopere ambiens VI. 1. 11. invasit, pessimus VII. 1. 12. 7. 9. jam sub Bonifacio irrepere voluit 1. 12. Baronio fur & latro, Pseudo-Episcopus & Antichristus, hæreticus etiam, & tamen juxta eundem munus exercuit, Silverio superstite ib. quo vi sublato VI. 4. 57. non aliter electus
units.tr: Vigilius, Pope, during the schism, by simony and evil arts (VII. 1. 10. 14.; VI. 4. 70.). Eagerly ambitious (VI. 1. 11.). He seized the office; a most wicked man (VII. 1. 12.; 7. 9.). Already under Boniface he wished to creep in (1. 12.). In Baronius, a thief and a robber, a pseudo-bishop and Antichrist, also a heretic; and yet, according to the same author, he exercised the office while Silverius was still alive (ib.). With that violence removed (VI. 4. 57.), he was elected in no other way

units.la: fuit VII.1.15. 6. quod tamen à Baronio pessi- me factum fingitur 1b. non factus est Papa legitimus 7. nugæ Baronianæ de ejus mu- tatione refutantur 18. vi sublatus & ipse VI. 4.57.
units.tr: than (VII. 1. 15.; 6.). Yet this is pretended by Baronius to have been done most wickedly (ib.). He was not made a lawful Pope (7.). The Baronian trifles about his change are refuted (18.). He too was removed by force (VI. 4. 57.).

units.la: Vindicta studium in Concl. est principium agendi VI. 1. 39. 3. 6. 8. 13.
units.tr: Desire for revenge in the conclave is the principle of action (VI. 1. 39.; 3. 6. 8. 13.).

units.la: Virtus quatenus in electione Pontificum requiratur VII. 7. 1. quænam maxime virtu- tes requirantur 2. vel simulatio virtutis pro- batur 3. ostentatio commendatur VI. 3. 2. vir- tus sæpe impedimento est 4. 5. ejus defectus in Pontificibus electis 7 seqq.
units.tr: How far virtue is required in the election of Popes (VII. 7. 1.). Which virtues are chiefly required (2.). Or a pretence of virtue is proved (3.). Display is commended (VI. 3. 2.). Virtue is often an impediment (4. 5.). Its lack in Popes elected (7. seqq.).

units.la: Vis Prædecessoribus & aliàs illata electionis Pontificum medium VI. 4.57. seqq.
units.tr: Force, used against predecessors and otherwise, as a means of electing Popes (VI. 4. 57. seqq.).

units.la: Viscontio resistunt Hispani VI. 2. 32.
units.tr: The Spanish resist Visconti (VI. 2. 32.).

units.la: Vladislai Hungariæ Regis Epitaphium de perjuris Pontificum consiliis VII. 7. 51.
units.tr: The Epitaph of Vladislaus, King of Hungary, on the perjured counsels of the Popes (VII. 7. 51.).

units.la: Vitramontani excluduntur VII. 4. 5.
units.tr: The Ultramontanes are excluded (VII. 4. 5.).

units.la: Vrbanus P. indoctus de processione Spiri- tus S se explicare non novit VII. 8. 7.
units.tr: Pope Urban, unlearned, did not know how to explain the procession of the Holy Spirit (VII. 8. 7.).

units.la: Vrbanus P. Conrado Imp. inurbanus VIII. 1. 21.
units.tr: Pope Urban, uncourteous to Emperor Conrad (VIII. 1. 21.).

units.la: Vrbanus II. in Schismate VII. 1. 56. à Glo- ro & populo IV. 1. 8. electus, Turbanus, in Im- peratores injurius VII. 7. 29
units.tr: Urban II, during the schism (VII. 1. 56.). Elected by clergy and people (IV. 1. 8.). Turbanus, injurious to the Emperors (VII. 7. 29.).

units.la: Vrbanus IV. extrà Collegium Card. electus VI. 4. 65.
units.tr: Urban IV, elected from outside the College of Cardinals (VI. 4. 65.).

units.la: Vrbanus VI. extra Collegium VI. 4. 65. electus VII. 1. 82. 83. ejus dilata fuit electionis publicatio 84 Cardinales metuunt; (vi creatus dicitur VI. 4. 58.) gratulationem accipit 85. electus in suam electionem inquirit, Cardinalibus, etiam absentibus, eam confirmantibus 86 oratio post confirmationem, acceptatio & intronizatio 87. Cardinalium trium promotorum petitiones approbatæ 88 in omnibus se Pontificem exhibet 89 severe Cardinales admonet 90. VI. 4. 54. hinc initium inobedientiæ IV. 2. 44. cui se severe opponit VII. 1. 91. à pluribus deseritur, atque alius eligitur 91, nimium severus VII. 95. 97. inceptus, rusticus b paci inter Christianos componendæ non, ut par erat, intentus 1b. Nepotem Principem nosse volens multis malis occasionem dat 1b. ejus acta & mors 1b. superbus, injustus, avarus, sanguinem sitiens VII. 7. 44.
units.tr: Urban VI, elected from outside the College of Cardinals (VI. 4. 65.; VII. 1. 82. 83.). The publication of his election was delayed (84.). The Cardinals feared him (he is said to have been created by force, VI. 4. 58.). He receives congratulations (85.). Elected, he inquires into his own election; the Cardinals, even the absent ones, confirm it (86.). Speech after the confirmation, acceptance and enthronement (87.). The petitions of three promoting Cardinals are approved (88.). He shows himself Pope in everything (89.). He admonishes the Cardinals severely (90.; VI. 4. 54.). Hence the beginning of disobedience (IV. 2. 44.), against which he sets himself severely (VII. 1. 91.). He is deserted by many, and another is elected (91.). Too severe (VII. 95. 97.), begun, rustic, not, as was fitting, intent on making peace among Christians (ib.). Wishing to know his nephew as a prince, he gave occasion for many evils (ib.). His acts and death (ib.). Proud, unjust, greedy, thirsting for blood (VII. 7. 44.).

units.la: Vrbanus VII. 13. dierum Pontificatu; Nepotibus spe sua frustratis, legatis nonnisi quibusdam prodest VIII. 2. 18. eum in deterius pro more mutatum iri, timuit Paulus Sarpius 6. non coronatus valide tamen dispositus VIII. 1. 30.
units.tr: Urban VII, in his thirteen days as Pope; his nephews' hopes frustrated, he benefits only some of the legates (VIII. 2. 18.). Paul Sarpi feared that he would be changed for the worse, as is customary (6.). Not crowned, yet validly disposed (VIII. 1. 30.).

units.la: Vrbanus VIII. quali omine præsignificatus sit VII. 2 7. ambit, & ad electionem omnia disponit VI. 1. 26. mendacio se promovet, & consilio mendacii VI. 4.9.13. statim post electionem mentitur VIII. 2. 6 in deterius mutatus 1b. de vestium Pontificalium gravitate testatur 1. 5 stultus electus dicitur VII. 8 15. eruditionem suam jactat 8. ejus Nepotismus, absolute regnans, avarissimus, injustissimus, ditissimus VIII. 2. 22 Papa vectigal audit IV. 3. 7. ejus in Nepotibus duobus constituendis fraus VIII. 2. 34. Sanctus sine Nepotibus fuisset 1b infelix fuit in Cardinalium creationibus IV. 2. 87. Cardinales indigne tractavit 40 qualis fuerit VII. 7. 69. ejus vita adulatorie scripta 75. Divinationem de Pontificum vitæ spatio vetuit VIII. 2. 9.
units.tr: Urban VIII, by what omen he was foreshadowed (VII. 2. 7.). He courts, and arranges everything for the election (VI. 1. 26.). He promotes himself by lies, and by the counsel of lies (VI. 4. 9. 13.). Immediately after the election he lies (VIII. 2. 6.), changed for the worse (ib.). He testifies to the gravity of Pontifical vestments (1. 5.). He is said to have been elected a fool (VII. 8. 15.). He boasts of his learning (8.). His nepotism; reigning absolutely, most greedy, most unjust, very rich (VIII. 2. 22.). The Pope is called a tax (IV. 3. 7.). His fraud in appointing two nephews (VIII. 2. 34.). He would have been holy without nephews (ib.). He was unlucky in the creation of Cardinals (IV. 2. 87.). He treated Cardinals unworthily (40.). What sort he was (VII. 7. 69.). His life, written in a flattering way (75.). He forbade divination about the length of the Popes' lives (VIII. 2. 9.).

units.la: Vrsicinus P. in Schismate VII. 1. 5.
units.tr: Ursinus, Pope, during the schism (VII. 1. 5.).

units.la: Vrsinus in Concl. ambit. VI. 1. 22 personato Papa imponere vult 4. 15. Ursinorum insignia à Martino IV. sub lata VII. 7. 38.
units.tr: Ursinus, in the Conclave ambitus VI. 1. 22, wants the Pope to be impersonated; 4. 15. The insignia of the Ursini were raised by Martin IV, VII. 7. 38.

units.la: Cùm errare humanum sit, etiam in arte Typographica, & Author ab Urbe absens unicâ, eáque sæpe, in temporis, nocturni interdum, angustia, fugiente oculo facienda correctione non omnia sphalmata emendare potuerit, pro iis, quæ in exemplaris impressi relectione præcipua notavit, ita legi vult.
units.tr: Since it is human to err, even in the art of printing, and since the author, who was away from Rome, had only one chance to make corrections, often in a hurry and sometimes at night with failing eyes, he could not correct every slip. For the errors he marked as most important when rereading the printed copies, he wishes the following readings to be used.
